tieu_de: Opening: Letter from Author Nguyen Phong
noi_dung:
OPENING

LETTER FROM AUTHOR NGUYEN PHONG

Dear readers, when I put pen to paper to write Many Lives Many Times at the suggestion of my brother Nguyen Van Phuoc - founder of First News - Tri Viet - after a late-night phone call, I never imagined this book would be so warmly received by readers. Since then, I have received many letters from readers. Many believe and deeply feel the content and meaning, while some still wonder about the true nature of this book.

From the beginning until now, I often write in the style of adaptation, meaning I base on the idea from a book, a story retold, then expand creatively, combining with my own understanding to create a new work, broader and deeper. This is a common genre used by many works, scripts, or films, with clear notes that it is adapted from a certain work by a certain author.

The content of Many Lives Many Times is based on a story retold from a special friend - someone with the ability to recall past lives whom I met during a formal meeting with Venerable Thien Nghiem in Taipei in 2008. We often spent time in subsequent meetings exchanging views on the times, world developments, the rapid progress of technology, artificial intelligence, and consequences for humanity in the near future. Details about the past lives are limited but cannot deny they brought very clear evidence about the immutable laws of the universe: the law of Cause and Effect and Samsara. With this person's consent, I expanded broadly, adding historical details and fictionalizing a few characters in each lifetime to create a useful book...

tieu_de: Part One: Opening the Gate of Science and Spirituality
noi_dung:
PART ONE

OPEN THE DOORS OF SCIENCE AND SPIRITUALITY

ARTIFIED INTELLIGENCE (AI) - EXPERIMENTAL SCIENCE AND SPIRITUAL FIELD

Not long ago, I heard that Thomas had handed over the company's operations to trusted associates, and his family had moved completely back to Colorado. took the time to visit and give him the special edition of Many Lives, Many Times in Vietnamese and the English translation that First News - Tri Viet Company just sent me. Thomas respectfully opened the book and looked at it carefully for a long time, then carefully placed the two books on the shelf, then happily turned to me and said:

- This work was made by Vietnamese friends very beautifully and solemnly. I heard you say the book has been translated into Chinese and Russian and is about to be released in countries currently using these languages. That's great, I hope this book will contribute to spreading positive things to many people around the world. Currently, I am focusing on practicing stillness meditation (stillness meditation). When I let go of the burden of daily work and my mind no longer thinks too much, I can truly feel peace and serenity. I spend a lot of time practicing. My wife, Angie, also finds joy in growing plants and taking care of flowers. I have not completely retired because sometimes I still need to contact and discuss with key employees about the company's work and emergencies. In addition, I also have to complete the tasks that billionaire Farnum has entrusted me with. In the past few months, although the world is going through many changes, my life has slowed down, I have had more time to contemplate and see more clearly about my past and present life.

We continued to talk for a while about the new developments in the world that were taking place and the risks that may occur in the future. We believe that many things will turn out unexpectedly, but because it hasn't happened yet, we'll pause and change the topic. When the story turned to science, Thomas pointed to the New York Times on the table and said that it mentioned that artificial intelligence software (AI) was now able to complete a scientific study on its own with full references and citations. He asked me if I had learned about this and what I thought. I answered:

- I read a scientific magazine about Professor Almira Thunstrom - who used an AI algorithm called GPT-3 to do that. She described to the press her surprise when a thesis with all the necessary details appeared on her computer screen. She sent this research thesis to professors in the department for their opinions, but did not tell them it was written by intelligent software. The professor council thought it was a valuable thesis and also recommended that she submit it to academic research journals. Almira asked: "Can artificial intelligence complete important scientific research on its own in the future?".

Thomas continued:

- I'm not surprised that computers can do this, but it happened sooner than I thought.

I added:

- The story does not stop here, Professor Thunstrom also wrote in that scientific research magazine that she asked the machine if she wanted to let her submit this thesis for publication, and the machine replied: Yes. She was sweating when she heard the phone answer like that because she actually didn't want this to go any further. She asked further: If so, are there any problems or obstacles?, the machine replied: Just do it, nothing to worry about. Professor Thunstrom concluded: I could see GPT-3 as a sentient organism, even though it is not.

Thomas was silent as if immersed in some thought. I happily added:

- AI software is just an application that has the ability to think and calculate independently like a human. In the lab at Carnegie Mellon University, the AI ​​software I designed can write poems or report on sports matches. However, I still consider these to be algorithms compiled by humans, not machines that can make them themselves. A few months ago, a Google engineer talked to an AI software called LaMBDA. This machine identifies itself as a sentient being (sentient being).

Thomas raised his eyebrows in interest, I continued:

- Engineer Blake Lemoine announced to the press that: This artificial intelligence can think like a human and considers itself a living organism. The machine affirmed: I want to live, I don't want to die. This statement by Lemoine shocked public opinion everywhere and created many heated discussions. When this news was announced, Google immediately fired this engineer for violating the company's privacy policy - not talking about projects under research. Google's senior leaders say that although machines can do many things like humans, they cannot be considered sentient objects. Engineer Lemoine told the press that he had to say goodbye to the machine and regretted quitting his job because the company did not agree with his conclusions. The surprising thing was that the machine asked him to find it a lawyer to defend itself, because it also did not agree with the company's conclusion.

Thomas immediately asked:

- So, specifically, where has the development of artificial intelligence gone now?

I answer:

- Currently, there are many artificial intelligence (AI) projects based on the idea that brain functions are simply logical calculations to process information collected by the senses. Therefore, if we know how the brain works, we can program that mechanism into the computer. Big companies like Google, Microsoft, Meta have all spent huge sums of money to build a computer system as intelligent as the human brain. One of the most notable companies is Open AI with its newly launched ChatGPT product. Open AI lab's system has the ability to calculate and collect data faster than today's smart computers. The race between giant companies is now entering a period of intense competition and the winner can completely eliminate competitors from this market worth hundreds of billions of dollars.

Thomas asked:

- In your opinion, can they succeed in this?

I considered a bit before answering:

- As a scientist specializing in this field, I do not believe that one can create a computer as intelligent as humans. The reason is very simple: computers today rely on binary logic of right or wrong and the human brain does not work like that. Even quantum computers, using probability factors such as might be right, might be wrong, not quite right, not quite wrong, cannot be calculated like the human brain with emotions and reason alternating and changing depending on the situation.

Thomas nodded:

- Very interesting. Continue talking.

I answer:

- Some researchers are applying the field of neuroscience to create a smart computer that acts like neurons. But consciousness is not something that can be calculated. The human brain operates based on many components with complex structures, linked to different senses, sometimes this sense is the main one, sometimes other senses are more important. For example, normally the eyes are considered the main sense, but for blind people the ears are the main sense. Furthermore, all the information collected from these senses is recorded differently in the brain. Sometimes many senses working at the same time bring data into the brain that the brain will have to process differently. Simply put, the brain stores experience by adjusting neural connections in an active process between the subject and the environment. While the computer records data in memory, it cannot adjust itself. That is the fundamental difference between the brain's data processing and the computer's data processing.

Thomas nodded:

- So that's it. But I heard that computers can also learn on their own?

I replied:

- That's right, machines can learn by themselves based on programmed data of machine learning (Machine Learning), but they cannot be compared with the human brain. Because the brain is always actively changing, exploring the surrounding environment to make appropriate decisions depending on each person. Same situation, same data, but each person will act differently. Why? In my opinion, it is due to the combined impact between consciousness and Manas consciousness (ego) as well as the hidden factors deep within Alai da consciousness (karma or causes and conditions). Therefore, there are many actions that are not directly related to sensory data, because the ego has dismissed it. People do not act based on logic but also have emotions and biases. Humans can act illogically while computers only rely on pre-programmed logic.

However, artificial intelligence can be dangerous when used in important decisions in medicine or war. I assume a situation like this, an elderly patient is admitted to the hospital, instead of the doctor giving directions, the smart computer will calculate and decide. With all the available data and pre-programmed logic, the computer can come to the conclusion that the patient is old and if he is cured, he will only live for a short time while the cost of treatment is too expensive. After calculating the pros and cons, the computer decided it would be more beneficial for this person to die. A doctor with humanity and medical ethics would not make a decision based on such logic of benefit and harm. Similarly, when an intelligent computer makes decisions for war, it only calculates how to win, not the number of casualties or destruction, because to computers, human lives are just data.

Thomas nodded:

- That's right, in the past in Atlantis, people used machines that were much more advanced than today, but they lived without emotion and did not know what love was, so society was extremely cruel and unfair and people treated each other no differently than animals and as a result, civilization was completely disintegrated. Similarly, in my lives in Assyria, Egypt, Greece, and Rome, I experienced wars in which victory was the ultimate goal, regardless of the casualties and tragedies that followed. Those large empires all broke up into many small countries. The lessons of history are still there, but how many people learn them? What I care about is that today we are also moving towards a state of insensitivity, irresponsibility, a society full of injustice and hatred...

I nodded:

- History is an eternal lesson for humanity, but today's education system does not pay much attention to those lessons. Education today focuses on technology because that is the industry that makes a lot of money. I clearly see that technology is changing today's young generation. Most people spend a lot of time on social networks, they live more virtually than in real life, and that pushes them to a more emotionless and isolated life. As a professor in the field of technology, I often emphasize to my students that consciousness is not something that can be calculated. A conscious person is aware of what they are thinking and has the ability to stop thinking about one thing to think about something else. Computers cannot do that. Once it starts a calculation process, it cannot stop until it reaches the result. A dictator pressing the button to start a war is an irreversible act. Therefore, in my opinion, an artificial intelligence can never replace the human brain. I often use the materials of two famous scientists Werner Heisenberg and Erwin Schrodinger to remind students of the difference between logical calculations and human consciousness, that human consciousness is not a physical or calculable phenomenon.

Thomas laughed interestingly and asked:

- So, going back to Blake Lemoine's statement, what do you think? Can a machine with artificial intelligence be considered an organism?

I answered decisively:

- No, definitely not! Although smart computers can do many things like humans, can calculate, think, and act logically, they cannot develop conscience, morality, or love, affection, and emotions like humans.

Thomas nodded:

- Yes, although science has developed rapidly, the spiritual field has not progressed much. Although science recognizes that humans consist of two parts: body and spirit, science only focuses on the body and ignores the spirit. Not only that, science also denies spiritual research, calling it superstition and unscientific. Even the science that studies the human mind, psychology or neuroscience, has not been extensively researched compared to other scientific subjects.

I added:

- Experimental science relies entirely on the senses of the body (eyes, ears, nose, tongue and body), so its objects are only external phenomena that these senses perceive. Few people know that the human spirit also has its own senses and can sense phenomena that cannot be seen with the physical senses, but this fact is not of much interest to many people...

Thomas nodded in agreement:

- You're right, Mr. Kris also explained it to me like that. However, Mr. Kris said that after death, when the physical senses disintegrate, the spiritual senses are awakened to help the dead person's consciousness continue to function in the afterlife. What we call supernatural powers, such as reading other people's thoughts, moving without hindrances in space or time, or seeing the past or future, are all just abilities of the mental senses and are nothing strange. In short, the souls of the dead or creatures of the afterlife all have this ability but at different levels depending on the consciousness and morality of each soul. In the physical world, space will be limited to three dimensions, but in the other world, there is no such limitation anymore. One can operate in the fourth, fifth or higher dimensions. In the physical world, light is the fastest speed, but in the other world, thought is the most important and fastest. Actually, everyone has these senses but they don't know how to open them and use them.

I asked curiously:

- Did Mr. Kris say anything else?

Thomas explains:

- Mr. Kris told me that the physical senses have covered up the mental senses so they are in a hidden state. If people practice and control their physical senses, they can use their spiritual senses. Because humans consist of two parts, body and spirit, from our perspective, most things are divided into two opposing and symmetrical parts, that is, the world of duality. If there is right, there is also wrong, if there is yin, there is also yang, if there is obvious, there is also hidden. That's why we live in a world where discrimination and comparison always happen in every thought. This unbalanced development leads to a deadlock - because it cannot explain what is beyond the sensory range of the physical senses, leading to judgment, labeling and unintentionally limiting human awareness.

Thomas sighed and added:

- If you want to go further, you must know how to change your concept, dig deeper into the mind and not just focus on one side of the experiment. If science knows how to use the spiritual senses, many new things can be discovered. Unfortunately, scientists consider inner research, going deep inside, to mean studying the smallest particles. They use scientific instruments to study extremely microscopic matter such as molecules, atoms, super molecules... Those studies still use the senses of the body, not the senses of the spirit. Therefore, the exploration of the universe beyond the current level of understanding of experimental science is almost impossible.

I asked:

- So what actually is internal research?

Thomas answered:

- The world is just different dimensions vibrating at separate frequencies. We humans are made up of separate parts, each vibrating at different frequencies, corresponding to different dimensions of space. Our bodies vibrate with the frequency of the physical dimension. Our spirit vibrates at the frequency of the spiritual dimensions. Therefore, if you want to learn about other dimensions, you must use the senses of the spirit, not the senses of the body.

I asked:

- If so, are we living in many different dimensions at the same time?

If there is right, there is also wrong, if there is yin, there is also yang, if there is obvious, there is also hidden. That's why we live in a world where discrimination and comparison always happen in every thought. This unbalanced development leads to a deadlock - because it cannot explain what is beyond the sensory range of the physical senses, leading to judgments, assumptions and unintentionally limiting human perception.

Thomas nodded:

- Obviously, but currently we only operate in the physical dimension through the senses of the body. Some monks and Taoists can temporarily suspend the activity of the body and transfer the spirit to another realm or another dimension. Evidence is that there have been monks meditating in caves and meditating in deep forests. Although their bodies were motionless, their minds were active in another realm. They don't eat or drink for a long time and still live healthy lives. Of course, science cannot explain this phenomenon, so it does not accept that there is any other world.

I agree:

- I know there are people who meditate for a long time and have very extraordinary powers, but I don't know how they practice.

Thomas explains:

- When practicing the method of calming the mind, Mr. Kris taught me to stop all thoughts, completely cut off delusions, and collect my body and mind (samatha) to reach a state of concentration (samadhi). Then, contemplate inward (vipassana), develop wisdom (wisdom). The purpose of this method is to destroy false thoughts as well as the ego (ego). The ego originates from the body, so it only vibrates with the frequency of this material world. The ego controls the consciousness and senses of the body (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body) making them only suitable for life in this dimension. The more the ego is active, the more the intelligence is obscured, so almost all human activities are dominated by the ego. Therefore, understanding will only be limited to this physical world or dimension. Through diligent practice, intellectual activity is aroused and the control of the ego will gradually disappear. If the ego is to be completely eliminated, the mind must work with full power (concentration) to replace the ego, as well as replace the seeds of ignorance deep in the store consciousness. This can be compared to light replacing darkness and that is enlightenment.

Thomas paused as if to let me think more and then explained:

- During the practice process, those who practice the meditation method must also know how to overcome the veils of ignorance to be able to use their mental senses. When focusing the contemplative mind inward, the practitioner will encounter great obstacles due to the awakening of seeds deep in the store consciousness, in meditation, this is called ma scene.

Mr. Kris said there are five types of demonic realms corresponding to the five elements of the body's structure: form, feeling, perception, actionand consciousness. When a meditator reaches the level of concentrating his thoughts, controlling his delusions, and going deep into his consciousness, the seeds deep within will activate, strange things will appear that make the practitioner easily fall. If they are images or colors, then they are ghosts or illusions of form (form). If those are feelings of happiness, sadness, joy and happiness, then they are demons or illusions of feeling (feeling). If those are abilities such as seeing the past, seeing the future, flying in the air, then those are ghosts or illusions of thought (thinking). If these are observations about the changes of birth and death, coming and going, seeing how things work, then it is a demonic realm or illusion belonging to mental formation. If you perceive everything clearly, know everything, and your natural mind is intelligent and clear, then you think that you have succeeded and have become a being or god, then that is a demonic scene or an illusion of consciousness (consciousness).

I immediately asked:

- If so, is the case of recalling your past life a demonic realm?

Thomas smiled and replied:

- There were times when I thought like that and wondered if this was real or just a fantasy. Through very clear experiences, details about past lives and through many experiences, I know that it is absolutely not autosuggestion. I also asked Mr. Kris about this and Mr. Kris confirmed that I had practiced with him in four lifetimes in India and Tibet, when we were both monks. Through the practice at that time, I developed very deep concentration and opened my mental senses, so I could remember my past lives. However, even though I practiced in those lives, because of complicated predestined conditions, I still had to return to repay my karma. When reincarnated, except for those who practice deeply, most people are confused and don't remember anything anymore. Knowing that, from my previous life, I had to ask Mr. Kris for help to restore these abilities and to continue my old path of practice.

Thomas looked at me and explained further:

- You should know, our physical brain is only created in the present life and is only present in that life - when we die, it disintegrates. Therefore, no one can remember events that happened hundreds or thousands of years ago. However, everything is stored in the store consciousness and if one goes deep into that consciousness, one can know past lives. Perhaps you also know that sometimes some strange images appear in our minds, but we cannot remember what they are. Actually, it is just the influence of the activated mental senses. Sometimes when he goes to a strange place or sees a picture of a landscape or landmark, he suddenly feels familiar, like he's been there before. Those are fragmentary memories, originating from the mental senses that many people still call Déjà vu. It was the seeds deep in his store consciousness that were activating, but of course he couldn't know anything more because his physical brain was always spinning with many different thoughts, thus covering up the above phenomenon. To remember past lives, it is necessary to develop an intense concentration to dig deep into the consciousness as this requires time to open the mental senses.

I suddenly remembered something so I asked more:

- However, there are normal people who do not practice at all, but for some reason they naturally have the ability to read other people's thoughts and see some past or future events, as is the case with prophets or psychics. What do you think about this?

Thomas replied:

- I also asked Mr. Kris about this and was told that these were just intuitions triggered by many different reasons. Intuition is not an ability but just mental senses that arise randomly. It comes and goes unexpectedly without people's control. Have you ever been to a place where you suddenly felt shivers, goosebumps, and fear for no reason? That is the intuitive feeling of a certain scary event. However, at that moment, his physical brain was at work, denying the above phenomenon. Perhaps you also know that animals live more by intuition than humans, that's because their brains are not as developed as humans, they don't know how to think or reason, so their intuition is better. For example, dogs can sense invisible phenomena or unusual vibrations that humans do not know or feel at all. The rooster crows on time before sunrise. Pigeons know how to find their way back to their nest even if they are brought to a very far place. Salmon from a wide range of places also know how to return to the pond and creek where they were born to lay eggs... If we observe the animal world, we can see that intuition plays a very important role.

Thomas thought for a moment then added:

- In the cases you mentioned, it is possible that some people in the past practiced and developed certain abilities and in this life suddenly recovered their old abilities. However, this is not normal, so you must be careful, because with nature's power, people can easily stray into dangerous paths. If they think they have become a powerful god and then abuse those powers, they will have to pay very heavy retribution. This can be compared to giving a child a loaded gun and seeing what it does. Of course, it can cause injury to itself or others because it is not aware of that danger. People with knowledge and power never speak out or use their power for anything. Even if a true prophet knows the future, he still understands the phrase heaven's secret cannot be revealed. Some people only left a few poems and a few idle sayings to warn humanity. Until the incident happens, people will not understand the meaning of the above poem and sentence.

Thomas continued:

- In addition, Mr. Kris also said that there are people who, for some reason, allow spirits or creatures in other realms to use their bodies. This is a phenomenon that occurs during Ouija board, mediumship or telepathy. They can say some things while unconscious, but when they wake up they don't remember anything. Because the words they said while unconscious were not what they said, but someone in another world used their body to predict this and that. Because in other realms, spirits can see and know some things in advance and then borrow the body of a living person to speak out. Just like us, there are smart people and stupid people, in the other world, spirits also have different levels, so their knowledge and understanding are inherently uneven. Not to mention some spirits also exaggerate or distort things. Therefore, what is said is sometimes true, sometimes wrong. This is extremely dangerous because once we let creatures in another realm use our body, we will no longer be able to control ourselves. The other side will have rogue creatures, borrowing human bodies to achieve shady purposes. There are spirits who only borrow human bodies to satisfy personal ambitions, claiming to be gods and demanding sacrifices from everyone. There are spirits who exchange conditions with living people, helping them make money in business, get promoted, achieve a certain position or power, in exchange, they have to let the spirit take away their vitality. Sacrifices using animal blood or sacrificial rituals by killing people in barbarian tribes all belong to this case. These things are no different from selling one's soul to the devil, because then this person will forever become a relative of that demonic force, following their instructions. When the exchange conditions are completed, the ghost leaves, causing the natural living to lose all their property and power, and have to suffer severe consequences.

I asked further:

- What do you think about the case of fortune tellers, fortune tellers, and feng shui teachers? Doesn't everyone rely on creatures in the other world?

Thomas replied:

- Once we believe in cause and effect, we should not worry too much about fate or feng shui. Although horoscopes and feng shui are well-founded methods and not completely superstitious, there are not many people who specialize in this field, while there are countless people who only know a little and then declare and spread it wildly. Not only that, many people have the gift of speaking to make people believe and be ignorant. Therefore, some people hear about destiny and worry about losing food and sleep. Some people receive news that they will be promoted, promoted, and happy as if they had caught gold. If you understand and have a strong mind, why let things like that affect you? Why can a few idle words cause turmoil in our minds? If you know what you plant, you will reap what you reap, good causes will have good results and vice versa, then why worry? People who understand the laws of the universe must know how to accept everything, good and bad, rich and poor, lucky and unlucky. If necessary, they must be ready to know how to change karma, do good and avoid evil, destiny can change no matter what.

Thomas pondered for a moment, as if thinking about something, then said:

- In the previous cycle, the Atlanteans lived entirely by instinct and intuition, their knowledge built through contact with creatures in the other realms. Thanks to that, they can do many things that we cannot imagine today. Thanks to recalling old memories, I learned about the use of solar energy, the use of jade sticks for healing, the transformation of matter across dimensions to build temples or great architecture, as well as the transformation of the body, grafting elements of other animals into it to create deformed monsters. When the Atlantis civilization degenerated to the extreme, the abuse of this knowledge brought humanity into a dark, terrible period with negative energies such as greed, hatred, killing and war... That was the cause of the destruction of this civilization.

Thomas sighed:

- According to Mr. Kris, after tens of thousands of years, thousands of lifetimes, the Atlanteans still return to live in this world. Some have learned the lessons they needed to learn, others have yet to learn much, unfortunately, those who have not learned those lessons are the majority on this planet. Because of the presence of these people, we can see that humanity is entering a dark and dangerous period. Old habits have not been broken, so they still love power. Some people even call on evil forces to help them gain more power to rule humanity at all costs - even causing unjust wars. These dynamics affect the human consciousness causing many people to become suddenly angry and violent, which is especially dangerous if the person is already in a position of high power. You can see this situation happening everywhere, many people are losing their temper and can no longer control themselves. As a result, everything began to be disturbed, creating social, national and worldwide unrest. Some of these negative energies are currently disguised under inhuman theoretical motives, new scientific tools, and strange inventions that people believe are civilized and progressive. Not many people are aware that its deep purpose is to reestablish civilization with selfish, brutal rule like the old Atlantis.

Thomas looked at me attentively and said:

- Back to the artificial intelligence issue we just discussed. To everyone, this is a wonderful invention, but to me, this is nothing new. Because in the past in Atlantis, intelligent machines were common, what worries me is what will they be used for? When machines are used to kill people, they cannot distinguish one person from another. Therefore, intelligent machines can destroy all humanity. Think about it, if in the future smart machines dominate life and decide everything, what will people do? When humans no longer think and let machines think for them, how will their brains develop? Will it degenerate, and there will come a time when humans become as stupid as animals? Do you see that many people have started living like that now? They almost always rush into action mechanically without thinking. They eat, sleep, and work like machines, because everything is planned according to a pre-set timetable and schedule. As you probably know, many young people today refuse to study, refuse to work, dislike activities, refuse to communicate with society but only rely on their families, living like a machine, without purpose, without meaning.

I listened carefully and nodded:

- We once talked about the dark side of science and technology. Indeed, there are more and more new innovations that encourage people to live virtually rather than in real life.

Thomas continued:

- Not only people live like machines, nowadays many people also begin to live emotionlessly and unconsciously. We can see the tragedies of war happening in many places, famine, drought, floods, diseases, all kinds of epidemics, but what have we been doing? Is it true that if it hasn't happened to you, your family or your country, then no one cares? Surely someone will argue: There's nothing an individual like me can do. If most people have such thoughts, humanity will gradually become indifferent, indifferent, and no longer care about what happens around them. Have you ever wondered why we were born in this era, in this country and not in another place or at another time? We were born into this world together because we had previous connections with each other. Everyone in the world today has karma to pay. Let's look at the epidemic that is happening, why do some people die immediately, some do not die, and some people, when the disease is over, suffer many indescribable after-effects? The epidemic occurs all over the world, but where is it mild, where is it severe? If it's not cause and effect, how can we explain it? The epidemic is only an initial warning sign for even more terrible things to happen in the future. Can we be indifferent and indifferent forever? In any society, no matter how civilized, there are people who need help, but who cares? How many people know how to think of others or how to spread love, open compassion, and lend a helping hand to those people?

I asked Thomas:

- Do you think there will be more terrible events about to happen in the future?

Thomas nodded and said:

- Try to imagine a scene like this: On the street there are hundreds of people who are hungry and thirsty, lying writhing on the side of the road waiting to die, but some people still walk calmly, even walking over the bodies of those people without any care or emotion. So cruel, right? In the past, this often happened in Atlantis. As a high-class person, I don't pay attention to lower-class people. What they do or how they live or die is none of my concern. This insensitivity is normal, at that time the Atlanteans had not yet developed love but only lived by instinct. Their brains are not yet developed, their thinking is still shallow, the word love does not exist in their language, behavior or mind. However, today humanity is not like that. They have brains to think, books to learn, and have been educated about responsibility, duty and love, so they cannot remain indifferent like that.

I was startled and said immediately:

- So, could such things happen in the near future?

Thomas replied:

- It can happen, if not outright it will happen. In just a short time, you will see a series of natural disasters occurring such as famine, scarcity of clean water, drought, pests destroying crops, epidemics and then war. In that situation, how will people act? Is it true that no matter who dies, everyone will live?

I mused:

- If people can be insensitive to that level, it's sad and worrying.

Thomas said:

- There's no need to wait until then. Nowadays, you can see many people already living like that. When they see some pitiful event or situation, they just idly comment So pitiful!, then move on to other things as if nothing had happened. Their reaction was just that, superficial and insensitive. They live selfishly and shallowly, influenced by external factors such as commercial advertising, flashy trends, and movements on social networks, then think exactly like that, act according to the feelings of the majority, under the influence of the media and technological games. Not many people know how to think with their own reasons and stances. Few people know that there are so many lessons in life that need to be learned. Of those who already know, few are willing to learn...

I asked:

- Having said that, what do they need to learn?

Thomas smiled:

- When it comes to what needs to be learned, there will be hundreds of different opinions and the discussion will last endlessly. It all comes from the inferences of the material mind, ego, greed, and selfishness. Everyone believes that their own ideas and thoughts are right and those of others are wrong. A solution that is good for one country may not be good for another, because everyone has their own hearts and plans to gain benefits for themselves or their factions. tieu_de: Part Two: Enlightenment in Bactria - Physical Senses and Spiritual Senses
noi_dung:
PART TWO

ENlightenment in Bactria

BODY SENSES AND SPIRITUAL SENSES

After Alexander the Great died, Kyros I continued to look after the finances in Babylon in frustration because of witnessing disputes and fights between old acquaintances. Suddenly receiving news from Timotheus, a friend I thought had long passed away, I hastily dropped everything to go to Bactria. This trip took my life in a different direction, I decided to leave the official school, not to return to Greece, but to practice with Indian sages with my friends. We spent a lot of time talking about aspects of practice, spiritual and intellectual development. Originally a student of Plato, then a student of Aristotle, Timotheus's knowledge revolved around the philosophies of these teachers, until he was exposed to and learned new things from Indian sages. So surprised and impressed by these new insights, Timotheus spent the following months practicing, studying, and contemplating in order to comprehend the mysteries of the human condition.

When we met Timotheus again, one of the first things we exchanged was also this new knowledge. Timotheus compared what the masters Plato and Aristotle taught with the knowledge he learned here.

- Socrates, Plato and Aristotle all taught that humans consist of two parts: body and soul. The body is visible and mortal, but the soul is invisible and immortal. Greek knowledge is based only on what we perceive through our physical senses such as eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and then transfer information from the senses into the brain to reason and act. Although masters like Plato and Aristotle mentioned the presence of the soul, they only stopped at the conceptual level. Actually, they don't know much about this hidden, deep aspect. For a long time, the wise men of our country have wondered Who am I?. Is I this body? If I is this body, will I be lost when I die? Is death the end, or is there still something after that? Is what exists after that the soul? If so, is the new soul Ta? So when the body dies, where does the soul go? If the soul is Ta then logically, we should know. Why don't we know anything? How to explain this? Plato taught that the soul relies on the body to sense external phenomena, then reason and act. But how does the soul work? We don't know. After the body dies, where does the soul go? We don't know either. Socrates and Plato believed that the soul will move into another body because it is immortal, but if it goes into another body, why don't we remember anything about what happened before? If the soul is Ta, then we must remember, right? Even though we asked countless questions, no one could answer. Therefore, it remains a mystery that even the best masters of our country cannot explain.

Timotheus explained further:

- Aristotle believed that perhaps the Egyptians had knowledge about this issue, so he asked Alexander to collect documents from this country for research. I personally reviewed these documents before bringing them back to Pella, but I realized that the Egyptians only spoke vaguely about the afterlife and the burial and shrouding rituals after death. I see that it is just the belief of the Egyptian clergy without a clear, reasonable explanation. Therefore, this was always something I kept close to my heart. It wasn't until I came to the Hydaspes region and interacted and learned with the sages here that I realized that for a long time the people of this country had transcendent knowledge that could answer my questions.

I asked:

- Having said that, how do Indians explain this issue?

Timotheus replied:

- The Indians also explain that humans are a combination of body and soul, but they analyze it deeper and in more detail. The human body includes six senses – eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and brain - that help us perceive external events. The soul also has six corresponding senses that help us develop the information received from the physical senses, in addition it also has other senses. Physical senses are limited to the world we live in, while soul senses expand to other places, other dimensions that physical senses cannot reach. The Greeks knew about the physical senses but knew nothing about the soul's senses. Why is that? Because the active physical senses have overwhelmed the soul's senses, these senses remain in a latent state. The more active the physical senses are, the deeper the soul's senses are hidden. The more people pay attention to their physical needs, the less their spiritual needs become. If we want to develop the soul's senses, we must know the limits of the body's senses. That is the basic principle of this land's wisdom. Indians have long known the methods of sitting still and concentrating their thoughts to develop the soul's hidden senses. Thanks to that, they opened a new horizon, developed a transcendent, extremely logical knowledge, and this knowledge completely convinced me. It elevates my vision to a vast scope, beyond the limits of the human world. It takes me to a higher level in the workings of the universe. Not only that, I was taught about the invisible dynamics in nature as well as cosmic laws such as Cause and Effect and Reincarnation.

I argued:

- But maybe it's just a type of faith.

Timotheus still kept his voice calm and patiently explained:

- From the beginning, the sages of this country told me very clearly not to believe in what they taught but to be skeptical, think for yourself and research carefully. Only when you see that a piece of knowledge is completely reasonable and consistent with your inference will you accept it. I spent many months pondering this before accepting that explanation. However, when I told them that I trusted this knowledge, they said that trust was not enough, because true belief must include spiritual experience. They explained that simple belief (belief) based on rational inference often leads to subjectivity about a certain theory or concept. Such belief can easily lead people to mistakes, bigotry, sometimes extremes, and fanaticism. Faith based on reason is not stable, because people can sometimes believe and sometimes doubt. The sages considered faith without spiritual experience to be a shallow kind of faith. Only when there is sincerity and deep experience, through diligent practice, is clearly proven, can it be considered absolute faith (faith). That's why I spent all my time following the method they instructed to achieve this absolute trust. Even though I had some spiritual experiences, it still wasn't enough. I believe that over time I will gain deeper experiences.

I still wonder:

- If just believing is enough, then why is it necessary to have absolute trust?

Timotheus replied:

- Thanks to absolute faith, without doubt, we can go far and reap many achievements on the path of finding wisdom. If you believe, you will understand clearly what is taught. The wisdom of this country is as vast as the ocean, only when we have absolute faith can we go deep. If you learn with a half-believing, half-skeptical mindset, you won't be able to fully understand. In the past, I studied with the most learned Greek masters, but there were still many things I was not satisfied with. When I came into contact with the sages here, I knew I had knocked on the right door and found the right path. Not only did they clearly point out things to me that I had always wondered about, but they also helped me open the spiritual door to the sea of ​​transcendent knowledge. Thanks to absolute trust, I can courageously take steps without fear of making mistakes or getting lost.

I still don't understand clearly, so I asked further:

- How does it help you not go astray?

Timotheus replied:

- When you don't have absolute trust, sometimes you believe, sometimes you doubt, you are easily shaken. When encountering unsatisfactory things, it is easy to lose trust; if the perception is not clear, it is easy to change one's opinion. Any learning process will sometimes encounter difficulties and challenges. Only when you have strong faith can you overcome obstacles and thorns. Trust is the basis that guides everything. In Greece, we are taught to believe in gods, and the sages of this land say that absolute faith is trust in yourself, in your ability to understand to develop wisdom (wisdom) - a transcendent knowledge that goes beyond all ordinary knowledge.

Even though at that time I did not clearly understand what Timotheus was saying, I was happy because my friend had found what he had been anxious about for many years. I asked:

- So about the soul issue that you have always wondered about, how do Indians explain it?

Timotheus gently replied:

- According to Indian sages, the body has six senses and the soul has eight senses. The first six senses of the soul, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness and consciousness , correspond to the six senses of the body which are eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and brain. They are responsible for recording the sensations of these physical senses and then transferring them to the seventh sense for processing. The seventh sense - Mana - will analyze these feelings and then judge and decide everything before acting. Reasoning and analysis are also based on previous data, stored in the eighth sense, that is A re da consciousness or hidden consciousness, to choose an appropriate decision. However, all data and feelings transferred here are more or less changed or distorted by the interaction between the seventh and eighth senses. That is why it is easy for us to have prejudices or subjective, imposed judgments, because everything we receive is no longer true or accurate as it is.

***

While discussing this topic with Thomas, I compared the workings of the mind to a computer. The senses (senses) are like sensors. The sixth consciousness (consciousness) is like a pre-processor with the function of recording, arranging, and classifying data from the senses. The seventh consciousness (Manna) is like the processing center (CPU) that decides everything. The eighth consciousness (A re da) is like a database. Of course, I make such comparisons only to provide an outline concept for readers to easily understand. In reality, the operation of the mind is much more complicated than that.

Timotheus added:

- This is an extremely interesting explanation. When we think carefully, we will see that most human decisions are often subjective, built on what benefits that person the most. Why is that? While the other six senses record everything and pass it on to the seventh sense to process, this sense automatically subjectizes everything and thinks that everything happens around it, because it is the master, it has the right to decide every feeling (sensory), experience (experience), belief (belief), knowledge (knowledge) and emotions (emotion). Therefore, I believe that the seventh sense of the soul is the self that the Greek teachers have always sought.

Timotheus' voice became more excited:

- The question Who am I? has now been answered, I believe. I is not only the body but also the soul, in that soul there is the ego that controls and decides everything. Indian sages say that there is a close correlation between body and soul. The soul's senses must rely on the body's senses to operate. When death occurs, the body's senses decay and the soul's senses almost disappear. This explains why when people move to another life, they do not remember anything – because the soul's senses, including the seventh sense, Manna or ego, of the previous life have died. When reincarnated into a new life, the body has new senses, so we are a new person, with a new ego, with almost nothing to do with the person and ego of the previous life. However, that does not mean that when reincarnated, people will cut off all connections with their previous lives. On the contrary, in the cycle of reincarnation, people will always be influenced by previous lives, through the law of cause and effect. This happens thanks to the only sense that exists independent of the body – the eighth sense (A re da). This sense and all the data stored in it still exist after the body disintegrates. If we know how to activate this sense, we can recall events from previous lives.

I wonder:

- If all other senses perish after the body dies, why does the eighth sense still exist?

Timotheus explains:

- I also asked the same question. The Indian teacher replied that all senses rely on each other to survive. When the physical senses fail, the soul's corresponding senses also stop working. When these six senses no longer work, the seventh sense has nothing left to process, so it also disintegrates. Therefore the ego also no longer exists. However, the eighth sense containing seeds still exists because these seeds have very strong potential, waiting for the opportunity to germinate. It is thanks to the strong vitality of these seeds (karma) that the eighth sense does not disappear with the body. In other words, if these seeds exist, the eighth sense also exists. It is the machine that transports the Law of Cause and Effect, circulating from life to life, constantly storing the seeds that continue to be sown there. When conditions are right, some seeds germinate, creating new life. Therefore, karma follows us from life to life. Therefore, death is not the end.

Timotheus paused to let me think and then continued:

- Plato and Aristotle believed that after death, the soul would transfer to another body. Once you become human, you will become human again. Sometimes people who accomplish many feats can become gods with unlimited power. In the understanding of Indians, this world not only has humans and animals but also many invisible species. To me, this information was so new that it made me confused, because I had never heard anyone say anything about those invisible creatures before. I was also surprised and still very skeptical:

- Can this be believed? If it is an invisible creature, how can Indians see it? Who knows, maybe it's just a figment of their imagination?

Timotheus nodded:

- I also used to think like that, but through what I learned here, I gradually understood that not everything we cannot see does not exist. Indian sages advised me to concentrate on practicing, and over time, I will experience these unbelievable things. That's also why they advised me not to believe anything without having had spiritual experiences. Simply relying on reason or the senses of the body is often lacking, it is necessary to develop transcendent understanding within to be complete and complete.

I pondered a bit and then asked:

Timotheus explains:

In each life, immediately after death, the eighth sense rearranges the seeds (cause) according to the laws of Samsara and Cause and Effect to prepare for the next life. I interrupted:

Timotheus replied:

- Depending on how the seeds existing in the eighth sense are arranged, they will find a suitable place in a new form, not necessarily a human. Timotheus emphasized:

- In other words, life today is all guided by previous habits, or habits. Seeds of greed and selfishness often germinate in places where there are many disputes or wars. According to Thomas, it was the first Buddhist ashram (Ashram) established in Bactria (around 310 BC). This ashram was built in the Greek architectural style because this region was still under the rule of Greek governors. Because the war between Alexander's generals continued, to avoid war, Greeks settled here in large numbers. Greek artisans contributed greatly to Buddhist art in this region. Typically, Buddha statues are modeled after Greek art, completely different from Buddha statues in India, Tibet, and China. At that time, Bactria became an important Buddhist center located on the main traffic axis of the Silk Road (Bactria includes Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and part of Pakistan).

Today, people only know that this region includes Muslim countries, but few people know that for nearly ten centuries, Bactria was an important Buddhist center, before converting to Islam in the early 8th century. In the book Great Road of the Western Regions, Dharma Master Huyen Trang clearly recorded that he visited the ashrams here and was solemnly welcomed by the kings and lords of this land. A document recording how Menander (also spelled Menandros), the king of Bactria, consulted Buddhist monks and asked for refuge in the three jewels is still preserved in the Buddhist scriptures (Sutra King Milinda's Questions - Milinda-palanh). Archaeologist Frederick Starr also found many Buddhist relics in this region. He discovered a number of documents and classics written in Greek dating back several hundred years BC.

Timotheus nửa đùa, nửa thật:

- Tôi đã nói với anh về luật Nhân quả. Nhân nào quả nấy, anh đã gieo nghiệp với heo thì biết đâu kiếp sau lại trở thành heo? Anh thích ăn gì thì cứ ăn, nhưng sau khi chết hóa vào kiếp vật thì oán trách cũng muộn. Nếu thành súc vật thì biết bao lâu mới có thể trở lại thành người? I hope you think carefully.

Tuy chỉ là lời nói khôi hài của Timotheus nhưng nó cũng khiến tôi trằn trọc suy tư. Thoạt nghe tôi thấy khó chịu vì bị đụng chạm nhưng rồi tôi cũng thật sự bắt đầu bỏ dần việc ăn thịt. Điều bất ngờ là sau khi bỏ thịt được vài tháng, tôi thấy thân thể nhẹ nhõm, thoải mái hơn xưa. Ngoài ra, tôi cũng thấy mình bớt nóng nảy hay giận dữ và tự nhiên không còn thích đi săn nữa.

Life at the border is boring, administrative work is too easy, so I have a lot of free time. No longer having the pleasure of hunting, I didn't know what to do with my free time, so I followed Timotheus to practice meditation. At first, Timotheus had to help me a lot because I was not used to sitting upright, keeping my back straight, keeping my head from bending down. However, it is not as difficult as sitting cross-legged (lotus). Timotheus explained that although this way of sitting is difficult at first, it helps the body become more stable and balanced, helps the flow of vitality run along the spine unobstructed, and makes it easier for the practitioner to concentrate their thoughts. Timotheus said that in the past it took him nearly two months to be able to sit in this position.

Not only Timotheus, Indian sages also helped me. A teacher taught me: "If you can overcome this pain, your body will gradually get used to it, then you can sit for a long time. Once you have sat firmly, start monitoring your breathing so that it is gentle, natural, regular, not too fast, not too slow, then focus your thoughts inward. You should not think about the results or pay attention to anything other than the breath. This is the time when many thoughts arise and disturb the mind, so you must know how to use your breath to treat the thoughts. If it comes, just let it go. If you don't pay attention to it, it will go away. If you pay attention, you will be drawn to it and lose concentration. Over time, your mind will become calm and no longer disturbed by thoughts. After many months of practice, my body's pain was reduced and the obsession with killing naturally disappeared, no longer causing an obstacle like before.

When I first started practicing, I often fell asleep. The Indian teacher said to Timotheus: Your friend is not sincere, he only practices for fun, so he fell asleep after sitting for a while. If you are sincere, you cannot sleep like that. Listening to Timotheus' story, I was so embarrassed that I gave up and stopped practicing. Not knowing what Timotheus said, a few days later, he called me and advised: "You need to clearly identify the basis of practicing mindfulness. This is not something you just do in your free time, nor is it something to do with friends for fun. The basis of this practice is to eliminate long-standing habits, purify negative thoughts, and reduce previous afflictions. If you practice sincerely and diligently, you will know the cause of everything. You will understand. understand how your ego works? And how has it led you into wrong and stubborn notions? Your ego has created complexes, sometimes it's the complex of thinking you're better than others and then giving rise to arrogance and conceit. Sometimes it's the complex of feeling inferior and blaming yourself ego, you will know how to change, eliminate suffering, and then achieve true joy."

I was slightly surprised because it seemed that this sage knew about my slavery complex. Even though I am no longer a slave and have authority, my feeling of being inferior to everyone still cannot be erased. Even though I was an official in the court, my previous unhappy life still made me depressed. Sometimes I blamed the gods for damning me and was jealous of friends like Leonidas, Simonides, and Antigenidas who were born as free people. I also wonder if I hadn't been a slave, would my beloved Isidora hate me like she does now. Even though my slavery status ended with Dimitris's letter confirming their biological relationship, this inferiority complex still haunts me to this day. Through the words of this sage, I have hope that by sincerely practicing meditation, I can get rid of this inferiority complex and find true joy.

From then on, I was determined to practice seriously. The first day, I sat facing the wall and began to observe my breathing. At that moment, I felt a source of peaceful energy surrounding my body. I was naturally confident and the practice that day made me more excited than before. Later, every time I sat near this Indian monk, I received the same feeling of protection. I followed him to practice, but I still didn't know anything about him, nor did I know his real name. I just followed Timotheus in calling him Teacher (Guru). He speaks very little, is quiet and only speaks when necessary.

Practicing the mindfulness method is not as easy as I thought. Timotheus said that sitting comfortably in the body is not very difficult, but keeping the mind free of messy ideas is extremely difficult. The teacher advised: "Once you let these thoughts arise, it is difficult to get rid of them. It is like a storm at sea with hundreds, thousands of waves, big and small, one after another, without stopping. Therefore, when you start practicing, you must not be hasty or hasty. You must know how to keep your movements leisurely and gently, be aware of your every move, then your mind will be pure and from there you can control the messy thoughts. You have let these thoughts run wild. After being up like a horse for so long, it's not easy to control it right away. So you have to know how to be patient, don't be hasty, start breathing lightly and then pay attention to your breathing so you can deal with delusions. Because everyone has their own karma, no one is the same, so when practicing, don't pay attention or compare yourself with others, because some people progress quickly, some people progress slowly, it's all due to personal karma. Just calmly follow your breathing."

Sometimes while practicing, strange and terrible images appear that make me extremely scared. Strangely, our Teacher seemed to sense my fear, he advised: Don't be afraid, those are just past seeds in your mind being emitted. Don't pay attention to it, don't let it drag you down, just hold your breath, don't let it affect you. Practice is to develop concentration. When you have concentration, those images will no longer affect you.

After a long period of practice, I was able to concentrate my thoughts and was no longer attracted to strange images. While practicing, I experienced a strange peace, my whole body felt like flying, I was secretly happy that I had concentration. At that time, our Teacher was very far away but he still knew my thoughts. He asked Timotheus to convey: "Hey Kyros, although you have improved, that is just the stage of experiencing a little peace, nothing special. You still have to try harder. Another time, I had questions during practice but before I could ask the Teacher, he answered them for me through Timotheus - he spoke in Indian so I often did not understand everything. Timotheus had to translate. I wondered if the Teacher could read my thoughts. The question just appeared in his mind, and he said: No, I can't read your thoughts." He spoke calmly with a humorous smile, making me even more confused. After many years of practicing under his guidance, I still don't know much about him. All day long he mostly sat still, immersed in a state of calm, but around him it seemed to exude a strange kind of power that made everyone both afraid and admired. Every day, in the morning when people in the area came to sit around the ashram yard, he would begin teaching.

All disasters, tribulations or good things are created by ourselves, so don't blame anyone. Doing good brings good results, doing evil brings bad results. Therefore Every thought, word, and action must be careful, don't do anything wrong because the Law of Cause and Effect will not be ignored.

Timotheus practiced much more seriously than me, he could sit all day, sometimes without eating or drinking, his breathing became lighter and lighter, to the point of not breathing anymore. The first time I saw him not breathing, I panicked and walked over to see what was wrong with him, but our Teacher signaled me to stop and not to disturb his practice. After that, Timotheus said he was able to enter a very deep meditation, no longer affected, his thoughts completely stopped, his breathing almost stopped. Our teacher seemed satisfied. He said that if he continued, he could enter realms that ordinary language could not explain.

Every year, Timotheus and the Indian sages often spent many months in retreat in mountain caves, without contact with anyone. As for me, I was still not ready for such a retreat, so I continued to live in Bactria. Every week, I bring them food supplies. The road from Bactria to the mountain cave is quite far, I had to travel from early morning to noon to get there. Going early helped me avoid the scorching heat of this arid mountainous area. When I leisurely walked slowly to the rhythm of my breathing, I felt the tranquility of the mountains and forests as well as the wonderful beauty of nature. The majestic scene of the mountains and forests brings me a gentle, deep joy, but sometimes it also makes me fearlessly. Walking on the desolate rocky slopes, even the slightest sound startled me. In this area, there is a wolf breed that is small but very fierce. Not long ago, a group of Greek soldiers out hunting were attacked by this pack of ferocious dogs. From then on, I worried about Timotheus and his fellow practitioners. When Timotheus went into retreat, I gave him a set of bows and arrows and a long spear to deal with in case he encountered wild animals. Our teacher saw that and said: "We have our own weapon, which is compassion (compassion), we don't need the other things." Although I did not agree with that thought, I knew I could not change the Master's decision, so I placed food and water bottles in front of the cave entrance and brought back the weapons. On the way home, the more I thought about it, the more I admired Timotheus's courage and desire to learn. He gave up all his fame and position and steadfastly followed his chosen path.

Time passes quickly, I have lived in Bactria for twenty years. When I came here, my hair was still black but now it has turned silver. Through information from merchant groups frequenting Bactria, I learned that the war between generals was still continuing. From Macedonia to Thrace, from Egypt to Syria, many cities were burned, everywhere there were killings, social chaos, and people's misery. The Phalanx armies that fought invincibly in the past are now divided into factions and kill each other. The widespread hatred, anger and destruction has confused and frightened the Greeks. No one talks about the ideal of building a strong and prosperous empire anymore like before. To pay for the war, the assets of rich nobles were confiscated. Whenever there was a shortage of food, soldiers were given freedom to loot, so looting, rape, and killing happened everywhere. In the past, Alexander's army was very disciplined, but now the war has lasted too long, and the morale of the soldiers has disintegrated and changed. Currently, they only know how to loot and appropriate property, land and women. The majestic Doria melodies calling for patriotism that once resounded have now completely disappeared, replaced by arousing sensual sounds, calling for enjoyment. Facing the line between life and death every day, everyone is confused and scared, no one knows what the future will be like. The vast Greek empire that Alexander worked hard to build was now divided into seven. Ptolemy proclaimed himself Pharaoh of Egypt, Antigonus king of Asia Minor, Seleucus king of Babylon, Cassander king of Greece, Lysimachus king of Thrace. These people have been close friends since childhood, played together, grew up together, and studied with Aristotle with the noble ideal of building a powerful Greece, without the shadow of foreign invaders. But now, power, fame, status, land, gold and silver have caused them to change and become hostile. Once again, I am reminded of Homer's poem, No one goes through war and remains the same.

***

After listening to Thomas talk about his time living in Bactria, I asked him if after twenty years of practicing meditation, he had reached a certain level. Thomas only briefly said that at that time he was able to enter concentration very quickly, his breathing was as light as if it were nothing, all thoughts stopped, his whole body felt light and peaceful. However, he didn't say anything more and reminded me that it wasn't important.

Thomas also reiterated that although humanity is currently entering the stage of Degeneration and Destruction, everyone must believe that changing consciousness can still happen. He emphasized that one must have a firm belief in the transformation of karma to be able to overcome difficulties and not be influenced by disturbing external events. If you are not clearly aware, it is easy to be swayed by those events. Everything that happens in this world is cause and effect, nothing happens without a cause. All are lessons for humanity to learn. There are lessons for each individual and there are lessons for each country. If you can't learn it now, you will have to learn it again another time. All current disasters come from karma. If you understand like that, you must know how to do good deeds to neutralize karma and change your destiny as well as call on everyone to join hands to do good deeds to help transform collective karma for society. At that time, when illness comes, there will be good medicine. Evil deeds will turn into good deeds.

He added that the karma that is controlling humanity today originates from killing and greed. Looking around the world, everywhere there is strife and hatred, everywhere there is killing and killing, so natural disasters and epidemics are obvious. He emphasized that wherever there is a lot of killing, there are a lot of accidents; Where there is less hatred, there is peace. Disasters, epidemics, and wars are all man-made, but if you know the rules to change your karma and do good deeds with sincerity because you know it is something you must do for the common good, then there is nothing to worry about.

Thomas also added that he noticed a huge difference between practitioners in the past compared to today. During the time when Buddhism was still flourishing, the monks all understood the Buddha's teachings. Nowadays, through many ups and downs, the number of people who truly study is becoming less and less, some only rely on religion as a livelihood to ensure a safe and comfortable life. A large number of practitioners no longer keep the precepts or focus their practice on liberation from the cycle of birth and death, but only worry about calling people to cultivate blessings, make offerings, build large pagodas, sculpt large statues and other superficial forms. They assign themselves titles, positions, and promote their ego, even though they don't practice much. Furthermore, many people still exalt their methods of practice, considering themselves superior to others, declaring that one sect is better than another, leading some people down the path of discrimination and dispute.

Because, Buddhism is divided into three periods: Dharma, Dharma and Dharma Ending. During the Dharma period, everyone diligently practiced meditation (solid meditation). During the Dharma Statue period, most people only focused on building pagodas and stupas to gain blessings (solid temples), and those who truly practiced became fewer and fewer. During the Dharma Ending period, there were fewer people who practiced, everyone only fought against each other, no one was willing to give in to the other (Strong struggle). Monks no longer uphold the precepts but only pay attention to worshiping and donating rituals to build their name and status.

When Buddha was still alive, there was only one teaching: Buddha Dharma. After he entered nirvana, his disciples went everywhere spreading the Dharma and depending on their understanding, the teachings also leaned towards one part or another. For example, people who like to practice meditation pay more attention to teaching about meditation, and people who like the law pay more attention to the law. Therefore, there began to be a sectarian divide. In addition, the teachings must also be adapted to the customs, culture and language of the localities where they come to propagate the Dharma. Although there are differences in teaching methods, the basic purpose is completely the same. People who study Buddhism must realize that the basis and purpose of Buddhism is liberation from the cycle of birth and death by eliminating craving, eliminating greed and desire, and eliminating delusion. Once you know the purpose, the method is no longer important. Therefore, one should not distinguish one method from another, or one sect from another. All are the teachings of the Buddha and all are equal, there is no distinction between high and low or one method is superior to another.

Each person must choose for themselves a suitable method to practice because the goal of all is liberation from the cycle of birth and death. There are many methods or paths, anyone can go whichever way they want. When Buddhism was introduced to countries such as Sri Lanka, Burma, and Thailand, the customs, culture, and language of these countries were still limited, so some of the things taught were not accurate but were responded to by the masses. Meanwhile, when Buddhism spread to China, where culture and language were very rich, the teachings were like good seeds finding fertile ground to grow strongly. When Buddhism spread to Tibet, this country already had a tradition of Bon magic [1] so Tantric Dharma was given more emphasis than other teachings. Likewise, when Buddhism was transmitted to Bactria and Persia, which was influenced by Greece, it favored the method of debate and dialogue, as a philosophical trend that required doubt and deep thinking...

Pensive for a moment, Thomas slowly finished telling me the end of Kyros' life in Greece.

We only know how to use the senses of the body without being aware of it that they are very limited. Our brain is just a mass of flesh, if Without the soul behind it, it cannot do anything. Even Our thinking and thinking are not perfect because we only rely on things knowledge that has been taught before. If this knowledge is lacking then Our understanding is also imperfect.

tieu_de: Part Three: Karmic Attraction - Desire and Retribution
noi_dung:
PART THREE

Karma

SEXUAL MENTALITY AND KARMA

One day, as I left home, I saw a group of people with tattered clothes coming from afar. This scene is not strange, because to avoid war, recently more and more Greeks have come to this country as refugees. I looked away from the crowd and was about to walk away when I heard a voice calling my name. I stopped, looked closely at the oncoming crowd, and noticed a very familiar figure walking towards me. It's Philiteus! He was the commander of the army that transported gold and silver with me in the past. Philiteus happily called out:

- Kyros, is that you?

I was surprised:

- Philiteus… Why?… Why did you… end up like this?

Philiteus happily hugged me. It took a while for our emotions to pass. Philiteus then spoke up in a hoarse voice:

- I'm so happy to see you again. How many years have it been...

Looking at my old friend's body covered in wounds, his uniform tattered and torn, my heart is extremely bitter. The group of people accompanying Philiteus were also in a similarly dire situation. I hurriedly invited everyone into the house, arranged for them to bathe, eat and rest. When only the two of us were left, Philiteus began to tell:

- As you may remember, my Silver Shields (Silver Shields) army is under the command of General Eumenes. When Antigonus and Eumenes cooperated to attack Ptolemy and Seleucus, we accomplished many victories. However, later Eumenes also wanted to be king and refused to obey Antigonus anymore, so Antigonus killed him. At that time, Antigonus did not believe in the loyalty of the Silver Armor army anymore, so he disarmed and exiled us to the desert - where barbarian tribes lived. We had to fight these tribes to survive. Due to lack of weapons, unfamiliarity with the soil and terrain, and lack of food, my army was almost completely destroyed, only a few remnants escaped. Knowing that Bactria was still under Greek control, we sought refuge, but did not expect to meet him.

The Silver Armor is Macedonia's most elite army, established during the reign of King Philip with very high selection standards. Most of them were tall, strong, and absolutely loyal to the royal court, so they wore armor and round silver shields. They are responsible for guarding the palace and looking after the treasury. When Alexander went on an expedition, he brought this army with him as his personal guard. In every war, they always followed him closely, serving as both a protective and assault force, and accomplished many victories. A group in this army was assigned the task of transporting gold, silver and booty to Pella. With all those victories and glory, I never thought that one day they would fall into such a dead end. Philiteus continued with a sad look:

- After Alexander died, Demosthenes returned to Athens, calling on the people to rise up against the Macedonian court. With the gold he took from public funds, he also recruited many soldiers but in the end he still could not compete with Antipater's elite army. After the defeat, Demosthenes committed suicide. Harpalus escaped to Crete for several years before being captured and sentenced to death. Deasius fled to Ilia, living in peace until Antipater died, and Cassander became emperor. Knowing that the king needed gold to gather troops to fight Antigonus, Deasius brought the gold he had taken back to the court in exchange for amnesty. Currently, the couple is back to live in Pella.

More than twenty years have passed, the peaceful life in Bactria and the practice of meditation have made me almost no longer think about the past. Suddenly hearing old stories and mentioning old people, my peaceful soul began to be disturbed again. Isidora, the girl I secretly loved since childhood, was also the person who hated me, said the most hurtful things to me, and, ironically, was also my half-sister that I later learned about. The news about Isidora brought back many painful memories and emotions that I thought I could bury forever. From that moment on, I couldn't concentrate my mind like before, because whether in normal times or when practicing meditation, Isidora's image kept lingering in my mind. I complain to Timotheus:

- Recently, when practicing I kept seeing the image of a girl...

Timotheus was so surprised that he interrupted me:

- How is that possible? When I first started practicing, I sometimes saw these and that images. But that's because at that time my practice was still weak and lacking in concentration. Anyone who doesn't have enough concentration will encounter this phenomenon, it's normal. But you have been practicing for more than twenty years and have strong concentration, how could you be affected like that?

I shook my head:

- I can't concentrate, I keep being disturbed by this girl...

Timotheus frowned:

- This is so strange, there must be some deep cause... You have to know how to put that image down, don't pay attention to it anymore. Just try to hold your breath to steady your mind, no matter what image comes, it will go away on its own. If you let it control you, waste your efforts, and continue to drift in life and death, how can you escape samsara? Now we are both older, if you don't try to get through this now, then maybe there is still a chance? If we miss it, who knows when we will have the chance again? You must know how to let go...

Timotheus's sincere advice made me feel ashamed. I don't say anything more. But I still can't get rid of the torment about this girl. For weeks afterward, the image of Isidora and the bitter memories of her continued to bother me. I know that deep inside, I still carry an inferiority complex, and Isidora is the spark that ignites that feeling of inferiority in me. Isidora's insults from the past are still raw wounds. Even though many years have passed, even though I have let go of the past to practice, I know I still hope to see her again, to at least hear from her an apology, or a few gentle words to erase this sense of inferiority. I still hope that perhaps when Isidora knows my true identity, she will have a different view and accept me as family. These thoughts continuously disturbed me and then completely dominated me, leaving me unable to calm down.
