After many sleepless nights, I decided to return to Pella to find Isidora. I wrote a short letter to Timotheus and invited Philiteus to go to Pella. At first Philiteus refused because returning to Pella at this time was very dangerous. However, when he learned that I was determined to leave, Philiteus changed his mind, because with the current unstable situation, it was difficult for me to resist bandits or undisciplined soldiers alone. Philiteus took five soldiers with him and set out with me. Because we were no longer young and the world was unstable, it took nearly six months for us to reach Pella. After many years of war, Macedonia has changed a lot, the former prosperity has been replaced by ruined houses, walls with burn marks - the result of battles between Greek generals. Passing through the ruins, we spurred our horses to run quickly to Dimitris's farm.

We went straight through the gate, through the large garden, where we met an old slave at work. He looked at us in surprise, then his expression gradually changed. He recognized me and quickly ran in to tell the owner. I had just dismounted when Deasius, who was inside, came out. He has aged a lot, but the unpleasant and hostile expression on his face has not changed much. His cold eyes looked straight at me, he said in a cautious voice:

- Kyros, what are you doing here? This is our house, don't even think about dividing the family property.

I shook my head:

- No, I was just visiting...

At that moment, Isidora walked out from inside. Even though many years have passed, even though she is old, Isidora still looks no different from the image in my memory, still beautiful and elegant. And I, after so many years, am still awkward, clumsy and cowardly in front of her. As soon as Isidora saw me, she spoke coldly:

- Slave, why did you come back here? Sophia told me your identity, but I did not accept it. Don't think you can become a member of this family, you're not worthy. You will forever be just a despicable slave.

Isidora's harsh words almost petrified me. I thought that a biological relationship would make her treat me more kindly and fairly, I thought that she would help me resolve my long-standing problems, but unexpectedly she stabbed me again. Is this the Isidora I've always loved? So many old and new pains came flooding back, I just stood rooted to the spot, unable to react, nor able to speak. Seeing that, Philiteus stepped out and said loudly:

- I was also present when I opened Dimitris' letter, he confirmed that Kyros was his son, this is undeniable! In addition, Dimitris also gave Kyros a part of this farm.

Deasius laughed and turned back to his wife:

- I knew right away, this vile group came here just to demand division of the estate.

Philiteus said nothing but his hand was on his sword. Deasius looked at the people standing behind Philiteus. Although no one was wearing military uniforms, with the tattoos on their bodies, every Macedonian would have recognized them as the Silver Armor troops. Deasius squinted his eyes, thinking for a moment, then changed his tone:

- Okay, everyone go inside, let me call Sophia to come talk.

We entered the hall with tall stone pillars, where we used to run and play when we were children. The scenery has hardly changed, but now everything becomes extremely strange and cold. Isidora turned and walked away without even glancing at me. Deasius called a few slaves over to whisper a few words and then motioned for us to sit.

I still couldn't get over the feeling of shock so I sat silently. Philiteus saw that and spoke up:

- Where is Melissa? Call her out here.

Deasius shook his head, his voice indifferent:

- It died a long time ago, it's no longer here.

I woke up as if I had just received a slap, stood up and asked:

- What? Is Melissa dead? Why die… Why?

Deasius shrugged:

- How do we know? I heard he got sick and died before we got here.

The news of Melissa's death shocked me. How could such a gentle, gentle, and loving girl have such a short life? Why is fate so unfair to her? I sat down on the chair stunned, Philiteus was also speechless. The atmosphere in the room suddenly became stuffy. Deasius looked at us uncomfortably, occasionally turning back outside as if waiting for something. Isidora stood still next to the stone pillar, his face not showing any emotion.

Suddenly, from outside came the neighing of horses and loud footsteps. Philiteus and the Silver Armor soldiers stood up in alert. At that moment, a powerful army of soldiers, swords and spears shining, rushed to surround us. Philiteus's soldiers also drew their weapons, but Philiteus signaled them to stop. The commander of the group of soldiers sat on a horse and shouted loudly:

- Those rebels, what are you doing here?

Being surrounded by a large, well-armed army, while Philiteus only had a few old soldiers, if he fought, it would be clear whether he won or lost. While we didn't know how to deal with dozens of spears pointed at us, from outside the gate, a horse-drawn carriage rushed in at full speed. Sophia rushed down from the car, looked at the army surrounding us, she shouted:

- Wait, wait... What happened? Why is this?... Where is Kyros?

Deasius saw this and shouted loudly:

- These guys are Antigonus's army. Don't let them escape.

At that time, the war between Antigonus and Cassander was coming to a fierce point. As soon as Deasius finished speaking, the group of soldiers surrounding us immediately took action. The scuffle happened as quickly as lightning, spears were swung, swords clashed and screams rang out. Philiteus described the sudden conflict and laughed loudly:

- Very good, it is better for me to die in my homeland than to leave my body in the mountains and forests.

Deasius stood to the side watching with triumph. Suddenly he pointed at me and shouted:

- That guy is the leader of this rebel group, we must kill him immediately.

I was so flustered that before I could react, I was hit by a spear in the chest, blood gushing out. My eyes were dizzy, my head was dizzy, and I was weak. I turned back to look at Isidora, she stood coldly behind the stone pillar, indifferently watching me fall, without the slightest expression of concern. I heard Sophia scream loudly:

- Stop, stop... don't kill Kyros!

I wanted to speak up but was hit by several more spears. I immediately collapsed to the ground, trying to look at Isidora again, but my eyes were dark.

When I opened my eyes again, I found myself lying on a small bed, my whole body was in so much pain that I couldn't breathe. A tall man with thick beard and hair was sitting next to the bed. It took me a moment to realize it was Antigenidas. I whispered:

- Antigenidas? Where am I…?

Antigenidas's voice trembled:  

- Kyros… I didn't expect… You're in Melissa's room. 

I can only say short sentences:

- Melissa... Where is Melissa?

Antigenidas shook his head sadly:

- He got sick and died a long time ago. At that time, I was still on the battlefield, completely unaware. When I returned from the army, I could no longer see him. I live here now, in Melissa's room.

At that moment, Sophia walked in from outside:

- Kyros, please lie still... wait until you get better and we'll talk later.

Antigenidas shook his head:

- Kyros' wound is very serious, it is difficult to recover.

I tried to ask in a whisper:

- How are Yasamin and Leonidas's child?

Antigenidas pointed behind:

- They are here, she and Alberla are still healthy.

I stammered and wanted to say more, but my whole body ached and my mind became dazed. Antigenidas leaned close to my chest to listen, then turned and said to Sophia:

- My heart is beating very weakly, it must be difficult...

Sophia burst into tears. Antigenidas whispered:

- Kyros, do you have any other wishes?  

Knowing I could no longer live, I whispered:

- I want... I want to hear... a song... Lydia.

Antigenidas immediately turned back and said to a young girl standing nearby:

- Alberla, please play Lydia for Kyros.

I tried to keep my mind awake but my breathing was interrupted. I know the final moment is near. Suddenly the Lydian melody of the Harp sounded. I realized that it was the song Melissa sent to Leonidas the other day. Sweet memories of my youth came rushing back, when I was the one delivering love letters to the two of them. My entire life flashed before my eyes – childhood friends, Isidora, music, war, prison, days of practice – at that moment I felt my chest ache, then my body suddenly felt lighter, as if a burden had been lifted.

I found myself floating in a pitch-black space. Time seemed to stop. I don't know how long I floated like that, but it was a very strange, indescribable feeling. I am aware that I am no longer myself because most of my memories gradually disappear, leaving only a vague understanding in the vast, endless space. This awareness is like a gentle, peaceful breath, spreading inside and outside me, then blending into everything in a strange way like when experiencing meditation practice. Timotheus's advice suddenly rang out: We are all older now, if you don't try to get through this now, then what chance will there be? If we miss it, who knows when we will have the chance again? You must know how to let go.... We must know how to let go... we must let go... Somehow, at that moment, my mind suddenly came up with an idea - I must return to Bactria to continue this unfinished practice. I have to return to Bactria...

***

Thomas stopped talking at that point because he was emotional. I remained silent so he could regain his composure. A moment later, Thomas continued:

- When I recalled that life, I clearly experienced death. In the past, Timotheus said that when one dies, the ego and senses perish, and the last thing left is A re da da consciousness. While listening to the lecture, to me it was just an abstract concept, but through that experience, I became very aware of what Timotheus had said. That vague awareness is no longer a sense of self or personal ego but a strange feeling of purity. I thought it was an experience of A re-da consciousness although at that time my practice was still poor and could not perceive clearly. But what I know very clearly is that all emotions and memories of the ego disappear, leaving only "knowing" (Awareness).

I asked further:

- So will you return to Bactria?

Thomas nodded:

- Yes, that was my last wish in that life.

We were silent, each chasing a thought. A moment later, Thomas smiled and said slowly:

- If you're ready, we can continue talking about my future life in Rome.

tieu_de: Part Four: Rome - Radiant Splendor and Killing Karma - Love in the Quest for Freedom
noi_dung:
PART FOUR

Roman - GLUE AND KARMA

LOVE IN THE DESIRE FOR FREEDOM

I don't remember what happened between my life in Greece and my life in Rome, but when I was born in Rome, the empire had entered a period of decline. Northern cities were often sacked by Visigoths and the imperial army was completely unable to defeat them. The southern coastal region is also constantly threatened by barbarians from Africa who come to harass. Many types of epidemics and natural disasters, from droughts to constant storms for many years, have weakened the economy, people have fallen into poverty and misery, and the court has continued to increase taxes to serve the lavish and wasteful spending of the emperors.

I was born in this life as the eldest child in a noble family. My name is Sirius. My father held the position of praetor (Praetor) at the port of Ostia, a position he saw as a means of ensuring the smooth running of the family's trade. My father owned a fleet of trading ships throughout the Mediterranean and at the same time he also had the right to decide which ships to search to collect taxes for the royal court, so my family's ships never had to pay taxes. Obviously, my family became one of the richest families in the Ostia region. Even though he lived in a luxurious and material situation, my father was still not satisfied. He always used all sorts of tricks to possess more. Everything in my house always revolves around money.

At that time, children of wealthy families mostly had tutors to teach at home. My brother and I had the same Greek teacher named Cyrus. He is a wise man, in charge of teaching us reading, writing, literature, history, mathematics and especially the art of speech. In addition, we also learned sports and martial arts with a retired gladiator named Marcus. From a young age, I did not like martial arts, but my younger brother Lucius was extremely passionate about it. Therefore, even though I am your brother, in matches I have never won against Lucius. Lucius is smart, excels in every sport and is always surrounded by many friends. On the contrary, I am a quiet person, do not talk much, do not like to gather with friends my age, I just like to be alone, quiet and thinking. This personality of mine is completely contrary to my father's expectations of his eldest son. To my father, I was a huge disappointment and he never hesitated to show that disappointment. I'm no stranger to criticism: You stupid, stupid boy, if you're like that, how can you become a Roman councilor?.

Having children as members of the Senate (Senatus) was the wish of parents belonging to the upper class and aristocracy at that time. The Senate is where all legal decisions will be discussed before being submitted to the emperor for promulgation and application. This was considered a prestigious position in society at that time, so entering the Senate was the goal of most children of the nobility. However, the real purpose behind wanting to become a parliamentarian is to protect the interests of the nobility through laws that benefit this class. The standard to become a congressman is to know how to be eloquent and reason based on historical or legal knowledge to win debates. Therefore, this is the subject that receives the most attention in the education of the nobility at this time.

Roman society at that time was divided into three classes. The aristocratic upper class (Patrician) are wealthy families, living in large, magnificent villas, owning a lot of property, land, gardens, and commercial establishments. Particularly close to the upper nobility in terms of wealth but with less political superiority were the merchants (Equite). Merchants who were rich enough could still enter the Senate, so merchants were generally considered to have equal status and the same class as nobles. After the aristocracy came the commoner class (Plebeian). This is the main part of Roman citizens, including the classes of farmers, workers and soldiers, although they are the majority but have no power, and have to live in small, narrow houses. Most commoners depended on the aristocracy, working for them in return for land and protection. Finally, the slave class (Slave) must serve both upper classes.

In our society, young people who reached the age of seventeen were considered adults, officially recognized as Roman citizens, and families would hold parties to celebrate this event. Noble families would hold lavish parties and invite other noble families to attend as an opportunity to socialize. Marriage between members of the nobility is a traditional covenant that protects each other's rights and supports each other. Unlike neighboring countries that allowed men to have multiple wives, Roman law clearly regulated marriage as monogamous. The purpose of marriage is to maintain the race and train future citizens for Rome. Family is considered the foundation of society and the eldest child has the responsibility to maintain this tradition by getting married and giving birth to children as soon as possible. At their coming-of-age party, young people will be called up to give a speech about life's purpose in front of all the guests. This is also the time when families with daughters will evaluate the young man to choose a son-in-law. In a society where marriage is decided by parents, according to the criteria of family registration or family interests, children, especially daughters, have no right to choose.

From a young age, we were trained in our ability to debate to prepare for our future careers. However, no matter how much I tried to practice, I still did not improve. Not only am I a quiet, reserved person who doesn't like to socialize, but I also have a stutter. As patient as Mr. Cyrus was, he also had to shake his head in frustration at my slowness. The feeling of inadequacy made me extremely miserable, but the most painful thing was that I was often compared to Lucius. My younger brother is not only talented but also extremely skillful. Lucius spoke fluently, his sports, hunting, and martial arts skills were all far beyond mine, so he was obviously loved by his parents. I also know that I am not as talented and clever as Lucius, so I still keep trying and often stay silent in the face of my father's criticism. However, deep inside me there is still resistance, I wonder why human value is only assessed by speaking or athletic ability and nothing else? Why can parents impose goals and then force their children to complete them, regardless of the child's true abilities, then compare superiority and inferiority, some love and some hate like that? What if your child doesn't become a member of parliament?

The only time I mustered up the courage to express my opinion on this matter made my father angry. He turned red and shouted loudly:

- You are the eldest child, you have responsibility for the family. Your future has been carefully planned. You must get married early to have children to continue the family line, then follow the trains to learn about the family trade. When you are old enough, I will arrange for you to enter the Senate to protect the rights of your family, and you must complete these things well. You don't have a choice.

Every few months Mr. Cyrus would take us to the Senate House to watch and learn more from the debates of the parliamentarians. Lucius could adapt to every situation and always behaved properly while I often asked questions that Mr. Cyrus considered inappropriate. I am an honest person and do not accept saying things that do not match my beliefs. Roman law clearly distinguished between right and wrong, but in debates and arbitration sessions in the Senate, I saw that most senators did not attach much importance to these laws. When people of the common class made mistakes, they were severely punished, but when the aristocracy made mistakes, they were given leniency. When we debated this issue, Lucius calmly defended those unfair decisions while I refused to accept what I thought was wrong. Teacher Cyrus shook his head and lamented:

- How can someone as naive as you become a member of parliament? In this day and age, you must know how to turn in the right direction. If you insist on doing the right thing, it will be very difficult to get ahead.

Roman education encouraged citizens to develop virtues such as courage, self-control and justice, but I witnessed that the law currently only protects the nobility, not caring about the common class or slaves. When a drought occurred, even though the food stored in warehouses in Rome was enough to last for six years, the Senate did not allow it to issue measures to respond and support the people because it believed that taking away stored food to relieve famine could put the capital in danger if the drought lasted longer. The famine occurred in remote areas, the victims were all from the common class or slaves, and had no effect on the aristocracy, so it was not worth worrying about for the parliamentarians. Their indifferent and insensitive attitude towards the extreme hunger and poverty of the people is something I do not understand and cannot accept.

My family owned a lot of slaves. Since I was a child, I have had a strong attachment to them and have always treated them very kindly. But my father and other family members often beat and tortured the slaves and servants, making me both angry and pitiful. Most of the slaves who carried goods or served on my father's trading ships had their seals stamped on them, as a way to mark the family's property sovereignty. Slaves who escaped and were captured would have a mark on their forehead to identify the slave who had committed the crime. If they escaped a second time, when caught again they would be subjected to severe torture, they could be beaten until their legs were broken, or even executed in front of other slaves as a form of deterrence. Witnessing these things, I was extremely upset but couldn't do anything. Therefore, since I learned to think, I did not want to become a slave-exploiting merchant like my father, nor did I want to become a congressman like my uncle, specializing in manipulating and cooperating with factions in the Senate to overturn the law.

I'm not good at what my father wants me to do. I like reading books, but my father considers books to be worthless. Therefore, the relationship between my father and me was always not good. Not only that, he also told my mother that he only wished Lucius had been born before me. Sirius is so weak, if he only had half of Lucius's talent, he could become the richest man in Ostia – I don't know how many times I've heard words like that. Living in a family with high expectations, often comparing, and always thinking about money, I found myself alone and isolated. I became increasingly quiet, completely withdrawn into the world of books, where no one could hurt me.

Because I live such a private life, I never share my secrets with anyone. One of the secrets I keep is my dreams. Since childhood, I often dreamed of a strange land, seeing people dressed in rags, with shaved heads, begging for food. They look extremely austere, but their faces exude a strangely relaxed aura. Even in my dreams, I still clearly feel the feeling of peace and serenity when I see them. These dreams recur over and over, and for me, they always hold a strange, haunting attraction. Sometimes I think of that strange land, wishing to live freely and comfortably like the people I saw in my dreams, far away from the troubles of my family, far away from the inappropriate expectations that weighed heavily on the shoulders of a child who had just reached adulthood.

The Romans have a polytheistic religion, we believe that the gods have the power to bless as well as bring disaster. Therefore, the coming-of-age party of noble children was often held in the temple with a ritual of sacrificing offerings to the gods to bless them. Before my coming of age party, my uncle discussed with his family:

- The most profitable trade route today is the Silk Road (Silk road), bringing goods from the East through here. The Romans bought a lot of silk, spices, perfumes and handicrafts from Asian countries. This is a ten-profit business, guaranteed to bring in abundant income. Therefore, we must find a way to connect with Beria, the family that holds a lot of power and profits from this trade.

My father pondered for a moment and then said:

- This is not easy. The Silk Road was a land route, requiring convoys of people and horses to transport goods long distances. In addition, there must be special relationships with local officials controlling the route. Our current strength is only the convoys of ships traveling around the Mediterranean, to penetrate land resources is not easy.

My uncle patiently explained:

- Don't worry. Beria used to be the governor of Syria, most of the officials controlling the route on that route were his people. Six years ago, Beria's wife died, he resigned as governor to switch to trading, and in just a few years became extremely rich. This family has no son but only one daughter. If we arrange for Sirius to become a son-in-law for this family, we can develop trade to the East. We now have ships operating around the Mediterranean, if there were more overland trade caravans through Asia, the entire Roman trade industry would be in our family's hands. If you don't take this opportunity, how long will you wait?

My father shook his head, his voice annoyed:

- But Sirius is so poor, he has no talent, how can he catch the eye of this family? What our family wants, other families like Marius or Celius also want, they also have sons.

My uncle smiled mysteriously:

- So we have to be one step ahead. I have a plan for them to meet and get to know each other. When boys and girls meet each other early, feelings can easily arise and from there we can more easily convince Mr. Beria. Currently, the road is no longer safe because Visigoth groups are looting everywhere, so Beria also needs boats to transport goods. This is a mutually beneficial cooperation. Don't worry, I have arranged for my family to sit next to Mr. Beria and his daughter at the upcoming Maximus [2] arena.

The most popular and popular entertainment of Roman society at that time was watching gladiators kill each other in the arena. Most of the gladiators were slaves recruited to the training school. Some were criminals who asked to become gladiators instead of being imprisoned. The gladiators will be fully equipped with weapons and participate in life-and-death battles with other gladiators. Sometimes they will have to fight wild animals such as lions, tigers or wolves to bring joy to the guests. Although we learned martial arts from a retired gladiator, Mr. Marcus, he did not want us to go to the arenas. The teacher told us:

- I teach you martial arts, but I never want you to see scenes of people killing people for fun like that.

I don't like that kind of entertainment so I've almost never gone to those places. Lucius is different, he often goes to the arena with his friends and excitedly recounts the things he has witnessed or the gladiators he considers heroes.

During the gladiatorial viewing at the arena that my uncle arranged, we sat in the row of seats reserved for the nobility. Most noble families knew each other and traveled and interacted with each other. My mother brought me and Lucius to introduce everyone. Lucius walked over to greet each person and then cleverly invited a few girls to sit aside and chat happily.

What life is like today is all guided by previous habits or habits. The seeds of greed and selfishness often germinate in places where there are many disputes or wars. The seeds of art find places with suitable circumstances to develop... Therefore, it is our thoughts, words and actions in this life that will lead us where we will go in the next life, not determined by any gods. We are completely responsible for our lives.

Lucius is naturally talented in speaking, so he always has many girlfriends. On the contrary, from a young age I avoided contact with women, I liked to spend time alone to think. My world is full of questions but still has no answers. The more I withdrew into my own world, the more my father scolded me. During meals or when the family gathers, I am often brought up as a subject of ridicule, making me feel even more self-conscious.

That day, according to my uncle's arrangement, we sat near Mr. Beria's family. While my father and Mr. Beria talked, my uncle cleverly arranged for me to sit next to a simply dressed young woman. Her outfit and demeanor seemed much gentler and more comfortable than that of the other Roman noble girl. According to my uncle's introduction, her name is Valeria. I'm not used to socializing, so I just nodded to her and kept quiet. Valeria didn't know if she was paying attention to me or because she was bored, so she started a conversation:

- Do you like watching gladiatorial combat?

I shook my head:

- I have never seen gladiatorial combat.

Valeria smiled:

- This is also the first time I went to see it.

My uncle sitting next to me interrupted:

- You live in the capital and have never been to a gladiator match?

Valeria turned and nodded at him, softly answering in a measured manner:

- My father is often busy and away, so he doesn't feel safe letting me go anywhere alone. Since my mother passed away, I just stay home and read books.

My uncle is not a reader, so he probably couldn't find a topic to talk about further. He signaled me to start a conversation but I remained silent. Valeria turned to me and started talking again:

- I like reading books very much, especially Greek literature.

Roman culture was influenced by Greece, so it was not strange that Romans liked to read Greek books. I nodded to be polite, then Valeria asked again:

- Do you like reading books?

I nodded again. Valeria didn't pay attention to my distant attitude, she said innocently:

- I like reading books by Ovid, Livy, Seneca, Horace, and I also like poems by Adrianus, Aristeas and Sappho. In my opinion, no one can express human emotions more delicately than poets. It is said that music expresses human emotions on an unconscious level, but poetry is truly the voice of the heart. Each sentence, each word blends together to create a wonderful poem. If we read carefully, we can see that each rhyme and each word contains profound meanings and wonderful emotions. I believe that only people with sentimental souls with deep vibrations can use words and letters to create such gentle rhymes. In my opinion, Sappho's poetry is the most sincere voice of the heart.

I am no stranger to this female poet's love poems, but she is not my favorite poet. I nodded and answered briefly:

- I don't understand poetry as much as epics.

Under the guidance of teacher Cyrus, I fell in love with the majestic epics of Homer and Virgil. Homer's epic Iliad talks about the battle of Troy with characters such as Achilles, Hector, Paris, Helen... Virgil's epic Aeneid talks about the expansion of Rome into an empire and praises the peace of Augustus, through the life story of Aeneas, a soldier of Troy who took the people to safety when the city was destroyed. The troupe of Trojans wandered aimlessly looking for a place to settle. Aeneas met many beautiful women who fell in love with him, wanting him to stop wandering and give up his dream of restoring Troy to live with them. However, Aeneas resolutely put aside his personal feelings to pursue the ideal of finding a new place for his people to live a free life like in the past in Troy. They wandered to a strange region, fought hard with the lords here and then built a majestic city like Troy. Aeneas named it Rome (Rome). Therefore, the people of this country all carry the heroic blood of the people of Troy. They did not forget that their homeland was burned, so they conquered Greece to clear away their grudge hundreds of years ago. Of course, this is just a legend written by the poet Virgil, but these majestic poems have also made me think a lot. Did the Trojans really return to being Romans? Will the eternal resentment be resolved at another time?

Our conversation stopped because of the resounding sound of brass. The gladiators stepped onto the field. After the procedure of greeting the audience, each pair rushed to kill each other without any mercy. The bodies fell one after another, blood poured everywhere, one gladiator after another rushed in to kill, the screams and screams became louder and louder. I saw Valeria cover her face in fear while my uncle was excited, loudly cheering for his favorite gladiators. The audience's screams echoed throughout the arena, and I didn't want to see this scene of killing any longer. I turned away, thinking of Mr. Marcus, a famous gladiator who had won hundreds of battles in the arena, becoming the idol of countless contemporary gladiators. He often told us: As a gladiator, I have no choice so I am forced to do many brutal things that go against my conscience. However, you have the opportunity to choose, so never do such killings. Even animals before being killed will be scared and scream, let alone humans.

I was lost in thought when suddenly Valeria turned to me and whispered:

- I don't want to watch anymore, can you please take me out?

I didn't know how to react, but my uncle gently pushed me on the back and said:

- Maybe Valeria is thirsty, Sirius should take her out to rest a bit.

At my uncle's urging and seeing that Valeria had stood up to walk away, I hastily followed. We sat outside the arena, eating fruit and exchanging stories. Actually, it was only Valeria who spoke, I mostly just listened and nodded, occasionally speaking up to be polite. However, I was very surprised and impressed because Valeria had a very broad knowledge, unlike other noble girls who only cared about entertainment and parties that Lucius often invited home. Not only is she well-versed in the books of philosophers such as Plato, Ovid, and Epictetus, but she also clearly analyzes those theories, making people like me who read a lot of books applaud. Valeria told me about the place where she was born and the cultural customs of that region. Her father was the governor of Syria so she was born and raised in Jericho. When her mother died, her father resigned and turned to trading, so she returned to Rome. Since childhood, she and her parents visited scenic spots everywhere. She talked about the lifestyle of nomads in oases in the desert, and the strange customs of Palestine. As someone who has traveled a lot and experienced a lot, her knowledge is completely different from that of Roman girls who have never left the city limits all their lives.

The story was unfinished when suddenly Lucius and two girls came from somewhere. My brother enthusiastically said:

- Today the arena has a very special performance. You guys should quickly go back to the stands to watch, if you miss it you will be very sorry.

Valeria was surprised:

- What's so interesting?

Lucius laughed and said:

- Today we will see the lion tearing apart the Jewish crowd worshiping God.

Most of those who worship God are of the common class, of Jewish origin, coming from remote villages in Palestine and Syria who have moved to the provinces to live. They did all kinds of jobs to make a living, but because of the spirit of mutual support and willingness to help each other, over time, many people from the Roman common class also converted and converted to worshiping God. Some slaves also converted to this religion because those who worshiped God considered them friends and did not discriminate between classes. If this group of people became large, it could threaten the power of the nobility, so the Roman government issued a law that executed anyone who refused to worship Roman gods.

As soon as we got to our seats, the trumpet sounded and a group of people in ragged clothes were brought out into the middle of the arena. Valeria exclaimed:

- Why are it all women and children?

Lucius calmly explained:

- All the men were executed, only women and children remained.

This group of people was chased by soldiers wielding whips to the middle of the yard, near the iron cage holding lions that had been starved for many days. The trumpets and drums sounded urgently, the screams and shouts were loud, and the victims sat down on the ground in fear. Another drum sounded, the iron cage door was opened, the lions immediately jumped out, then leisurely walked around the huddled group of people, growling as they walked but not attacking. Lucius shouted in encouragement:

- Tear them apart, what are you waiting for!

The people around immediately chimed in:

- Tear apart! Tear apart! Tear away!

I sat there as if petrified, my chest beating continuously because I had never witnessed such a terrible scene. My head was filled with questions. Why can people enjoy the sight of wild animals tearing apart their fellow human beings? Why can people consider it entertainment?

The hungry lions continued to roam around the group of people cowering in fear, their growls getting louder and louder, clearly they were about to attack. Suddenly an older woman in the group of people in the yard stood up, clasped her hands together and prayed loudly. The whole group of people seemed to be urged by some force to stand up at the same time, clasping their hands and praying.

Suddenly, a strange scene happened. The largest lion with gray fur suddenly turned tail and ran back into the cage as if afraid of something. A group of ferocious lions were roaming around the group of people as if controlled by some invisible force. The whole group lay down on the ground, their growls silent. The audience was stunned, the cheers and screams died down, the entire arena was silent. At that moment, I felt my whole body vibrate as if an electric current ran from head to toe. Before I could calm down, I heard a loud scream:

- Where are the soldiers? Drive them to feed the lions!

A soldier holding a whip quickly ran up and swung it repeatedly at the group of people praying. Suddenly, a lion lying still nearby jumped up and pounced on the soldier, causing him to fall to the ground. The soldiers standing around rushed to save him, but it was too late, the lion had already bitten this man's throat. The hungry lions lying still, smelling the scent of blood, immediately jumped up and rushed to the soldier's body. The soldiers holding the whips were all so frightened by that scene that they quickly ran back, watching the lions tear the soldier's body into pieces. The audience was excited so they cheered loudly:

- That's right! Eat it, tear it apart!

The sound of the trumpet sounded again, but only for a short time and then fell silent. The screams of the audience gradually died down, because the lions only tore into the soldier's body and did not attack the people praying nearby. Chatter arose throughout the arena. Both emotional and scared, I sat motionless, my fists clenched, my chest beating continuously.

Suddenly on the emperor's honor stand there was a loud trumpet blast. A group of soldiers armed with bows and crossbows thundered out onto the field. After a loud shout, a series of arrows were shot, aiming straight at the group of people praying. Some were hit by arrows and collapsed, the sounds of women and children crying sounded pitifully. Despite the rain of arrows, some people continued to pray even though they had been hit by arrows, leaving only a little bit of their breath left.

Too scared and shocked, I turned away because I couldn't witness this scene anymore. I caught a glimpse of Valeria also turning away, discreetly wiping away her tears. Our eyes met and I felt a strange sympathy happening between me and her, as if our hearts were vibrating at the same beat. Suddenly Valeria stood up, turned and said to Mr. Beria:

- Father, I'm so dizzy, please take me home.

Beria was slightly surprised but also stood up and left the row of seats. Seeing that, my uncle immediately pulled me up and quickly followed Beria and his son. When I caught up with Mr. Beria, my uncle spoke:

- Perhaps my brother has already mentioned to you, we would be honored if you and Valeria could please take some time to attend Sirius' upcoming coming of age celebration at the Temple of Jupiter.

Beria stopped and looked at me intently. He was a stern and cold-looking man. His eyes looked at me with a questioning look, making me very confused and not knowing what to say. He thought for a moment then nodded:

- Okay, we will come.

My coming of age ceremony was held in the garden next to the temple of Jupiter. Before that, I tried to memorize the prepared speech. It was a cliché speech, filled with polite phrases and only expressing family expectations. I felt like that speech had nothing to do with me, but because I wanted to be left alone, I still tried to memorize it.

The guests attending that day were all noble families, many families brought their daughters because they considered this an opportunity for families to find partners for alliance through marriage.

The coming of age rite takes place inside Jupiter's temple, a place only for family members. I took off my protective necklace (Bulla [3] ) offered it to the gods, then received a blessing from the priests. Next, I put on new white clothes. My name is recorded in the Roman citizenship book. The ritual ended after my father donated a large cow to the temple so that the priests could make offerings to the gods. Thus, I was officially considered an adult. After that, we left the temple together and moved to the adjacent garden, where a sumptuous feast had been prepared and guests were waiting.

When I arrived, I saw that Beria's family was also present, Valeria was still dressed simply like the day we first met. This is a big party and everyone sees it as an opportunity to learn and make friends, so the girls attending all wear gorgeous makeup and formal jewelry. Valeria stands out from the crowd because of her elegance and serenity. We nodded slightly to each other, then I followed my father to greet the attending guests.

In the middle of the party, I was called up to give a mature speech. Although I stuttered a few sentences, I finally completed my prepared speech to the joy of my family. My father looked excited, he laughed loudly and said to the guests:

- You heard, my son not only wants to follow the family business but also has the ambition to become a member of the Roman parliament.

The crowd burst into laughter and applause, only I knew that what I had just said was not true. While everyone was happily eating, drinking and chatting, my uncle brought me to sit next to Valeria. All eyes at the banquet table were focused on us, perhaps because they knew that these were two people who were becoming the object of a negotiation between the two families. I was extremely confused, but Valeria seemed very calm, she freely talked to everyone. A moment later she turned to me and asked:

- It seems like you want to become a member of the council?

Normally in a situation like this I would just nod for formality, but without understanding what motivated me, I suddenly wanted to be honest with Valeria. I answered decisively:

- No! I never wanted to be a member of parliament.

Valeria showed a moment of surprise but quickly regained her composure, she continued asking:

- If so, do you want to take care of the family's merchant ship?

I answered frankly:

- No! I don't have that intention either.

This time, Valeria did not hide her surprise anymore. She raised her eyebrows and looked at me intently:

- So what do you want to do in the future?

No one has ever asked my opinion about what I want to do with my life. Since childhood, I was forced to do one thing or another by order of my family, no one cared about what I wanted or wanted to do. This was the first time someone paid attention to my wishes, even a stranger. Feeling both emotional and confused, I shook my head:

- I don't know yet, but I definitely won't be a councilman.

Valeria looked skeptical:

- But you just spoke...

Long-pent-up resentment suddenly flared up, I interrupted Veleria:

- It was all my father's idea. I'm just saying what you want. Actually, I...

I didn't finish my words because I suddenly realized I was confiding my secret feelings to a stranger. Valeria looked at me sympathetically and then asked just loud enough for me to hear:

- Is there anything you don't like?

I was startled:

- Did you notice that?

Valeria nodded and said gently:

- I know there are things we cannot change, but we can still control our attitude towards this undesirable situation. We can still find our own joy.

Valeria's sincere words of comfort made my sympathy for her grow more and more. But why does she use the word we? Does she also have things that are not as expected? This is the first time I feel like I can boldly talk to someone of the opposite sex without feeling embarrassed. I asked:

- Do you also have things that are not as expected?

Valeria nodded, her eyes flashed with sadness, but she quickly regained her composure and turned to other things. I sensed that Valeria had something she didn't want to confess, so I didn't force her to do anything. I asked to avoid it:

- So, when something goes wrong, what do you do?

Valeria answered softly:

- I pray to God to help me distinguish clearly and clearly between things that can be changed and things that cannot be changed, so that I can do the things that can be done, and I don't care about the things that cannot be changed.

I grew up with books and have read most of the famous philosophers, but the words that came out of Valeria's mouth still impressed me greatly. This is a new thought that I believe I have never heard or read before. Valeria hesitated a bit then added:

- I ask Him to help me have enough courage to accept things that don't go my way so that I can comfort others rather than being comforted by others; to be able to sympathize with others rather than be sympathized with; to be able to spread love rather than being loved, because I know that only when I truly give will I receive. Only by forgiving others can we be forgiven...

So impressed with the unusual words I just heard, I stared at Valeria, unable to react. It took me a while to realize I was being rude. I regained my composure and asked her:

- But who did you ask for at that time? Do you pray to Jupiter, Neptune or Apollo?

Valeria was thoughtful and a little hesitant. She did not answer my question but gently asked again:

- It seems you don't believe in prayer?

It is true that I have never been interested in gods like Jupiter, Neptune, Mars or Apollo. Living in a family that only values ​​money, my parents view clergy as people who take advantage of the gods to parasitize society. Therefore, even though I live in a polytheistic Roman society, I never pray. I nodded:

- You could say so. My parents taught me to worry about making money and not to expect anything distant or useless from the gods.

Valeria did not show any displeasure but said sincerely:

- I think we don't have to worry too much about money like that. You won't worry if you know that all your needs will be met, if you know how to give, you will receive it back. If you serve, blessings will come to you...

I was both confused and surprised, I didn't understand what she was referring to. I asked:

- What do you mean by that? Is prayer going to solve everything, even the unsatisfactory things?

Valeria smiled:

- If you pray sincerely, there will definitely be an response. If you knock on the door, it will open, but you have to knock first. When you pray, you will see your soul gradually calm down, all your worries will be erased, and you will be able to overcome these undesirable things.

I was surprised:

- Do you really believe that?

Valeria's eyes sparkled, she looked at me sincerely, then said in a very soft voice:

- I believe in prayer and I pray every day. Since coming to Rome, I have had no one to share my feelings with, so I always hope to have someone who understands me, but if I want to find such a friend, I must share it first. If I say something incorrect, please ignore it.

I was moved, unconsciously holding Valeria's hand:

- No, you said it very well. I'm willing to be friends with you.

This is the first time I feel like I can talk naturally with a girl, partly because what Valeria shares is very new and impressive, partly because she always shows me sincerity and is not polite like other girls.

Valeria continued to share:

- Since my mother passed away, my father switched to trading so he often goes far away and is rarely home. Now I have returned to live in Rome, but I still prefer Syria.

I consoled:

- Maybe you don't like Rome right now, but living here for a while you will have many friends, attend many entertainment parties and you will like it.

Valeria shook her head:

- No! I see Rome as just a dry desert, full of brutality, strife, and cruelty, incomparable to Syria, where there are long, green, cool oases that bring peace to the soul. It is a place full of love like a stream of cool, sweet water where travelers in the hot desert can stop to drink and soothe their souls.

Valeria's unusual comparison surprised me so much. How can Rome with its magnificent and splendid architectural buildings be compared to a dry desert? And Syria, a desolate, hot desert, is praised by her as a green, cool place with cool, fresh water? Seeing my silence, Valeria gently asked:

- You didn't answer me just now, what do you want to do in the future?

I was confused:

- I don't know... My parents have arranged everything, I just need to follow...

Valeria looked at me with deep eyes, she considered her words and then gently said:

- Do you think you should let someone else arrange your life? In my opinion, life is yours alone and only you have the right to decide. In addition, the purpose of life is not just to achieve a certain position, but what is important is what to do to make life more meaningful.

I hesitated:

- But I'm not as talented as Lucius. My brother is smart, talented, he succeeds in everything he does.

Valeria shook her head:

- Feeling inferior like that doesn't make any sense. If you know how to use your life to do meaningful things, everything you need will come to you. If you have firm faith in your work, everything will magically come to you. Don't worry too much, because once you honestly dedicate yourself, you won't lack anything. What do you want to do most now?

Without thinking or being cautious, I blurted out:

- I just want to be free to go here and there like you...

Valeria smiled, nodded:

- If you have a chance to go to Syria, I will introduce you to my friends there. They will take you to visit the sights like you said.

We continued to chat comfortably and intimately until the party ended and the guests left. I said goodbye to Valeria and promised to visit her in a few days. I returned home with a happy heart. For the first time in my life, I had friends and was no longer alone. For the first time in my life, I really thought about what I wanted to do in the future.

Not long after returning home, my father called a family meeting and announced:

- Perhaps Sirius did not make any impression on Beria. I proposed but he refused. However, Marius' family likes Sirius.

Lucius smiled mischievously and interjected:

- Maybe Beria did not intend to choose a bridegroom, but did everyone notice how intimately Sirius and Valeria talked to each other? Sirius has never talked to a woman before.

My uncle was surprised:

- Is there such a thing? We were so busy discussing that we didn't pay attention.

Lucius looked at me and smiled, his eyes blinking:

- Sirius, what do you think? I saw the two of them chatting happily. Do you like Valeria?

Everyone turned to look at me, making me flustered and speechless, I could only nod awkwardly.

My uncle laughed and nodded:

- Great, if so, we need to create opportunities for the two of us to be closer together. If his father is not ready, I will make him ready. A fire that has been near straw for a long time is also sharp. From now on, Sirius must visit Valeria often, as much as possible.

The whole family gathered together to talk, and like always, no one asked me anything else, and this was probably the only time I didn't feel offended about it. However, just a few days later, my uncle came home in a panic. He rushed to me, panting:

- Sirius, from now on don't contact Valeria anymore. What a shocking thing...

My father heard the noise so he walked over and just heard my uncle's words. My father was surprised:

- Why is that? What happened?

My uncle grimaced, shook and said:

- Unbelievable. For a long time, the royal court has been monitoring a group of Jews operating secretly in Rome. Yesterday the soldiers arrested this entire group while they were meeting to pray. The surprising thing was that little Valeria was present in this group and was one of the children traveling to preach Christianity. The fact that the daughter of a Roman official worshiped God greatly discredited the court, so the emperor ordered her to be executed immediately. Currently, the court is investigating those involved, so we must avoid contact with this family to avoid being implicated.

My father quickly asked:

- What about Mr. Beria?

My uncle replied:

- Beria did not know anything about his son following this group of Jews. He went to the temple of Jupiter to apologize and loudly curse the Jewish gods, doing so to ask for pardon for his son. This matter was assigned to Judge Summarus to judge. However, once the emperor gives an order, sooner or later he will be brought to the arena to be prey to the lions.

I was stunned and stunned by what I had just heard. Recalling the scene where Valeria shed tears because the worshipers of God were executed in the arena, I now understand that it was more than simple compassion. My chest was pounding, my heart felt like it wanted to jump out of my chest.

Lucius grimaced in fear:

- How could such an innocent girl be a missionary?

My uncle explained:

- Maybe he lived in Syria since he was young so he was influenced by the Jews. When his mother passed away, his father was busy with business and paid no attention to him. Luckily, we haven't yet connected with this family. From now on, we must be careful. If anyone asks, we must say that we do not know this family. Sirius must absolutely never mention anything about that girl again, much less go see her.

Since childhood, I have always been an obedient child, always following my parents' arrangements, but this time I know I can't do that. Even though we've only met and talked a few times, Valeria has left a special impression in my heart. I decided to meet her for real. Knowing that Valeria was imprisoned in the arena, I went to Marcus, told him about my feelings for this girl and asked him to help me meet Valeria again. Marcus is a famous gladiator. Although he has retired, he is still highly respected by contemporary gladiators, so entering and leaving the arena is not difficult. He listened to my presentation and then said:

- I can take you to the arena to meet your lover one last time, but you must absolutely listen to me and not do anything careless.

Want to return to my true self (true self) must know how to let go of frivolous values and illusory fame to develop the ability to understand deeply.

Marcus gave me a helmet that covered my face and led me into the arena. We went straight down to the deep cellar. When they saw him, all the gladiators politely greeted him. We arrived at the prisoner's cell and saw a group of gladiators standing around Beria. In front of them was a man who seemed to be a high official. I knew it was Summarus. Marcus signaled me to stand still behind him. Most of those captured were taken to the cellar door to prepare for the arena. Valeria alone was taken to the corner for final interrogation. Summarus spoke up:

- Hey little girl, because your father has contributed to Rome, I give you one last chance. If you kneel before the statue of Jupiter and loudly curse your god or something three times, I can be lenient.

Valeria firmly shook her head. Summarus smiled faintly:

- Because I sympathized with your father, I gave you a favor. If you are so stubborn then I must enforce the law.

Beria collapsed in front of Valeria, trembling and said:

- My child, please love this father. You just need to kneel before Jupiter and swear to worship the Roman god forever, everything can change...

Valeria firmly shook her head. Beria hugged Valeria's leg:

- My child! Please love this old father. I cannot live without children. Please listen to Summarus, my child...

Seeing that Valeria remained silent, Summarus shouted:

- We don't have much time. Hey girl, I give you one last chance. Hurry and curse your god loudly and everything will be saved.

Valeria solemnly replied:

- My life and soul belong to Him. Only He has the right to judge me. Your laws mean nothing to me…

Summarus was so angry that he gritted his teeth. Beria cried out loudly:

- My child, listen to Summarus and then you can have whatever you want.

Suddenly Valeria knelt down and took Beria's hand:

- Father! I only ask you one favor.

Beria said immediately:

- Whatever you want, whatever you want, I'm ready...

Valeria said:

- I ask you to take care of Sirius, if that's the case then I'll leave without any regrets...

Beria was surprised and asked:

- What? Sirius? Why?

I was also surprised and shocked. Why is that girl I just met still thinking of me at this moment? Valeria answered slowly:

- Up until now, father has always lamented not having a son to continue the family line and wanted to find a husband for him. Now I have found it for you, Dad. It's Sirius.

Beria collapsed to the ground and cried loudly:

- Valeria, Valeria, my child, why can't you deny the gods of the Jews? He died on the cross a long time ago, so who else can he save?

Valeria stood up, clasped her hands and prayed:

- Our Father in heaven. Father, please forgive us as we also forgive those who sin against us because they do not know what they are doing. I will obey Your will on earth as well as in heaven...

Summarus saw this and became furious, shouting loudly:

- You bastard, take this girl out to feed the wild animals immediately.

Valeria did not flinch, she stood there and continued to pray:

- In places full of hatred, Father, please let me sow the seeds of love...

A gladiator standing nearby spoke up:

- Sir, the other day, the fact that the lion did not eat the Jews created unfavorable public opinion. This time the emperor ordered them to mutilate their bodies, put them on crosses for the kites to eat, and let the crows eat them, so that they would slowly die to deter the people.

Summarus waved his hand to signal execution, two strong gladiators stepped forward and pulled Beria out, his cries echoed throughout the tunnel.

I was shocked and horrified by that terrible punishment. With this punishment, the sinner will be mutilated in many places on the body and then hung on a wooden pole in the middle of the arena for crows and kites to gouge out their eyes, pick off every piece of skin, every fiber of flesh down to the bone, lasting for several days, wanting to die but not being able to die. This was a punishment that the Roman people at that time enjoyed very much, because they could both watch kites eat crows and bet with each other to see when the sinner would die or who would die first. A gladiator pulled out his sword and walked up to Valeria as she still clasped her hands in prayer. I was about to step forward when Marcus turned to stop me. He leaned into my ear and whispered:

- You must stay absolutely silent, let me take care of this.

Not waiting for me to react, as soon as I finished speaking, Marcus stepped out and said loudly:

- This girl is stubborn, please give me the honor of punishing her.

Seeing their idol step out, all the gladiators in the cellar shouted in unison:

- That's right! This honor belongs to you, please take action.

A gladiator stepped forward, respectfully offering his sword to Marcus with both hands, but he shook his head:

- Just a little girl, I don't need a sword, one hand is enough.

The gladiators in the cellar cheered in unison:

- Marcus! Marcus! Our hero!

Marcus leisurely walked next to Valeria. Because he had his back turned to the gladiators, no one could see what he was doing, but in the next corner, I clearly saw him whispering in Valeria's ear. Valeria, who was praying, suddenly looked up, her eyes turned to where I was standing, her mouth moving as if to say something amid the cheers of the gladiators resounding in the cellar. Marcus leaned closer to the headset and nodded. He raised his big hand and squeezed hard on the girl's slim neck. Valeria let out a sob, her throat broke, she looked at me one last time and then collapsed. Marcus stood still and waited until she was no longer breathing before ordering the gladiator standing nearby:

- Bring it out for the crows and kites to eat.

After speaking, he raised his hand, a sign of victory for the gladiators when completing their task. Cheers rang out. Marcus leisurely walked out of the tunnel, patting the shoulders of the gladiators standing around as if nothing had happened. I unconsciously followed him, my whole body no longer felt, my consciousness became vague. It happened so fast and so horribly that I was completely paralyzed.

When we reached the main street, Marcus leaned into my ear and whispered:

- I couldn't bear to see her die in pain so I had to act first.

I nodded to show I understood and squeezed his hand in gratitude. Marcus continued:

- I let her know that she braved all dangers to come see her. Before she died, she texted me that she hoped she would be free to go here and there as she wanted.

Valeria's death was a major event in my uneventful life over the years. Her unwavering faith and the words In places full of hatred, Father, please let me sow the seeds of love awakened something that had always been hidden in me. I feel like I've heard someone talk about this kind of love before. Growing up in a family that valued money and material things, in most situations, love was a concept I never heard or talked about, but Valeria's words had a strangely transformative power, my still-dreaming soul seemed to have been awakened. As if someone carried a torch into a dark room and made the darkness disappear, I felt like I was no longer the innocent young man I used to be. I began to reflect on my life's purpose, a purpose that is not determined by my family but must be found and grasped by myself.

Many months have passed quietly since the day Valeria left the world. One day, my uncle gathered everyone in the house, saying it was to announce the good news. He excitedly told my father:

- I just negotiated with Beria about transporting goods by sea. Very surprisingly, he was also willing to cooperate with us on the land route through Asia. Even more surprising was that he also offered to let Sirius follow him to learn.

I quietly received the information, not reacting, but an emotion mixed with sadness gently flowed through me. I know Beria did that because she wanted to fulfill Valeria's wish. My mother was very surprised, she immediately said:

- Why Sirius? This job should be left to Lucius, right?

My uncle explained:

- I offered to let Lucius go with me, but Beria said he only wanted Sirius to follow him through Asia.

My father pondered for a moment then slowly said:

- It's okay, this rare opportunity our family cannot miss. This time Sirius went first to find the way, next time it will be Lucius' turn. The important thing is that we have people exploring this path so that the future will develop through the East. Once we have mastered the way, there is no need for Beria anymore.

My uncle turned to me and advised:

- Sirius, remember to carefully consider all relationships with the officials in charge of the checkpoint, pay attention to what they ask for. We must seize this opportunity sooner or later.

I listened to my father and uncle's instructions but did not respond, just nodded silently. Thinking of Valeria and her last words, I knew this trip was my chance to have the freedom that Valeria and I both wanted. Maybe this is also the trip that helps me find the answer about the meaning of life. No matter what, I knew that I had to take this opportunity, the opportunity that Valeria, a simple but loving girl, gave me as a final gift.

***

Roman was a vast empire stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to Asia Minor, including nearly half of Europe, parts of Africa and Asia. The battle-hardened Roman army conquered surrounding countries, establishing a system of governance that lasted nearly five centuries. Over time, the Roman Empire collapsed because of the wasteful spending and debauchery of the kings as well as the corruption of local rulers. Later historians also determined that the fall of Rome came from within, from within the people, within morality, within the bureaucracy, from commercial failure and endless class struggle. The national treasury was in deficit, there was no longer enough budget to pay soldiers' salaries, some elements of the military force turned to bandits, causing Roman society to become unstable and lacking security. When the royal court could not control the situation, local rulers took action to appropriate land and property from the people, then epidemics occurred continuously, society was in chaos, and national defense was no longer effective. Northern tribes came in to plunder and set fire to the Roman capital. After that, other tribes in North Africa also took the opportunity to raid everywhere. Although Emperor Constantine later built the Byzantine Empire, considered by historians to be the second Roman empire (also known as the Eastern Roman Empire), which lasted for a while longer, the glorious prosperity of Rome at that time was over.

The fall of the Roman Empire has been clearly recorded by historians, but Thomas especially emphasized two causes that are rarely talked about. The first reason is the wealth inequality between the upper class, including royal officials, and the majority of the people belonging to the common class or slaves. The upper class controls almost all resources as well as trade, they create a system of hidden power to sway the court, enacting laws that benefit them most. Roman commerce was also concentrated in the hands of a few dozen extremely wealthy families, with great influence on the emperors. They buy officials to sell their positions to get rich. The situation where a minority force took control and decided the fate of tens of millions of people living in misery and poverty brought the Roman Empire to destruction.

The second cause leading to this collapse is killing (killing karma). When invading surrounding countries to expand their empire, Roman kings killed many people, and this murder caused the empire to pay the consequences.

According to Thomas, all disasters that happen to any country are the consequences of previous causes. When the consequences happen, no one can avoid it. History has never recorded any lasting empire or dynasty. History is a lesson that helps people review past events to learn and gain experience for today. The current question is do the leaders who are ambitious to annex countries around the region to expand their influence and appropriate resources know anything about this lesson? Are they aware of the consequences that will happen to their country and its people? Is it true that ambition and passion for power have made their minds dull, so history continues to repeat old lessons? Anyway, if you create a cause, you will definitely reap the result, this is an undeniable truth. All those who contributed to the invasion, plunder, and killing will be born as victims of war in the future as retribution. Powerful empires will be devastated, broken into many small countries, and people will have to endure the common karma of living in hunger, cold, misery, and injustice. Most disasters are caused by killing karma. If you don't know how to change and get rid of greed and murder, it will be difficult to save future disasters.

Even though history has proven so, until now, few people are aware and believe in these lessons. Natural disasters are a lesson to correct human ignorance and blindness. If we pay attention, we can see that every time greed, anger, and violence increase, natural disasters occur more often than before. The place that never rained was hit by floods. The place where there is a lot of rain is suffering from drought. The hot desert has snow and the cold plateau has drought. Why is there such a strange phenomenon? Climate change is a warning sign that famine, food scarcity, water shortage and war to compete for these resources are about to happen. Then, perhaps a cataclysm or earthquake will split some large countries into many small pieces. All natural disasters originate from negative energies such as greed and anger arising from the human mind. Therefore, to avoid natural disasters, disease or war, people need to change from the heart. We must know how to turn our minds to goodness, avoid killing, and put aside anger and greed, only then can we expect peace. When the mind is peaceful, the world will be peaceful, when the mind is peaceful, the world will be peaceful.

PART FIVE

MAGIC SIGHTS AND TRUE CONCENTRATION

PAST LIFE POWERS

Shortly after Valeria's death, I began to follow Mr. Beria as he traveled with his caravan through many strange lands that had only been heard of before. I learned many new things, witnessed many strange things and opened my eyes. I visited Asian countries, even Valeria's hometown of Syria. Previously, I only knew about this place through Valeria's story, but now that I have arrived, I can truly clearly feel the strange peace and relaxation that Valeria once talked about. I felt like I was immersed in nature, integrated with the people here, and like Valeria, I also fell in love with this land.

After stopping in Syria for a while, I and Amir and Harahvi, two close subordinates of Beria, led the caravan to Bactria. This trip gave me the opportunity to meet an elder who helped me have a profound and meaningful experience about past lives and reincarnation. Memories and old habits flooded back layer after layer, awakening deep corners of my subconscious that were always anxious about the meaning of my life.

Bactria was Harahvi's hometown, so when we got there, Harahvi arranged for me and the trading group to stay in his house to wait for the weather to be favorable before leaving. After packing my things, Harahvi offered to show me around to familiarize myself with the situation. We visited many places, Harahvi enthusiastically introduced me to the scenery and people here. Late in the afternoon, we passed by an ashram, where I saw many monks practicing meditation. That scene attracted me so I stopped and stared for a long time. Seeing that, Harahvi happily said:

- Maybe you should try meditating too, it looks like that but it's very difficult!

As if there was some powerful attraction, I agreed immediately without any hesitation. Harahvi was surprised for a moment then followed me. We stayed at the ashram for the rest of the day.

The next day, on the way back, Harahvi said in a voice both curious and skeptical:

- Growing up in Bactria, I witnessed monks who had to practice for a period of time before they could enter concentration. He was a Roman who grew up in a place with no tradition of practice, but when he first came here, it was surprising that he could sit for more than a day.

I replied moderately:

- Actually, I don't know why I was able to enter concentration for so long.

What I did not share with Harahvi was the feeling of belonging I felt when entering the ashram. I'm not sure if my experience is unique, but since following Beria's footsteps here and there, sometimes, going to some strange place, even though it's the first time, I feel like I've been there before. When I left Syria for Bactria, this feeling was especially strong. On the way, I always felt familiar as if I had passed this road many times. In the vast desert, I still know oases with water and winding paths leading up to the plateau of Bactria. In my mind, it seems like something is starting to wake up. Until he stood in front of the ashram and saw the monks meditating, his old subconscious emerged strongly. In my mind, the name Timotheus suddenly appeared and the reminder echoed If I miss it, who knows when I will have the chance again? You must know how to let go.... Therefore, when I entered the ashram to participate in the meditation challenge, I felt like I was returning to my old habits. I sat cross-legged, followed my breathing, entered meditation and suddenly saw ancient images from my past life. Even though it was only fragmentary images, I still remembered my friend Timotheus who practiced with me, remembered having a secret love with a girl named Isidora, giving up his practice and finally dying unexpectedly at Pella.

After returning from the ashram, those flickering memories of my past life kept disturbing me, making me not feel at ease for a moment. I went to Harahvi and asked him about that ashram. Harahvi said the ashram has existed for a long time, he himself does not know the exact time, he only knows that it was built by Indian monks. For many years, the monastery has always been a spiritual refuge for the people of Bactria. As Bactrians, almost everyone has come to listen to lectures and experience practice at the ashram. Harahvi saw that I was in an uneasy mood, so he suggested:

- If you have such a chance, let's go back to the ashram to see what happens. You can meet the monks there to talk, maybe your heart will be resolved.

So Harahvi and I arranged to return to the ashram. As soon as I entered, I saw an old monk standing there as if waiting for us. He has clear blue eyes, a tall figure, a graceful posture, radiating an unusual feeling of relaxation. We walked in, he clasped his hands in greeting and invited us to sit down. A strange sense of familiarity came over me as we sat down, face to face. The monk looked at me intently and then slowly said:

- I'm very happy that you're back. But your problem, you can solve it yourself. The reason he is suffering is because he is attached to the past. If you know how to let go, no one can cause you trouble.

Harahvi and I looked at each other in surprise, because I hadn't spoken yet, but he had already voiced my concerns, knowing what I was here for. I carefully chose my words:

- Elder, how can you know my thoughts?

The monk smiled gently and leisurely explained:

- When you came here the other day, I was very surprised that a Roman who had no tradition of meditating like you could meditate for so long. I entered meditation to observe and saw that he was suffering because of an old incident. You should know that every suffering is a lesson that helps you understand better when you learn from the experience with a learning mindset.

Seeing my confused look, he slowly continued:

- However, what I am most concerned about is your unfinished practice. He has meditated very well, developing concentration that can help him go even further. When you have such true concentration, such things cannot cause trouble for you. When practicing meditation, sometimes unexpected images appear, which we call demon scenes. If the practitioner does not recognize or are not aware of these demonic scenes, they are often captivated by them. He had seen some images of the past. If he calmly let them appear and then disappear, it would be okay. However, in this life he had not practiced and his concentration was weak, so he focused his mind on that demonic scene and was unable to remove it. Everyone has moments of weakness, but when practicing meditation, the most important thing is to have self-control. You came here, proving that your base is still high, your opportunity for the path of practice is still there. I'm very happy.

I clasped my hands and nodded to the elder:

- I am still looking for my path in this life. Indeed, I believe that fate from my previous life brought me here. Maybe I used to practice and be diligent, but now those are all blurry memories that I only see fleetingly. I don't know what to do next. Please tell me more, Elder.

The monk's deep blue eyes stared at me, but it was not a judgmental look but filled with affection and affection. He said:

- He had the opportunity to practice. Although it was interrupted, the practice still remained, thanks to which he was able to enter concentration quickly and meditate for such a long time. If you want, you can still continue your practice path. But now his concentration is weak, his mind is not yet pure, so he does not recognize the demonic scene appearing in his mind. He has not yet mastered his mind, so he is attracted to those images, making him miserable. If you continue on the path of cultivation, you will gradually be able to conquer the demon realm, but you must be determined. Practicing meditation without a pure mind can easily lead you astray and lose all your efforts. You must know that only when the mind is pure will wisdom arise. If you have wisdom, no matter what happens, you will not be affected. If you practice meditation and your mind is distorted, even just a little, you will lose your right view and immediately fall into wrong views.

I was confused, was this monk referring to my feelings of resentment towards the people who caused my death? When I reminisce, even though the death in my previous life was just a fleeting image, I cannot help but feel pain and shock. The more pain I felt, the more I resented those who did evil things to me. As if seeing through my confused thoughts, the monk gently continued:

- You complain so you get angry, you get angry so you get more entangled. If you continue with this resentment, it will cause you to meet those people again. No one wants to meet someone they don't like, no one wants to meet someone who has treated them cruelly, but if you keep holding onto hatred, you will create more connections with that person. If we don't meet in this life, we will meet in another life. All those who have a grudge against each other will meet again to repay or collect debts. Cause and effect continues like that, it's impossible to end it. You must know, once the mind of anger arises, there will be hundreds, thousands of unwholesome seeds in the mind that will also arise, creating many obstacles. Therefore, you must practice developing compassion and tolerance towards everyone. No matter how cruel or evil they are, you must have compassion. They have their karma and will have to learn their own lessons. Their karma is none of your business, you have to let karma work. You have to know how to let go so you won't be entangled anymore. Even if you encounter things that don't go your way, don't blame others, blame yourself...

I spoke up:

- I understand the other things you said, but why do you have to blame yourself when you encounter things that don't go your way?

The monk gently explained:

- If you want to go far on the path, the first thing is to give up old things. Being attached to the past is like tying stones to your feet, so how can you take a step forward? If you want to let go of the past, you must know how to repay the loan. Ask yourself why things don't go your way? Is it because the causes created long ago have now come to fruition? You need to ask yourself why you are being treated so cruelly? Why were you born as a slave? Why do we love without being reciprocated and even be scolded and humiliated?

Obviously, such things may have been too heavy for you at the time, but if you look back to even older lives, perhaps you will know the root cause and no longer react like that. That's why I advise you not to blame others but yourself.

It seemed that this monk not only saw through my thoughts, but also knew my past clearly. Just as she was about to ask him a question, Harahvi spoke up:

- But how do we know what we did in previous lives? We don't have any memories.

The monk leisurely replied:

- The reason people cannot remember the things they have done in the past is because in thousands of lives people have created so many good and bad causes, it is impossible to know which causes are bearing fruit. That's why people have to go through many lives, many lifetimes, to learn, because each lesson is an opportunity to help them change gradually, but no one can learn everything in just one lifetime.

Harahvi asked:
