- But at least we have to know what we did to change it, right?

The elder replied:

- Remembering things in past lives is not necessarily as useful as you think. Suppose you knew that your wife and children in this life were the people you killed in the past, how would you feel? Or if you eat meat, and the animal that was killed was your parent in your previous life, what will happen to you? If you understand cause and effect, you will see that life is really just about repaying loans and repaying loans. Because of ignorance, people keep causing causes and then repaying the results, borrowing and then repaying debts, wandering around from life to life, immersed in the cycle of reincarnation with no way to escape. That's why people who understand cause and effect try to practice, keep a good heart, keep a pure mind, hoping to pay off all their debts soon so they can escape samsara. However, the interconnected cause and effect is not easy to escape. To escape samsara, everyone needs a place of refuge and guidance from those who have gone before.

If you want to go far on the path, the first thing is to give up old things. Being attached to the past is like tying stones to your feet, so how can you take a step forward?

Harahvi continued to ask:

- But who can do that?

The monk slowly explained:

- As a merchant traveling on the natural road, he needed a guide who knew the terrain well to guide the trading group on the right path and choose a convenient route. Likewise, on the spiritual path, practitioners need the guidance of those who have gone through that path, overcome challenges, and are willing to share their understanding and help those who follow. Thanks to this guidance, they can clearly know the path and prepare to deal with challenges. Therefore, once you have determined the path of practice, you must have teachers who have experienced the states of mind to guide you so you can go far.

He turned to me and said kindly:

- In the past, he practiced meditation but still lacked learning, like someone who abandons the roots and grabs the branches. A tree without roots cannot grow no matter how much you water it. The same goes for practitioners, they must have clear goals, and if they learn, they must practice to be successful. People who study but don't practice can only talk but can't do anything. Your case is different, you only have practice but lack study so you don't know what happens in your mind. When practicing meditation, even a small evil thought or a secret wish can attract extremely subtle demons that few people can perceive. Therefore, the most important thing for meditators is to keep their mind pure.

Harahvi wondered:

- But what did my friend do?

The monk looked at me and said slowly:

- In his previous life, he had the opportunity to practice, but before he could get there, he abandoned it because he followed his secret desires. Even though I was able to enter concentration, my mind was not yet pure and was still entangled in the emotions of men and women, so I lost mindfulness. Although he was able to keep his mind from wandering thoughts and eliminate gross delusions, when he went deeper into concentration, he encountered subtle delusions or strange images. Most of these images belong to warm colors. Because of his lack of learning background, he was not aware of this type of demonic realm, so he was attracted to it. Demonic scenes are images, emotions or realms that appear from within your mind like a dream, but you believe they are real. The reason is because his mind is not pure, for many lives, he has killed, lusted, and practiced evil dharma. If you want to change, you must rely on the Dharma, know how to repent, and gradually improve, then you can hope to eliminate these bad causes.

Is it possible that in the distant past, I can't remember that I did such terrible things, things that make me shudder just imagining them now? But if that's not true, then why did I experience a life of slavery, have been imprisoned, humiliated and hurt, and then died suddenly? This monk's explanations made the suffering I had endured seem lighter. I looked at him attentively and in the gentleness of those deep blue eyes, I felt a strange familiarity. Is it possible that he is also a fate from a previous life? Thinking about that, flickering memories of his friend Timotheus in his previous life appeared before his eyes. As if reading the confusing thoughts in my head, the monk looked at me and smiled, then slowly continued:

- People who want to practice meditation must first follow some disciplines, or precepts, to keep their mind pure. There are four things that our master taught very carefully that any Zen practitioner must follow: don't kill, don't steal, don't lust and don't lie, which are four karma: killing, morality, lust, and delusion. Among these things, keeping the mind free from lust is the most difficult thing.

When entering concentration, although he had eliminated his crude delusions, he still thought about women, so he stimulated the seeds deep in his mind to activate. Seeing images of ancient people appearing, feelings of love and lust arise in the mind. It is an emotional demon scene. When he saw images of the past, he thought he remembered his past life. From then on, he wanted to know more about his past life, so he followed this delusion and was transformed by the demon world. People lacking wisdom, when they see these demonic scenes, will think that they have the ability to gain access to their lives, that is, to understand their past lives, and then become complacent. But if the mind is not pure, how can one have magical powers? That's just a ghost scene that emotions draw. In short, he was influenced by all kinds of demonic minds but remained carefree and unaware. People who do not practice, when their lustful mind is not satisfied, often give rise to thoughts of resentment, which then lead to many more bad things. If not adjusted, these wrong views will easily be drawn into evil. When you deviate from this path, resentment and resentment will ebb and flow, life after life, you will continue to collect debts, repay debts, make enemies of each other, and will forever fall into evil places.

He leisurely emphasized each word:

- You should know, true Zen practitioners are not disturbed no matter what image they see, no matter what sound they hear, no thoughts arise. They are completely in control, as if they are motionless, not being influenced by anything outside. That's called being diligent.

I sat there listening passionately, like someone in the dark suddenly seeing the light, the question about the purpose of my life may have found an answer. I knelt down and sincerely:

- Elder, please open your heart and teach me so I can continue on my unfinished path.

The monk smiled gently:

- We already have a destiny, I will teach you. I hope this time you will go all the way and not give up halfway. However, he had to start again from the beginning. You must first learn the basic precepts to transform your mind, then learn to analyze the states of your mind to avoid unfortunate events.

After that day, I stayed at the ashram with this monk to learn the basics of precepts and concentrated on practicing meditation with the monks here. Thanks to that, I have learned more about practice methods that I did not pay attention to before. On the first day of starting practice under the guidance of the monk, he carefully advised:

- Before practicing meditation, you must prepare both your mind and body to support your practice. The first thing you need to do is to eliminate the causes that help false thoughts arise. That is to avoid killing, do not eat meat, fish and stimulating spices such as onions, chives, garlic, or other things that have a fishy smell. These are things that can stimulate physiological abilities and increase delusions of desire. Therefore, the people who practice here are vegetarian and only eat frugally. If you don't know how to eliminate the seeds of lust right from the beginning, when practicing meditation, lustful thoughts will arise, it will be difficult to control your body, then you will break the precepts and get lost in the devil's path. Eating meat can easily give rise to anger. If you do not control your anger, even if you enter concentration, you will not be able to have wisdom. Without wisdom, the mind is dull and cannot distinguish between right and wrong. When something goes wrong, anger arises, obscures reason, easily makes mistakes and gets involved in bad things.

To have solid preparation, you must follow the precepts to eliminate subtle delusions, deep in your mind. All desires from food to sex originate from consciousness, so you must avoid thinking about those things. Eating is just to nourish the body, not to enjoy it. Therefore, you should only eat enough, not too much. Eating too much creates greed, which then leads to other bad things. You should also not drink alcohol or any stimulants because it will affect your mind, making it difficult to control your mind and giving rise to other desires. Every day before going to sleep, you must check yourself to see if you sowed any bad deeds that day? Causes here are actions, words or thoughts that are not in accordance with the precepts. An evil thought is also a cause planted in the mind, waiting for an opportunity to arise when you lose mindfulness. If you keep the precepts strictly, you will avoid tempting outside influences and will turn your mind inward, only then will your practice progress.

From there, under the guidance of this monk, I began to learn and practice meditation step by step. When spring came, the snow melted and the weather became warmer, the traffic routes were expanded, but I decided not to follow the trade group anymore but would continue to stay in Bactria to practice. Amir and Harahvi led the trade caravan to China and then returned to Syria.

The following year, Amir returned to Bactria, bringing Beria's letter to me. Amir said that when he learned that I had decided to live in the ashram in Bactria, Beria was extremely surprised and touched. He told Amir that Valeria had chosen an ideal path, now perhaps I had found my own ideal path and he was very happy about that. He knew that Valeria would be pleased. The difficult thing was that he didn't know what to say to my parents. Beria also guessed that if my father knew that I stayed in Bactria to practice, he would never leave it alone. After discussing with Amir, Beria decided to inform my father that I had fallen ill and died along the way. After that my father wanted Lucius to take my place in Beria's caravan, but he refused, saying he didn't want to be responsible for such a thing anymore. From then on, the two families became discordant.

Beria's heart and thoughts for me touched me very much. While away from home, although I sometimes missed my family, I had determined the path to take, and all feelings of nostalgia and sadness were suppressed. Now that I know that my family has accepted that I will not return, my heart is more at peace.

I found a quiet place and opened Beria's letter to read. The letter is long, each stroke is precise and neat, just like Beria's personality that I still remember.

Sirius, I hope you are well.

Even though you and my son are not officially married, through Valeria's advice, I consider you my son-in-law. I don't know what your life is like right now, but I'm sure that your choices, like Valeria's in the past, are the right choices and have special meaning.

Most of us as parents only know how to worry about making sure our children have a good, happy and prosperous life. Not many people know how to help our children choose a meaningful life. Since Valeria's death, I have thought about this issue a lot. Why did she choose a life different from what I had prepared for her? Why didn't it choose an easier life but chose a different and harsh lifestyle like that? Who taught her to do those things? Who gave it such solid faith?

Before something happened to my son, he gave all the assets that I had reserved for him and divided them all among the poor slaves. Until the last moment of his life, he still tried to find a way to help him find a way out of living in a family that only knew about money, always planning to take advantage of others. These actions of hers surprised me greatly. I also did not expect that a gentle, innocent person, always obedient to his parents like you, would dare to risk his life to go to the arena to meet my daughter at the last moment of her life. Who made an innocent child who was pampered since childhood become such a courageous girl, who gave her the strength to defy death and nurture such absolute faith in the divine?

I have lived more than half of my life, only now awakened when I witnessed these things. We realize that in this life, spiritual transformation is extremely important. If you don't find the true meaning of life and are still as confused as before, it's not worth living at all. For that reason, I chose to stay in Syria to interact with my daughter's friends, to learn more about the things she once believed. Thanks to that, we know that anyone can transform their life if they open their hearts to receive spiritual blessings. From then on, we learned to rise from the bad to the noble, from selfishness to altruism.

Once upon a time, I was the governor ruling over a desolate border region like Syria, but I was always concerned about the situation of Rome before the threat of invasion by the Northern Visigoth tribes. We see that today's society is increasingly disturbed by the insensitivity and depravity of the royal court. Rome is like an unmanned ship floating at sea. When faced with a storm, you don't know what will happen. I have met and contacted people like me, trying to find a solution but to no avail, that's why I gave up my position and switched to business to no longer worry about those things. My daughter's death changed everything.

I believe that no solution can save Rome, but only spiritual revival can rebuild society, train elite citizens and people worthy of leading Rome. Therefore, I am preparing to do this and hope that you can return in the future to help me restore Rome.

Later, back and forth with Amir and Harahvi, I learned that Baria asked for baptism after a period of learning about Christianity, and he also became a leader of this group. Under his direction, this group of people gradually became a very strong force in Syria, and was no longer threatened or banned like before.

***

The conversation with Thomas about life in Rome was interrupted a few times because Thomas was quite emotional. Although life in Rome did not have too many events or dramatic stories, it was a life that left many regrets as well as lessons for Thomas. When talking about the period of practice with the monk at the Bactria monastery, he stopped to share his thoughts with me:

- As you probably know, the bad karma we have sown in past lives is endless and extremely heavy, it is impossible to pay it off in just a few lives. Everyone has times when they doubt, hesitate or are tempted by bad habits and habits, so only those who are truly determined to practice have enough strength to overcome these obstacles. This is a very difficult battle, taking place internally, that few people can overcome easily. During my life in Rome, although I had learned a few things, there were still many other things that needed to be learned. There were still many things that I learned but did not understand, so I had to re-learn them.

I asked in surprise:

- But didn't you stay in Bactria to continue your practice?

Thomas shook his head:

- As I said, in that life, I was a gentle but weak person, with a lot of inferiority complex, so I could not follow the strict discipline of the monastery. At that time, my mind was still dull and lacking determination, so I could not comprehend the noble truths that that monk taught.

Speaking of the monk, I couldn't help but wonder:

- Is that monk Timotheus? He had said that Timotheus also had blue eyes, and didn't the monk remind him of his old friend?

Thomas smiled:

- When I was Sirius, I only had the same suspicion, but now I can look back at my past life more clearly, I believe that indeed that monk was Timotheus. That friend of mine in the past always persevered on the path of practice, so he progressed very far and became a noble person. Perhaps because we have been destined for many lifetimes, I was able to meet him again and follow his instructions. However, during the time Sirius was in Bactria, the monk never talked about himself or his past relationships but only focused on guiding and encouraging me to practice. Even though at that time I knew how to turn inside to practice meditation, I was still not sure whether I could complete the practice as expected. The monk knew that so he advised me that instead of having a negative attitude that I am weak, not strong enough or lacking intelligence, I should rely on the blessings and protective powers that always help those on this path. According to the monk, blessing is an energy originating from within on the level of consciousness that can give practitioners unexpected strength. It is like an invisible hand leading practitioners on a dark, dangerous path. It is the silent voice of the inner mind in the vastness of heaven and earth, a bright ray of hope in the dark night. Blessing is a mysterious energy that comes from a sacred, wise source of energy within and if you believe in this source of energy, anything can be accomplished. I use the word energy to make it easier to understand and consistent with modern science, but in fact it is something invisible, indescribable or identifiable. Hinduism calls that source of energy the true self, Buddhism calls it Buddha nature, and Christianity calls it God. Many people still mistakenly think that blessings are an external source of energy, but in fact, it is inherent within us. Buddhism believes that every living being has Buddha nature, Christianity believes that God resides in our hearts. It is not an empty idea but a clearly defined truth for those with sincere beliefs. However, because science cannot prove the existence of this internal energy source, many people still do not believe it. That's understandable. Although blessings act very gently and slowly, the impact is extremely profound and mysterious, and it only comes when needed, not just by praying. For example, when people fight with desire, in the most desperate, difficult, and painful times, blessings will appear. Blessings come to us in many forms, sometimes as a mysterious light that flashes and then disappears, but in that magical and glorious moment, people receive a strong energy to help them overcome suffering. Sometimes blessings appear as a reminder in the ear, giving people hope to believe and be more confident in their path. Receiving a blessing is a sacred moment that can change a person's life because when receiving a blessing, their consciousness is raised to a higher level, so that they can perceive the truth of things. However, that excitement and progress is not easy to maintain. Many people whose karma is too heavy will easily fall into old habits, dragging them down to a lower level. Sirius is such a case. At that time, I had lived in Bactria for more than ten years and my practice had progressed a lot. Then that monk passed away and I had no support, so even though I was still practicing at the ashram, I gradually lost my spirit and was no longer as enthusiastic as before. It is the consequence of years of growing up in a family full of criticism, comparison and scolding. I have grown up to be a weak person. Valeria changed my life. Her strong faith has helped me be more courageous and choose a meaningful, goal-oriented life for myself. Faith is also the most important lesson in my life. But in the end, I'm still a weak and easily swayed Sirius. Therefore, when I received news that Rome was invaded, houses were burned down, and the port of Ostia was destroyed, my heart began to be disturbed. I stood still until I received news from Amir, informing me that my parents had been killed, my younger brother had been enslaved, and that Beria had commanded an armed force of Christians who had merged with Constantine's army and were moving to liberate Rome. Then I could no longer calm down. I left the ashram and returned to find Beria to help him according to his request many years ago.

I was surprised:

- So your practice was interrupted again?

Thomas nodded:

- That's right. Because I didn't have enough intelligence, I couldn't continue steadily on my path, I followed other urges. Being a weak person with an inferiority complex, at that time I wanted to become a hero and I had to pay the price for that foolishness. In life, there are so many people who have missed good opportunities because of such lack of insight... In the end, Sirius died in the war, ending his life in loneliness and regret. No heroes, no glory.

Because of this unfinished business and regret, according to Thomas, he returned to continue his lessons. And that lesson fell during a period of turmoil in Europe due to religious wars...

Blessing is an energy originating from within on the level of consciousness that can give practitioners unexpected strength. It is like an invisible hand leading practitioners on a dark, dangerous path. It is the silent voice of the inner mind in the vastness of heaven and earth, a bright ray of hope in the dark night. Blessing is a mysterious energy that comes from a sacred, wise source of energy within and if you believe in this source of energy, anything can be accomplished.

tieu_de: Part Six: The Light of Meditation - The Path to Wisdom
noi_dung:
PART SIX

THE LIGHT OF MEDITATION

THE PATH TO WISDOM

Colorado, present.

After a few weeks of tiring work, my wife and I went to Colorado to rest for a few days, ready to visit Mr. Kris. This trip includes Andrew and Connie. After meeting Mr. Kris before, Connie changed a lot, her personality became more gentle and calm. She practices meditation diligently and also has many questions about meditation, so when she heard we were preparing to go to Colorado, she immediately offered to come with us to visit Mr. Kris.

It was already late afternoon when we arrived in Colorado, but because Connie was so impatient, and we hadn't seen Mr. Kris for a long time, everyone agreed to go straight to his house. Mr. Kris waited at the door, welcoming us warmly. We went inside, naturally as if we were back in the old place, each of us found a comfortable seat and asked about each other's situation. Connie quickly asked Mr. Kris to teach him about meditation:

- After listening to his instructions last time, I also began to learn and start practicing meditation, but it was not easy. I could only sit for a while before countless confusing thoughts began to come to me, and soon I felt depressed. Can you tell me how I should start practicing meditation to be effective?

Mr. Kris listened and then leisurely said:

- Many people do not have the habit of turning inward to observe their inner self, so it is difficult to meditate. Because their nature is chaotic, they cannot sit still. Even if you sit, your mind is still busy thinking about the outside world and then quickly gets bored and stops practicing. In the past, when guiding meditation practice, Zen masters taught very carefully about the preparatory steps. However, in the West, most meditation teachers skip this preparation step. She is a very active person and busy thinking about all kinds of things, so she needs to create a good habit to calm her mind before starting to meditate. A simple but effective method is to enjoy art, or you can also immerse yourself in natural scenery. These habits will gradually affect your inner self, helping your mind become less disturbed.

She can admire landscape paintings by famous artists, read poems praising nature or enjoy the sound of classical concertos to find noble inspiration. Every day, you should spend time early in the morning walking in the park, listening to the birds singing and the wind blowing to evoke in you noble vibrations instead of the noisy and bustling feelings of life. These activities can leave a pure aftertaste in her, helping her change her chaotic daily habits.

Andrew laughed:

- Have you heard, from now on, don't listen to loud music that sways and dances anymore, your favorite rap songs are okay too.

Connie glared at her husband and continued:

- Does that mean I should only listen to classical music?

Mr. Kris smiled and shook his head:

- Not necessarily so. There are many talented artists today and their works are very valuable. In my opinion, in this day and age, artists with noble vibrating souls can replace the role of priests when they reflect the beautiful state of the sacred universe into their works, making viewers open their souls to tune into that wonderful feeling. True art is symbols that can lead us back to the spiritual fire that exists in each person's soul. When musicians apply their artistic fingers to the instrument, they turn it into a magic wand that can change the noisy, bustling scene into a bright dawn, filling the listener with magical images as if being transported to a fairyland. Those emotions will penetrate the listener's soul, helping to reduce those rough, chaotic thoughts.

Mr. Kris turned around and said to all of us:

- Today we all live in a world of turmoil and haste due to the mechanical activities of technology. It attracts us like a fierce hurricane, pulling everything under its control. Therefore, most people yearn to find some peace to have enough strength to cope with these difficulties. However, in a storm, even though the sea surface may vibrate, the sea bottom is always quiet. Our soul is the same, deep inside it is completely quiet and this is the center of humanity, because its nature is peace and clarity. One of the ways to bring us back to this pure self-nature is meditation.

Currently, meditation has been widely popularized everywhere, but unfortunately it has been commercialized, corrupted and become a movement rather than a method of practice. Many Westerners are curious and curious, just wanting to try it out and not understanding the true purpose of meditation. In addition, some people have taught meditation in a wrong way, adding a little Yoga postures, a little Qigong, a little Tai Chi movements, and then giving it very catchy names like meditation for success, meditation to find love, meditation for healing in order to attract the masses. For those who really understand meditation, this is a farce, but for some people who only come to meditation out of curiosity, this is something that can help them achieve what they want.

Mr. Kris smiled and turned to me and said:

- You are someone who works in the commercial market, you probably realize that today meditation or mindfulness has become a brand worth billions of dollars. Currently, in the United States there are more than a thousand meditation centers and in the world the number has reached more than three thousand. A large number of these centers have nothing to do with religion, but exist independently as commercial establishments. This number is increasing day by day, so people claiming to be meditation masters are making a lot of money.

I nodded, not surprised by what Mr. Kris said. When researching the market, there was a time when I was overwhelmed by the number of commercial investments in meditation schools by these Zen Professional (Zen Professional).

Mr. Kris continued:

- Currently in the West, most people who teach meditation are not Zen masters, nor are they related to religion. Some are fitness or yoga instructors and add meditation courses to their exercise programs to attract customers. Others self-study through books, attend a few meditation courses, and then confer themselves a certain title to recruit students for the purpose of making money. Many people with skillful speaking skills can attract many students, develop into companies with branches everywhere and earn huge profits. What is worrying is that this baseless teaching can cause harm, not only to the body but also to the mind of the student. Meditation is not just sitting still to relax as many people misunderstand. Meditation is a science of the mind that requires commitment to practice seriously and properly. Meditation is not for entertainment, to show off, or to follow trends, but for it to become a part of life with a clear purpose. There are some basic principles you need to understand in order to commit to the practice. When you practice with this understanding, you will find meditation very simple; otherwise, you will soon feel lost and give up sooner or later.

Connie looked confused:

- So how do you think I should practice meditation?

Mr. Kris replied slowly:

- Meditation must be natural, with a clear purpose. Her life cannot go in two opposing directions. She cannot have an active and bustling life at the same time as her spiritual practices. Meditation is breaking down duality to return to the self (Inherent nature). If there is duality, there cannot be meditation.

So, when is the best time to practice meditation? It was early morning, before sunrise. At that time, the space is quiet, a time to concentrate a lot of positive energy, suitable for practice. After waking up from a long sleep, you should do a few warm-up exercises for about ten minutes to refresh your body before starting to practice. If you practice meditation in the afternoon or evening, you need to set aside a certain amount of time to rest for your body to stabilize and relax, because you are tired from a day of work. The main point is that you must learn to rest comfortably and reduce physical tension before starting. You need to practice breathing lightly and slowly, don't do anything too hard. All meditation methods begin by bringing the body to its natural state. This is important because improper breathing can be dangerous. You should know that breath is a regenerative energy of life because when circulating in the body, it contains powers that can heal many internal organs.

Connie wondered:

- I have read some books on meditation, instructing you to breathe according to the diagram into the chakras...

Mr. Kris interrupted Connie:

- I want to warn you that you should never practice any unnatural breathing method. Taking deep breaths and then pouring the breath into any organ in the body to stimulate the chakras is a practice of pagan voodoo magicians. This can cause the practitioner to lose control, causing the nerves to become disordered and unable to control themselves. The method of focusing vision on a point on the forehead, to paralyze the mind, is a way to call invisible forces to enter, then follow them out of the body, flying into another place or realm. That is something she must absolutely avoid because the consequences of these things are extremely harmful, not only in this life but also in future lives.

Mr. Kris emphasized:

- Meditation is a practice method to master the mind, not to gain some power. Being an active person, her mind often wanders, and she follows it. The purpose of meditation is to reverse this, to train your mind to slow down. There are many methods to do this such as following the breath, paying attention to the subject, the koan to keep the mind from wandering.

Connie asked:

- I read through the literature on meditation and saw a lot of koans mentioned, but I don't understand what it is. Can you explain a little?

Mr. Kris slowly:

- In the simplest terms, a koan is a Zen story, a Zen problem. The words and deeds of high-ranking monks through the ages were recorded to serve as a guideline for Zen practitioners. Over time, they became a type of object for consideration, called a koan. When a meditator chooses or is assigned a koan, he uses that koan as an object of consideration while meditating, called studying the koan. Studying a koan is not for the purpose of finding a solution, the role of a koan is to give the meditator an object to contemplate, to focus his or her attention on in order to maintain mindfulness.

You can choose a koan, a mantra, a Buddha statue or an image of a Mandala, the cosmic circle, to focus your mind on. It is important that you choose carefully because once you have chosen, you cannot change it. If you change it, it will lose its original value, then you keep changing one thing after another and it will be difficult to progress.

The first step of practice is always difficult because her level of mental control is still weak. As soon as she concentrated on a koan, other thoughts rushed in from somewhere, opposing the peace she wanted to find. Controlling the mind and not letting it run wild is one of the most difficult problems any beginner faces. If you feel discouraged, uncomfortable, or don't want to practice anymore, remember that the mind that created those difficulties is the same mind that will help you solve everything. Once you stop chasing unrealistic thoughts, you will see those thoughts come and go naturally.

Connie wondered:

- But how long do I have to practice to get to that stage?

Mr. Kris smiled and said:

- You shouldn't put too much emphasis on that. When you first practice, don't do anything too strenuous, just do short training sessions. Sitting for a long time will only make her more tired and won't help. She only needs to practice for about fifteen to twenty minutes. The important thing is to practice regularly every day, at a fixed time so that practicing becomes a habit. One thing you shouldn't do is use your will to prevent messy thoughts from happening. You will find that the more you try to resist, the stronger those thoughts will become, and thus you will be drawn in by them. The opposing attitude only makes her stressed and angry because she has to fight against her previous habits. Instead, practice observing thoughts as they occur. When a thought arises, don't react, don't judge, don't resist, wait patiently, because when it comes, it will go. Consider thoughts like tidal waves, they drift layer by layer to the shore and then quietly sink. By doing that, she can resolve almost any dispute.

The important thing when practicing meditation is to never give up because of boredom. When seeing that their practice seems ineffective and progressing, many people complain that it is too difficult and are tempted to give up.

In fact, meditation is a natural act of nature, anyone can reach the state of concentration (samadhi). The problem is that when someone is impatient, always wishing to achieve something quickly, they will lose the necessary peace. Practicing meditation is also about changing your habits to let your noisy mind control you. She's been doing this for so many years, how can she reverse it in just a few months? If you believe in Reincarnation then you need to understand that this habit has been there for a long time, not only in this life but also in many previous lives. But every effort she made, however slow, contributed to her ultimate success, the state of tranquility. Her mind will gradually begin to focus, stay on a concept and she will have concentration.

Connie wondered:

- There are many books written about concentration, some say it is a feeling of joy and happiness, some say it is a feeling of escape...

Mr. Kris laughed and interrupted Connie:

- Those are just the fancy words of writers to describe something they don't know clearly. Concentration means harmony between the thinker and the thing being contemplated, between subject and object no longer distinguishable. Simply put, it is complete concentration. In the state of concentration, the practitioner finds himself lucid, not because of external circumstances, but because his mind can see clearly and understand everything. At a higher level, the practitioner's mind will be completely quiet, without any more thoughts, until even the object of contemplation is no longer there. That is the light energy of truly wise understanding or wisdom (wisdom). This peace and clarity is concentration.

Connie asked:

- How can they know everything?

Mr. Kris explained:

- Our understanding is different from the clear, comprehensive understanding of someone who has reached the state of concentration. The understanding of these people has two aspects: a thorough understanding of an object and a general understanding. In other words, the former is vertical understanding and the latter is horizontal understanding. Let's take for example a glass of water. For us, it's just liquid to quench our thirst. To scientists, it is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms. For Zen masters, water represents the state of mind. Each person's understanding ability is different depending on their level. Our abilities also depend on our education, environment and daily experiences. For those who have achieved concentration, their understanding is extremely profound, it goes through every layer of life to enter the essence of things as well as their relationships with other things. It is a deep understanding, beyond the limits of reason, scientific knowledge, philosophy and religion.

Meditation is a practice method to master the mind, not to gain some power. The important thing when practicing meditation is to never give up because of boredom. When seeing that their practice seems ineffective and progressing, many people complain that it is too difficult and are tempted to give up. Actually, meditation is a natural act of nature, anyone can reach the state of concentration ( samadhi). The problem is that when someone is impatient, always wishing to achieve something quickly, they will lose the necessary peace. Practicing meditation is also about changing your habits to let your noisy mind control you.

Connie wondered:

- I don't quite understand horizontal understanding, please explain more...

Mr. Kris leisurely explained:

- Horizontal understanding is the understanding of all things as well as their relationships with other things. This is comprehensive and clear understanding. In the past, Plato said: Life is limited, understanding is infinite. Socrates also taught: What we know best is that we know nothing. So how can this understanding be explained? For everyone, comprehensive understanding is just an illusion, unattainable. However, we need to understand that the human mind today is very limited because it has been guided and taught to collect, to adhere to, and to limit by the education system that has existed for thousands of years. It's not easy to break that framework. In fact, our minds have great potential but not many people know how to exploit it. And meditation is the way to help us destroy habits and habits, free our minds from conventional constraints, and help us expand our horizons and reach places that few people have observed.

Connie looked confused:

- I still don't understand how people who have a plan are different from ordinary people?

Mr. Kris patiently explained:

- The thoughts of most people are cumulative, because knowledge is gathered gradually over time. For example, when going to school, students must learn from the basics, learn to read, learn to write, then write, reason, learn from basic knowledge and then professional knowledge. This knowledge is accumulated and will develop the ability to understand, thanks to which people can express complex thoughts. However, this understanding is just water in a small pond, it cannot be compared to the boundless, clear understanding like water in the ocean of someone who has attained samadhi. Furthermore, our thoughts are also influenced by desire, so all thoughts are often subjective or according to desire. The human mind is always confused between desire and reason, these two are often in conflict, causing the mind to be torn between two extremes. Desire induces us to do what we like, while reason advises us to avoid bad things. Pulled between two extremes, the human mind is like a battlefield, constantly fighting like water and fire. For some people, when desire arises, reason escapes. For others, when reason is active, desire is silent. Because these two motivations are never present at the same time, the human mind is rarely balanced. For people with concentration, it is different, because they have transformed desire into love and reason into wisdom, so both combine closely and appear at the same time in wonderful balance, creating an extremely profound and lucid understanding.

Connie hesitantly suggested:

- Please explain more clearly, because I'm still confused between these nouns.

Mr. Kris explained further:

- People act using their senses to collect data and then bring it into the brain for processing. The intelligent or rational mind will analyze these facts to come up with an action or solution. However, it does not raise the issue of whether the collected data is complete and accurate or not. It decides on its own based on its own logic, what we call intelligence. Most people rely on reason to set standards for judging right and wrong, right and wrong. For people who have concentration, this is not perfect, because just relying on data collected by the senses is not accurate enough. This common sense does not include a comprehensive insight to understand the facts or the relationship between events and give an overall view. People who have concentration do not use intelligence to differentiate but use another type of wisdom called Prajna Wisdom. Therefore, their decisions no longer have judgment or discrimination.

Connie asked impatiently:

- If I practice diligently like you said, how long will it take to reach that state?

Mr. Kris shook his head and smiled:

- Like I said, this is something you shouldn't worry about. You cannot practice meditation with the expectation of achieving certain results. Perhaps because she has worked for many years, she is used to enjoying the results of her work. However, practicing meditation only aiming for results is completely counterproductive. Instead, you should direct your energy into enjoying the process of practice, like a leisurely, relaxed person, leisurely walking on the road, keeping your mind calm, not knowing when you will arrive at your destination. I advise you to set limits on daily activities. She needs to know what she can do and what she shouldn't do, because these activities can interfere with her retreat, causing her to become distracted. She needs to ask herself whether what she usually does is consistent with her practice goals.

Andrew laughed and immediately said to his wife:

- Well, from now on I no longer have Facebook, Instagram, TikTok or YouTube.

Mr. Kris gently advised:

- I know that letting go of habits is not easy, and you should also avoid sudden changes. Once she has decided to practice meditation, she should seek to stay away from activities that she knows are not in harmony with her goals. But if you change immediately, within a short time you will feel depressed and frustrated. Everything must be done slowly, forming a new habit, gradually replacing the old for a long-term sustainable approach. If you want to change unnecessary habits, you need to replace them with other habits such as studying scriptures. A huge mistake of Zen practitioners today is that they often ignore studying and pondering the Buddha's teachings. Some extravagant young people have abused the phrase no writing, no external teachings to go straight to meditation without studying the scriptures. They do not understand the true purpose of meditation. They only practice vaguely for a short time and then find everything boring and boring. Studying and meditating on the scriptures will give you a clear and precise idea of ​​the purpose of meditation. Thanks to that, you will feel confident when practicing. If you don't know where you are going, what you are doing, and for what purpose, everything is meaningless, just like a person entering the desert without a map or compass.

Mr. Kris returned to explain more to all of us:

- Recently I have read a number of books on meditation by several authors who claim to be experts in this field. Maybe they are intelligent scholars, and in their enthusiasm, they write instructions based on book research and have no practice experience. Most of them skip the basics and go straight to practice. Therefore, they cannot speak clearly about the deep activities of the mind and only use strange nouns that confuse and confuse the reader. Reading such books did not get her anywhere but only made her more lost. If you want to practice meditation, you should have a guide, not just learn from books, and that guide must be a meditation master with many years of practice. The popular retreats that are heavily advertised today are mostly only superficial. You can observe the instructors, if they only teach how to sit, how to breathe or a few postures without explaining the basics and purpose, it proves that they are not truly diligent people, taking those classes is just a waste of money in vain.

Connie wondered:

- But my meditation teacher quoted the Buddha, the Buddha himself said that there is no need for scriptures or texts, because meditation is independent of these things. Just now you mentioned no writing, separate teachings from outside, that's exactly what he meant. Chẳng lẽ Đức Phật nói sai?

Ông Kris nhẹ nhàng hỏi:

- Is your teacher a real Zen master? Ông đã tu tập ở đâu? Which teacher to study with? According to which sect? Ông đã thực hành được bao lâu rồi?

Connie was confused:

- My meditation teacher is not a monk but has a certificate from a Zen center in Japan, that he has attained enlightenment...

Mr. Kris shook his head and smiled:

- That's it! As far as I know, no genuine Zen master would issue such a certificate. Đó chỉ là trò lừa bịp. Only the teacher can know the level of enlightenment of the student and this is a private matter between teacher and student, it cannot be expressed by a diploma or label to be stuck on the body.

Connie frantically:

- Do you want to say that I was deceived? So is unwritten, specifically transmitted by pagans really the Buddha's words? What does it mean?

Mr. Kris explained:

- Patriarch Bodhidharma, also the Patriarch of Zen Buddhism, indeed taught like that, or at least in the scriptures, his words are recorded like that. However, today many people misunderstand or deliberately abuse this teaching to serve their own purposes. To put it simply, the path of meditation sometimes cannot be expressed in ordinary language. If I say it, it is only reluctant because language cannot express the indescribable things. Like a person drinking water, knowing whether it is hot or cold. The words spoken can cause the listener to misunderstand. And once it is not written down, it cannot be taught according to normal scriptures. Saying so does not mean rejecting the written word, but rather that each person's meditation path is based on the mind, directed towards the mind. But first, she should still read and meditate on the scriptures to create a foundation for herself and then find a teacher to guide her. She also must know how to choose a teacher, find the right teacher, in the right place, and cannot just believe in certifications or advertisements. Nowadays, there are many people who want to practice meditation, but there are very few genuine Zen masters. Even if she was lucky enough to meet a Zen master, he would only give her general instructions until she was ready. Therefore, make yourself ready, because when the disciple is ready, the teacher will appear.

Connie asked:

- So what do I have to do to get ready?

Mr. Kris leisurely explained:

- Until you find a genuine teacher, you should spend time reading more scriptures and attending sermons at monasteries or religious establishments. Genuine monasteries never collect money or require any payment, because Buddha forbade selling Dharma. This is a standard that can help her distinguish a place of genuine practice that keeps the precepts from places that only operate for commercial purposes. And even if she finds a true teacher, she should still keep herself in the mindset of learning, exploring, always alert and reflecting, and not necessarily listen to everything the teacher says. In my opinion, this cautious approach is best.

Mr. Kris turned to all of us and added:

- Practicing without a theoretical foundation is easy to get lost. But no matter how good the scriptures are, they cannot guide as effectively as interaction with an experienced teacher. In my opinion, first of all, practitioners should take the time to study the scriptures and then ponder the meaning in them. I know many people who have practiced meditation for many years, thinking that they have improved, but without the classic texts to refer to and confirm, they still easily stray into certain types of pagan meditation or are lured into the superstitious path of sorcerers, which is very difficult to escape. All this confusion can be avoided through learning and studying the scriptures to see your path clearly.

Connie hỏi:

- Tôi muốn biết rõ hơn về việc thực hành có thể giúp gì cho sức khỏe của tôi hay có thể trừ được bệnh tật không?

Ông Kris gật đầu, trả lời điềm đạm:

- Nếu thực hành đều đặn, cô sẽ thấy sức khỏe của mình phục hồi một cách bất ngờ. Nhiều người duy trì thói quen tập thể dục thể thao hằng tuần, đó đúng là một thói quen lành mạnh, nhưng cũng chỉ gia tăng sức khỏe bên ngoài. Most illnesses come from within or from the mind. Nếu cô bận rộn, lo lắng đủ mọi chuyện rồi dẫn đến mất ăn, mất ngủ, sinh bệnh và như thế thì việc tập thể thao cũng không giúp được bao nhiêu. Practicing meditation through slow, gentle breathing can calm her turbulent nervous system. Hơi thở nhịp nhàng sẽ mang sinh lực (prana) vào các cơ quan nội tạng, có công dụng chữa lành được nhiều thứ bệnh. Nếu nói một cách khoa học thì khi máu huyết lưu thông đều đặn, không bế tắc, các cơ quan nhận được đầy đủ oxy sẽ hoạt động hữu hiệu hơn.

Connie ngần ngại:

- Tôi có một câu hỏi tế nhị là khi thực hành thiền, miệng tôi đã tiết ra nhiều nước bọt làm tôi khó chịu. I'm a clean person so it was very distracting. I don't know if there is any way to make less saliva?

Mr. Kris replied calmly:

- It is normal to secrete a lot of saliva during practice and it has a very mysterious effect that few people know about. In terms of practice, it is often considered a good sign and the practitioner swallows it rather than spits it out. Scientifically speaking, saliva contains many antibodies with special effects. By practicing meditation and breathing prana into the body, the structure of saliva will change, increasing the amount of nerve growth factor (Nerve Growth Factor - NGF). When NGF is produced, it increases the efficiency of nerve cells, helping them grow or survive longer. Increasing NGF can reduce the effects of aging, and especially limit diseases such as Alzheimer's and cancer. She can see that people who practice meditation rarely get sick and have a very Many Lives, Many Times expectancy, which is also thanks to this factor.

Connie nodded:

- I see, but I didn't know for a long time, so I kept getting annoyed.

Mr. Kris smiled and continued:

- Practicing meditation properly must include two parts. The theoretical part is what she learns through books or classics. Practice is about cultivating and training the mind, body and emotions. Theory and practice can be compared to the wings of a bird. With both wings, a bird can fly in the vast sky. Without either one, birds cannot fly. Nói một cách khác, lý thuyết hướng dẫn thực hành vì nó cung cấp các khái niệm căn bản để cô có thể thực hành một cách vững chắc. Practicing helps her understand herself better. Khi đã hiểu biết, cô cần phải trở lại kinh điển để kiểm chứng xem việc thực hành đó có đúng với ý nghĩa chỉ dẫn trong kinh điển hay không. If everything becomes clear, precise and meaningful, she can continue with peace of mind. At that time her practice also became deeper. The deeper she practiced, the more clearly she understood everything and thus her meditation practice improved.

Practicing meditation without the foundation of studying the scriptures is very risky, because the practitioner can be led to blindness, ignorance and astray. The experience of practicing meditation that is not verified by scriptures or Buddha's teachings is just a vague experience, without anything to determine or evaluate, it is easy to get lost in pagan meditation practices or the methods of magicians and witches. Currently, there are many meditation methods spread by these people for the purpose of profiteering and seducing people's minds for some obscure purpose. Therefore, when practicing meditation, you must be careful and study with Zen masters in temples and monasteries and not follow those who claim to have attained enlightenment.

Connie asked:

- So in order for meditating to achieve good results, what do I need to pay attention to while meditating?

Mr. Kris replied:

- The important thing when starting is to sit firmly, because meditation is a very complete and rigorous form of practice. Currently, there are many types of support tools on the market, but in reality, meditation does not require these things. She just needs a thin pillow or a towel. Don't worry about the tools, as long as you sit firmly, that's enough.

Connie was surprised:

- I see that most people who meditate use special chairs or cotton mattresses designed specifically for meditation. These mattresses are sold in meditation schools and I also bought one.

Mr. Kris smiled:

- Those things don't matter, you can sit on special cushions or sit on the ground, it's all the same. Nowadays, meditation has been commercialized, creating many support products. Many people are taught that when meditating, they need special mattresses, burning incense to purify the air, sometimes even having to play meditation music while practicing to promote the effectiveness of the practice, and then using meditation applications on their phones to support them. All of these are just commercial advertising tricks. In the past, Zen masters did not have those things. They only sat on flat ground, in stone caves, but still attained enlightenment. Nowadays, meditation instructors are just pretending to make more money.

Proper meditation practice must include two parts. The theoretical part is what we learn through books or classics. Practice is about cultivating and training the mind, body and emotions. Theory and practice can be compared to the wings of a bird. Only by having both wings can a bird fly in the vast sky.

Connie asked:

- I have been practicing meditation for a long time but have not seen any significant results or changes. Don't know what I should do now?

Mr. Kris smiled patiently:

- As I just told you, in the first stage, what you need to do is change your daily habits through contemplation and purification, to calm your mind. Next, she needs to practice reflecting on herself. She meets friends, talks, thinks and behaves in social environments, but does she ever think deeply about those things? Do you treat people kindly? Will she offend anyone? Are her words gentle? Will her actions hurt anyone? When you examine yourself, you will understand yourself better.

Connie was surprised:

- How does this relate to meditation? My teacher has not taught anything about this. Why should we examine ourselves? I am an honest person who never harms anyone...

Mr. Kris nodded and explained:

- That's right, at first glance this seems unrelated. But it is the first step of preparation that can help her go further in her meditation practice later. If your life is clean, your soul is calm, and not disturbed by anything, then when you practice, thoughts of anger, hatred, or worry will no longer arise. When her mind is not disturbed by selfish, harmful, dishonest, or deceitful things, her meditation becomes easier. If you don't examine yourself, change your life, purify yourself, and keep your body, speech, and mind pure and virtuous, bad thoughts will easily arise during meditation and disrupt your practice. Most people who practice meditation have difficulty with these thoughts, so they need to reflect, repent, repent, and change their minds first to go far. If you can adjust so that the three karmas of body, speech and mind (body, speech, mind) are pure, your meditation practice will easily yield results. Letting go of everything is something that ancient Zen masters taught their students very carefully during the preparation stage. Unfortunately, today people just want to take shortcuts, just want to get results quickly, so not many people can go far.

Connie thought and asked:

- If you know how to contemplate and change your mind, what will be the next step?

Mr. Kris continued:

- When the mind is pure, undisturbed by the messy thoughts of daily life, the next stage is to concentrate to reach a state of concentration, this is when she uses breathing to naturally treat delusions. When your consciousness is natural, calm, clear, and balanced, you will see your life begin to be reoriented. Her priorities will become much clearer and clearer. When she decides on something, she will do it naturally, clearly, without thinking too much because her mind is no longer disturbed like before. From there, you will clearly understand the benefits of meditation. If you can properly apply what I instruct you now, about six months later, you will find yourself having a clear transformation, you will have more energy, more strength, and be able to make wiser, clearer, and quicker decisions than before.

Andrew happily interjected:

- If that's the case, it would be great because my family is the type of person who worries about all kinds of things, always wonders about everything, wants to control and think a lot but has difficulty making decisions.

Mr. Kris smiled and explained:

- The mind is like a lake. All worries and thoughts are likened to winds blowing on the lake surface, creating waves, and the lake is disturbed. When the mind is concentrated, it is like the surface of a lake without wind so it is completely calm, everything calms down, the surface of the lake is quiet and everything is reflected in it perfectly, from the stars, to the sun and moon shining clearly. When all false thoughts stop, we have concentration and from there we will develop the ability to see everything clearly, deeply, and easily. At that time, you can see everything deeply and make decisions calmly and quickly.

Connie asked:

- You mentioned earlier about having to breathe naturally but I still don't understand clearly how to practice breathing correctly, could you please explain more?

Mr. Kris slowly explained:

- Natural breathing simply means you just breathe normally, don't do anything unusual. However, you need to be careful to avoid irregular inhalation and exhalation, such as when inhaling is long but exhaling is short or vice versa. Inhalation and exhalation must be regular and continuous, not interrupted because this will cause problems. Just breathe evenly and naturally, don't try too hard. In fact, breathing is related to the state of the mind. If you try to breathe in a certain way, it will disturb the mind, making it very difficult to concentrate.

Connie hesitated a bit and then asked:

- My meditation teacher instructed me to practice focusing my breath down to my stomach...

Mr. Kris sipped a cup of tea and slowly explained:

- When you use your ability to inhale deeply, forcing your breath down into your belly will cause your muscles to contract, disrupting your concentration. She thought to herself, are you meditating or exercising? The essence of meditation is that the body must be natural, relaxed, and comfortable, not forced. When you breathe lightly and naturally, your breathing will gradually become regular, and you will feel comfortable and relaxed. Meditation is about focusing the mind, nothing else. If she focuses too much on gathering her breath and forcing it down into her stomach, she will have difficulty concentrating. Once she breathes evenly, her breath will guide her, she does not need to control her breathing. When your breathing is gentle, your mind will become relaxed, and you will find yourself able to concentrate on the practice and no longer pay attention to your breathing.

Connie still wonders:

- But do I need to monitor my breathing to treat delusions?

Mr. Kris smiled:

- Once she has a steady rhythm, breathing will happen naturally and her mind will then pay attention to other things. At that time, you can observe the delusions happening in your mind, when they come and when they go. If you don't let them transform, you will have the practice. If you can do that, then over time you will have concentration, when delusions will gradually disappear and you will be in a peaceful, free state. When her mind is clear and calm, she will enter a very special psychological state, with a close connection between herself and her spiritual state. This state is inherent in everyone, but you don't know it. In the past, she let messy thoughts obscure it, making it vague, but when her mind is clear, she will easily recognize it. That clear mind is wisdom, not intelligence. Meditation is about returning to find the wisdom that is always there, and that wisdom is inside us, not anywhere else.

Mr. Kris concluded:

- After completing your daily meditation session, don't do anything right away, but walk around the room for five or ten minutes to pay attention to your surroundings and observe your mind comfortably. When she arrives at work, she must keep her mind calm by being alert and mindful when engaging in normal activities. Avoid activities that can cause excitement or anger, then say things you shouldn't say or do things you shouldn't do. Eating is also an important factor in meditation. Be careful while eating because using food is to nourish the body, not to care or focus on whether it is delicious or not. Eating well will lead to cravings and then desire. Rest is the same, you need to get enough sleep, not too much or too little. Sleeping too much will make the mind confused, sleeping too little will cause memory loss, forgetfulness, and neurological complications. Get into the habit of going to bed and waking up on time. When it's time to sleep, put everything aside and go to bed right away. When you wake up, don't rush to follow the news or open Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter because those things will distract you from practicing meditation. When she pays attention to messages, compliments, and unconscious comments from irresponsible people, she can be influenced and lose herself. Limiting these activities will help you develop the mental strength to support your meditation practice. In addition, I advise you not to say much about spiritual matters or about your practice at inappropriate times. It's best to keep your practice as private as possible to avoid prying questions or useless criticism. If you meditate regularly, you will find that even in the busiest work or most stressful conflicts, you can still find your peace. In my opinion, meditation is one of the most valuable gifts today for busy people like you. Thanks to her diligent practice, she was able to restore her spirit with a magical source of peace even in the midst of the most stressful times. Time is precious and you must use it for yourself, not let it be your master. The schedule is created by her, not by someone else. You should learn how to organize your work and use your time effectively. By doing so, she will adapt to a more lucid and meaningful rhythm of life than the usual tumultuous rhythm to which she is accustomed.

Meditation is about returning to find the wisdom that is always there, and that wisdom is inside us, not somewhere else. Consciousness is like a lake. All worries and thoughts are likened to winds blowing on the lake surface, creating waves, and the lake is disturbed. When the mind is concentrated, it is like the surface of a lake without wind so it is completely calm, everything calms down, the surface of the lake is quiet and everything is reflected in it perfectly, from the stars, to the sun and moon shining clearly. When all false thoughts stop, we will have concentration and from there we will develop the ability to see everything clearly, deeply, and easily.

tieu_de: Part Seven: Holy War - Faith and Desire
noi_dung:
PART SEVEN

Holy WAR

FAITH AND LUST

The fall of the Roman Empire ended the period of slavery in Europe, opening the feudal period. For many centuries afterward, Europe fell into chaos, with prosperity and decline, conflicts, usurpations, self-appointments, and divisions - especially in terms of religion. In 1095, Pope Urban II launched the Holy War with a call for Christians to liberate the holy city of Jerusalem from Muslims. This call spread throughout Europe and was strongly responded to by Catholics. Since then, for nearly two hundred years, a series of intermittent religious wars have taken place, causing people's lives to constantly change...

***

Guiole is a small, remote village in France, the lives of the people here are extremely miserable and boring. Therefore, when the Pope's call spread here, most of the young men in the village volunteered to go. My father is also one of them. When my father left, I was less than two years old, and all the memories I have of him are only through fragmentary accounts from my family. However, the image of a hero dying for his religious faith left a good impression in my heart.

Two years after my father passed away, my mother fell ill and passed away, and since then I have lived with my grandparents. Although I lack the love of my parents, the care and love of my grandparents fully compensates me. Like everyone in the village, my grandparents also struggled with a poor life. The three of us lived crowded together in a rotten house, next to a small garden, with a cow, four sheep and a flock of chickens.

Since I was very young, my grandparents taught me to always strictly adhere to moral standards, to know right from wrong, to always respect God, and to always have compassion for others. Whenever there is a chance, my grandmother reminds me never to take anything that does not belong to me, not to do anything that harms others, not to steal, not to lie or make things up... My grandmother reminds me so much that I wonder why she has to keep saying things that I already know by heart.

In our place, everyone has to work hard, busy from early morning until late at night to have enough to eat, because every family has to save rice, vegetables and fruits to pay to the lord who governs this area. Under feudalism, lords and nobles had full authority to kill and kill serfs in their lands. Even though we are just a poor village, every year we still have to pay enough rice, vegetables and fruits to the lord according to regulations in order to live in peace. Even though we live in poverty and hardship, our family is still full of love and laughter.

When I was sixteen years old, an unexpected event happened, disrupting our peaceful pace of life, taking my life in a different direction. One normal morning, my grandparents and I were working in a small garden when a strange man, dressed in rags, entered. With his barren appearance, it was difficult to guess his age. My grandmother raised her head and as soon as she saw the man, she immediately put down her shovel and shovel and walked towards him. She trembled:

- Daniel! Daniel! Is that you?

Daniel is my uncle's name. Since I was a child, I heard my grandmother tell me that my mother had an older brother, but he left home to join a theater group before I was born.

The man came forward to help his grandmother, and the two hugged each other in joy and sadness. I stood to one side confused, while my grandfather just coldly looked at the other person, mumbled something I couldn't hear clearly, then he turned back to continue working as if nothing had happened.

My grandmother brought the man into the house and signaled me and my grandfather to follow. I looked at my grandfather, then we followed her into the house. I looked curiously at the thin man with scraggly beard and ragged clothes sitting on the chair. He also looked back at me, then turned to ask his grandmother:

- Who is this boy?

- It is Jean, Babette's child. Jean, this is Daniel, your mother's older brother. Say hello to him.

I nodded to greet him. My grandmother sat down next to me and told me about my mother's death and my father's disappearance for many years.

When Daniel heard about my father, he got angry:

- That's also the reason why I came back here. That bastard currently lives in Verden, he is the lord in charge of that area, eating well, dressing comfortably, and enjoying luxury.

My grandfather had been silent all this time, but when he heard that, he immediately spoke up:

- How did he become a lord?

Uncle Daniel avoided his grandfather's eyes, looked at me intently, and said in a somewhat sad voice:

- While on tour in Verden, I saw Robert sitting in the stands with his wife and children. I recognize it but it doesn't recognize me.

Grandfather asked again:

- Are you sure it's Robert?

Mr. Daniel answered firmly:

- That's it. On its face there are still scars left by the child. Furthermore, its right hand also lost its little finger. Can't be wrong.

The grandparents looked at each other thoughtfully. After the meal, Uncle Daniel discussed with my grandparents and allowed him to take me to meet my biological father. He said:

- I originally intended to report this to my brother, so he could find Robert to figure things out. Now my brother is gone, but Jean is still here. After all, it was Robert's child, he couldn't help but recognize it as his own. Now he is also a lord, believing that he can give Jean a better life.

After a while of discussion, my grandparents agreed to let me go with my uncle, because they believed that getting my father back would help my life improve and have a better future than continuing to live in this poor, remote village. My mood at that time was extremely disturbed, my mind became foggy. In one morning, I had to receive too much news. My father is still alive and has become a lord, so why hasn't he come back to look for us all these years? If I go with you to find my father, I will meet again the father I never knew but always considered him a hero. But to do so would mean I would have to leave my beloved grandparents, the people who raised me since I was young. My grandmother understood my hesitation so she tried her best to advise me. She told me to go find my father, and once I recognized him, I could still come back and reunite with my grandparents. Her words made sense so I finally agreed.

My uncle stayed home for a few days, helped me arrange the housework, and helped my grandparents a bit. Then we hit the road. After about two days of traveling, we arrived at the edge of a forest. In front of us was a group of horse-drawn carriages stopping to camp. The people there were wearing strange and colorful costumes. The Gitan [4], I think.

Gitan is a group of nomads, wandering here and there, doing many jobs to make a living. At that time, the true origin of the Gitan people was still shrouded in mist. Due to their wandering life, they gathered many different ethnicities, mostly from India, Egypt and Persia. Giving up their homeland and accepting the four lakes as their home, the Gitan people are often discriminated against and oppressed by local people. They are not welcomed, disrespected and have to constantly be on the move. They clustered into a separate society, living as independent tribes, and thanks to traveling here and there a lot, they formed an extremely diverse and unique culture. They are talented in dancing and performing, so many Gitan groups form singing troupes and tour everywhere to make a living.

Now I know that the theater troupe my uncle followed belongs to this group of Gitan people. As we approached the camp, an older man with a thick beard and hair approached. He raised his hand to stop Daniel.

- Who is this kid? Why did you bring him here?

Mr. Daniel replied:

- It is my sister's child. I want to take him to see his father in Verden. Please allow it to stay.

The man looked at me quizzically and then signaled Daniel to step aside to discuss. At the same time, he turned around and called a boy playing nearby. I don't know what he said, but the boy walked towards me and coldly asked:

- What is your name?

I guess this boy is one or two years older than me. I cautiously answered:

- I'm Jean.

He looked at me from head to toe as if evaluating, then suddenly grabbed my hand and introduced himself:

- I'm Pedro, do you want to go out there and play with us?

Following the direction Pedro pointed, I saw not far away a group of children gathering to play. I looked at Daniel but he was still engrossed in talking so I timidly followed Pedro to the group of kids.

Pedro pointed at me and introduced himself to the children:

- Everyone, this is Jean, a new kid, let's welcome him.

I noticed Pedro emphasized the word welcome in an unusually formal way. The children stopped playing and surrounded me excitedly. I was still bewildered when suddenly someone in the group rushed towards me and pushed me so hard that I fell to the ground. The remaining children immediately rushed towards me, pinned me down and began to strip my clothes off. I tried my best to resist, swinging my arms and kicking around, struggling to get up. The whole group shouted and took turns pushing me. One of them hugged me and threw me to the ground again. We wrestled, dust and sand flying amidst the cheers and cheers until I realized my naked body so I didn't want to fight anymore, just worried about covering my body. At that moment, a girl ran over, pushed the other child away, and threw me a torn blanket. I quickly stood up, wrapped the blanket around me and looked at the group of laughing children with hatred.

The girl said loudly:

- Okay, that's enough. That welcome is enough.

Pedro laughed:

- He's uncle Daniel's nephew, you should give him a real welcome.

The children burst out laughing, making me both confused and embarrassed. I turned around and was about to leave when Daniel and the man with a thick beard walked over. Mr. Daniel patted my shoulder:

- Now you have become a Gitan like me. We will go to Verden, but it's almost winter now, the weather is getting colder, we have to go to the South first. In the spring, when the weather gets warmer, we will go to the North to find your father.

The man with the bushy beard said to me:

- From now on you will live with Pedro, he will teach you what to do.

At that time, the girl who brought me the blanket also came over and introduced herself:

- Your name is Jean, right? I'm Ella.

I nodded and was about to say thank you when suddenly Ella swung her hand and slapped me, causing me to be stunned.

I was angry and shouted:

- What are you doing?

Pedro laughed and explained:

- It welcomes you.

I tried to swallow my anger and followed Pedro into the nearby carriage. I was about to take out some clothes to change into but Pedro signaled to stop me. He rummaged around for a while and then threw me a strangely styled set of clothes. No longer looking as bossy as before, Pedro used a gentle tone to explain:

- Now that you are a Gitan, you must completely transform, giving up everything related to your previous life. According to tradition, to join us, you must be welcomed by being stripped of your clothes and subjected to a beating, because from now on you are a new person, living a new life, according to Gitan law. I'll teach you these things, now get changed.

Still holding the clothes in my hand without moving, I looked at Pedro and protested:

- But I'm not from Gitan.

Pedro shook his head:

- Right now. If you want to stay here, you must live like a Gitan. If you don't want to, you can return to your old village.

Pedro finished speaking and left, not giving me a chance to argue. I thought for a while and then put on the clothes Pedro left behind. I know, my life has changed forever from now on.

I got to know everyone in the troupe quite quickly. The man with a bushy beard I met the first day was Alfonso, the leader here. This troupe consists of six families, all of whom are related to each other. Most of them have special talents, people who know how to use musical instruments, people who know how to do acrobatics, people who sing and act. They move here and there, taking performing as their livelihood. Alfonso is a very strict person while Mona, his wife, Pedro and Ella's mother, is gentle, quiet but has a great influence on everyone in the troupe. She is the only person in the group who knows how to read, write and understand historical legends, so the children in the group love to follow her and listen to stories. In addition, Mona is also the person who prepares medicines, reads palms, tells cards, and predicts everything with a crystal ball.

Mona often advises us many things. She taught that illness stems from living unconsciously, indulgently and excessively. The disease originates in the body due to excessive eating, anxiety, fear or anger. The disease also occurs due to external causes such as hot, cold, dry or humid weather. If you know how to live according to nature, without worrying, being sad or overeating, your body will have fewer illnesses.

Living together, we kids sometimes have conflicts and quarrels and often come to Mona to arbitrate. At times like these, Mona will advise us: You must know how to look at everything in life as the weather. Spring comes, plants bloom; When autumn comes, the grass and trees wither. Whatever happens, it comes and goes, nothing lasts forever. Therefore, don't let anything affect you and cause resentment and sadness. You must learn to be patient, no matter what problem or challenge, you must learn to endure, be patient, and when you overcome it, you will be at peace.

While practicing for a performance, if someone proudly bragged about their talent, Mona would advise: Look, when alive, birds eat insects, but when dead, insects eat birds. Time and circumstances always change, sometimes this way, sometimes that way, that is the cycle of life. Nothing lasts forever, so never be proud of yourself at the expense of others. What goes up will come down, sometimes glorious, sometimes humiliating. Therefore, whatever you do, you must be humble and think of the consequences before acting.

When someone is disappointed because they are not as talented as others, Mona will advise: Everyone has their strengths and weaknesses. If you feel that you are not equal to others, don't be afraid to learn from their good things to supplement your bad things. As long as you try, you can overcome any obstacle and achieve many achievements.

When going through the cities, looking at the magnificent, splendid castles and the happy, comfortable, and prosperous life of the aristocracy, Mona taught us: "Don't look at the rich life of the aristocracy and covet it. You must know how to distinguish clearly between what you need and what you want.
