If you already have everything you need, you must know how to be satisfied, anything more than what you need is just a reward. It's okay to have it, it's okay to not have it, and Not everyone has it. Don't compare or be jealous of rich aristocrats, they have so much to lose that they are always worried and afraid. We have nothing to lose so we have nothing to worry about. But if we have too many choices, we will want one thing and then another, and from desire will come greed and many bad habits, hatred and jealousy, leading to a ruined life If you give up, your life will be happier. If you know enough, your life will have no more troubles.

After learning that I lost my mother at a young age, Mona took special care of me more. Even though she is the shared mother of the children in the troupe, I feel that she always finds ways to teach, care for, and spend more time with me. I am very grateful to Mona and love her too. I often follow her, listen to her read and preach the Bible. She told me: Nothing in the world can replace a mother because a mother is an expression of love. The mother is the embodiment of God, because He cannot take care of all of His children, so He created the mother to do that. Because I didn't have a mother since I was young, I see Mona as the mother that God has compensated for me.

I lived in the same car with Pedro and five other children, all of whom were members of the group. At that time, I had been with the troupe for more than two months. Every day I followed everyone to do odd jobs such as carrying loads, setting up the theater, and cleaning. One day, while the theater group was gathering to eat and drink, Gilbert, who specializes in performing knife throwing, said to Daniel:

- I see that your nephew is agile and can learn to throw knives. Let it follow me.

Mr. Daniel agreed, I was also happy. From then on, besides my daily work, I followed Gilbert to learn knife throwing. Pedro and other young men learn music performance.

At that time, the Church held the greatest power and monopoly on both ownership and production of music. Most music was composed by monks because only these people had the right to create and maintain musical manuscripts in monasteries. Music was considered a gift that God reserved for them, so the clergy did not accept any other form of music. The Church considered other types of music immoral, despised religious authority and asked the court to severely punish those who composed or performed this music. However, musicians called troubadours or troubadours, mostly Gitan, still secretly create music in their own way. The fact that they chose to live a wandering life, traveling here and there with traveling theater troupes was also to avoid being hunted by the court. Their music is largely based on folk legends, some create lively melodies, mainly praising human love, especially love between men and women. This type of music is heavily condemned by the Church but is most loved by the masses. Alfonso is one of the talented and famous buskers in the Gitan community. He has extensive knowledge and is responsible for teaching music to the children in the group. I also often follow Pedro to attend Alfonso's teaching sessions to learn as a group. Once, Alfonso told us:

- Most of the music of the aristocracy is more about repetitive, long-lasting sounds to praise their gods or kings. We Gitan people use musical instruments in our own way. For example, when strumming the lute [5], they often use the pick, while we strum with our fingers. You must learn this way of strumming. Aristocrats use the lute as a secondary musical instrument, accompanying the melody of the main musical instrument, while we use the lute as the main musical instrument with an independent sound to express our emotions, not accepting anyone's restraint. We use musical instruments with our hearts to praise human love, not to praise gods or kings. Therefore, when using the lute, you must let your emotions guide you, let your fingers vibrate according to your heart, and the sound you pluck must resonate, in harmony with your heart. Music is created by melody and emotions, so you must feel your emotions while strumming the guitar to create real music. To become a musician, you must know how to be moved by everything that happens around you to be able to express people's feelings, thoughts, and emotions, happiness and sadness, joy and suffering. When you sing, you must put your whole soul into the words and melody, because there is no better way to expand and touch the hearts of others than music.

Even though I don't study music, I often sit and listen to Pedro practice the piano. There is something very familiar and attractive about the melodies that Pedro is practicing. I can distinguish between the majestic, majestic Doria melody, evoking courage and confidence, from the gentle Lydia melody, full of nostalgic sentiments, to the clear, calm and solemn Phrygia melody.

Ella and the other young women in the troupe learned to sing, dance and act. Among them, Ella is the girl who sings and dances best. As soon as I met Ella for the first time, I had a strangely familiar feeling. At that time, I still thought that feeling came from the fact that she was the first person to be polite and help me when I came here. But the longer we interact, the more I feel like we once knew each other. Especially when I saw her dancing, I felt even more familiar, as if I had seen these dances before. Every rhythmic step, every graceful gesture of hers is both attractive and familiar. Of course I don't share this feeling with anyone, but I still often find opportunities to watch Ella dance.

During my childhood, I lived in a remote village, so my knowledge was very limited. Since living a wandering life with the Gitan people, I have witnessed many unbelievable events, making me think about what I was taught before. I clearly saw the brutality of the warlords against the people in their territories, witnessed the corruption, arrogance, and hegemony of the soldiers under these warlords. Feudalism requires people to be absolutely loyal to the court and lords. The lords all live in large, luxurious, splendid castles, built by the labor of serfs. They set their own laws for their land in order to appropriate property and thoroughly exploit people's labor. Not only that, the warlords are always fighting and fighting to usurp each other's land. To maintain power, most of them had their own military forces and those loyal to the lord were awarded knighthoods.

At that time, the most prestigious and influential force was the Church, so from kings to lords all sought to associate with the Holy See to receive legitimate support. Therefore, every region built many large cathedrals and monasteries and lavishly treated the clergy. To have money for construction, the lords imposed many religious taxes, forcing people to contribute money or effort, despite their abject poverty. In many territories, lords issued extremely harsh laws, with heavy punishments, sowing fear to oppress the people. With the strong influence of the Church, many lords joined hands with clerics to enforce laws. The decision of guilt or innocence is considered the right of God, through the intermediary of the clergy. Courts are often held in churches, where God is present. In some places, the law forced criminals to fight with knights to decide their fate. The fight took place in front of the people. The winner is considered innocent, because God gave them victory, the loser is guilty and must die at the hands of the executioner. Most criminals are ordinary people, few people can win in fights with knights who are both strong and skilled in using weapons. Many unjust deaths have happened in these matches. My life of wandering also allowed me to witness the disadvantages and hardships of nomadic people. Wherever we went, we faced harassment from local soldiers. Every time we go to a new land, the soldiers there find excuses to search, demand bribes, and sometimes plunder until there is nothing left. These injustices and brutality made me begin to doubt and wonder, why do people treat each other so cruelly as children of God? Doesn't God teach us to love everyone? The clergy are messengers of God, how can they join hands with those brutal people to do things that are against God's will?

The more we experience these hardships and disadvantages together, the more attached I become to everyone in the theater group. One day, when the whole group stopped to rest at the edge of the forest, Gilbert pulled me aside and whispered:

- Jean, how do you feel about Ella? Do you like her?

Why did Gilbert ask that?, I wondered. Surprised and confused, I didn't answer, just looked at him bewildered. Living with Pedro, Ella's brother, I also consider her as my sister. Seeing my bewildered look, Gilbert smiled meaningfully:

- Have you heard Ella sing recently? Its voice contains more emotions than before, which is a sign of a girl just falling in love.

I objected:

- I see Ella singing like that all the time.

Gilbert shook his head:

- Maybe because you don't understand anything about love, but I see it has noticed you. Once Gitan's daughter loves someone, she will live and die with that love. Haven't you heard how it often sings about Eurydice's love [6]? It's waiting for you to show your attitude. I advise you not to miss this good opportunity.

That day I didn't answer Gilbert but tried to steer the conversation in another direction, but from then on I began to notice Ella's attitude. I realized that every time she sang, Ella indeed often turned her eyes towards me. In addition to regular songs, Ella also composed short songs praising love, which surprised Alfonso. As a young man, I also had moments of fluttering in front of women, but in the face of Ella's feelings, I did not find myself fluttering. Even though I consider her my sister, I still feel there is a huge gap between me and her. Sometimes, to reassure myself, I told myself that when I saw my father again, I would no longer live with Ella and these Gitan people but would live the life of the aristocracy. That's my real life, I can't be tied to these people for the rest of my life.

Not long after, our troupe went to a small village. Daniel and I were assigned to find a place to set up a stage for the troupe to perform. While walking, Daniel suddenly stopped and looked intently at a man in a robe sitting under a tree. Mr. Daniel cautiously stepped closer, then he suddenly cried out in an emotional voice:

- Piere! Pierre, is that you?

The person raised his head to look at us. After a second of confusion, he recognized Daniel and happily replied:

- Who do you think! Turns out it was you.

Daniel walked up to the other person and asked:

- What are you doing here? I heard you went with Robert to join the Holy War, what happened? I know it has become a lord. And you, why are you here alone, and dressed like a priest? What happened in the end?

When alive, birds eat insects, but when dead, insects eat birds. Time and circumstances always change, sometimes this way, sometimes that way, that is the cycle of life. Nothing lasts forever, so never be proud of yourself at the expense of others. What goes up will come down, sometimes glorious, sometimes humiliating. Therefore, whatever you do, you must be humble and think of the consequences before acting.

Piere explained, his voice melancholy:

- The four of us left the village to participate in the Holy War under the command of Knight Theodor in Count Ulrich's army. After many battles with the Muslims, Count Ulrich died, and out of the four of us, only Robert and I survived. We liberated the Holy Land, burned down Muslim cities, and captured countless gold, silver, and jewels. When he returned, the court gave gifts and land to those who had meritorious services. Because Count Ulrich died, his followers were not cared for by the court and were only given land in remote and remote areas. Theodor was made count and given the region of Verden. He brought a few trusted people to the land to receive the reward. On the road, while Theodor was sleeping, Robert assassinated Theodor, then identified himself as him. Because he had a certificate from the royal court, Robert automatically became the lord of this region. After that, Robert sent me to the monastery to study to be a priest to help him manage the territory. However, I didn't know how to read or write. When I entered the monastery, I only worked as a cleaner. After many years of living in a monastery, I felt like I didn't belong there, so I ran away. Now I live wandering through the villages, the little knowledge I learned at the monastery helps me play the role of a priest.

Daniel nodded and said:

- So that's it. I still wonder how an uneducated guy like Robert could become a lord. Turns out he was a traitor. She still owes me my sister.

Daniel looked at me and added with an angry voice:

- Babette has died a long time ago but her child and Robert are here. I want to take Jean to see his father. Robert has the responsibility to raise and care for his child's future properly and kindly.

Piere shook his head:

- No, Robert is a count under the name Theodor, he is married and has several children, how can he take care of Babette's children.

Daniel was angry:

- When he promised me all sorts of things, he had to keep his word, otherwise I would slit his throat.

Piere shook his head and waved his hand:

- No, it's not like before. How did you meet it? How could he get past its guards?

Daniel was startled but still spoke firmly:

- I will find a way...

Piere thought for a moment then said:

- Okay, if you insist on going to Verden to find Robert, I will go with you. I also know people there, and will find a way to arrange for the father and son to meet. What happens after that is up to you to decide.

Daniel happily nodded:

- That's great. Currently we are traveling with the Gitan troupe, we just stopped here. The weather is gradually warming up now, and we plan to go to Verden after the performance in this village. Now you come with me to meet Alfonso, he is the leader of our group, I have to ask permission for you to join.

Piere returned with us to meet Alfonso. At first, when Alfonso saw Piere dressed as a priest, he was very wary and opposed him joining. Uncle Daniel had to persuade Alfonso for a while before agreeing to let Piere stay. From there, Pierre joined us and not long after the group departed towards Verden. Knowing that Piere was my father's battle buddy, I proactively became friends with him to ask questions. Since I was young, my grandparents didn't like to talk about my father, so I didn't know much about him. Uncle Daniel gets angry every time I mention my father, so I don't want to ask. Pierre is different, he is very interested in me and often talks to me. When I asked about my father's past, Pierre sighed and said:

- Maybe you don't know, in the past your uncle Daniel led a bandit group that specialized in raiding and robbing villages around the region. To avoid being hunted by the law, he lives here and there, rarely in the village. Babette, your mother, was an innocent young woman who was seduced by Robert into becoming pregnant. However, Robert refused to marry, causing many scandals and damaging the family's honor. Hearing the news, Daniel immediately returned to the village, slashed Robert's face, and forced him to get married or else he would kill him on the spot. Robert had to cut off his little finger, swear to marry Babette and take good care of his child to escape death.

I was shocked to the point of silence. I didn't expect the truth about my family to be like that. Now, I understand why my grandparents don't like to talk about my father who has passed away, despite my many inquiries. I painfully realized that I was not a child born from my parents' love, but just the result of a secret affair, leading to a reluctant marriage.

Piere continued:

- Life at that time was very miserable. The drought lasted for several years, so many people in the village died of starvation. There was also pressure from the lords to pay all kinds of taxes, so everyone lived very miserable lives. Therefore, when there was a call to join the Holy War with the good promise of being rewarded with lots of money and land, poor young men like us all enthusiastically joined the army. Partly because they want to escape suffering, the other part hopes to become rich and if they have any sins, they will be erased and when they die they will go to heaven. No one expected that Jerusalem is very far away, it takes more than a year to get here. When we arrived in the Muslim land, we were surrounded in the desert, lacking food and water, countless people died of hunger and thirst. Fortunately, at a desperate time, reinforcements arrived, we broke the siege, and attacked Jerusalem. When we entered the city, we were ordered to directly kill all pagans and their families, regardless of whether they were Muslims or Jews. In the days that followed, there were killings, rapes, looting, and arson everywhere. Blood and corpses littered the streets. When we arrived at the city center, where the Muslim temple was located, we were extremely surprised because there was a lot of gold, silver, jewels and precious things that we had never seen in our entire lives.

I interrupted Pierre in surprise:

- Are Muslims that rich?

Piere nodded and confirmed with a bitter voice:

- That's right. We were all surprised, no one knew that those pagans were so rich and happy, while we, the children of God, lived in extreme poverty and misery.

I hesitated:

- But... saying that, you guys are no different from looting?

Piere did not appear confused by my accusation:

- We fought hard but only wanted to be rich. No one can take the gold and silver of the Muslims. So, everyone threw away all their weapons and armor to fill themselves with gold and silver, even putting them in cloth bags slung over their shoulders. Unfortunately, the joy was short-lived. The next day, the soldiers were ordered to bring all the gold, silver, and precious objects back to the royal court. Anyone who disobeys will be immediately executed. This made everyone surprised and extremely dissatisfied. However, we were promised that everything captured would be divided equally by the royal court among those who contributed. So everyone had to sadly watch the spoils of war being stored in large trunks and then loaded onto carts to bring back to the royal court. No one dared to think of touching these chariots, because they were all carefully guarded by elite Templar troops.

I was surprised:

- If you say that, the royal court is no different from robbery?

Piere laughed:

- Why are you so naive? Property, wealth, gold, everything of value captured in war belongs to the winning side. As the victors, we have the right to take everything to compensate for our years of hard fighting.

Piere's answer made me feel even more wrong. It's completely contrary to what I was taught, that "don't be greedy for others or take what doesn't belong to you". The fact that the victor gives himself the right to rob, kill, and rape women makes me feel disgusted by this war.

Piere sighed:

- However, when we returned from the battle, we learned that only princes and nobles were rewarded. Lowly soldiers like us were discharged and returned home without getting anything. When leaving, everyone hopes to return in glory and wealth, but when they return, they only have empty hands and a body full of injuries, decay, and illness. With such a situation, how can we return to our families?

I have always been taught to always be loyal to the court and the lords, but after many years of living in a situation of oppression, and now witnessing the greed and lies of the court, cracks have appeared in my trust.

Piere continued with a bitter voice:

- In the past, we lived in poverty and lack of food, so we signed up to participate in the Holy War, considering it the only way out to improve our lives. Who would have thought that so many sacrifices would be blatantly taken away by the nobles sitting around eating golden bowls. Even Theodor, our commander, went through many life and death battles and was only given the remote land of Verden. We were so disappointed, but we didn't know what else to do, so we followed Theodor to claim the land. On the way, Robert discussed with me that even if Theodor became lord, we would still be just lowly soldiers and could not get rich. To change our fate, the only way was to take over Theodor's identity. Waiting for Theodor to sleep, Robert assassinated him, stole the credentials, and impersonated Theodor to become lord of Verden. Because on that trip, Theodor only brought along two close people, me and Robert, so only the two of us knew about this. To keep it a secret, when he became lord, Robert sent me to a monastery to learn to be a priest and promised to build me a large cathedral to govern the people of Verden. But I was originally just an uneducated person. When I entered the monastery, I could only do odd jobs. Life there was boring and austere, so after a while, I ran away, lived a wandering life, and then met you and Daniel.

I'm so sad I can't speak. The image of my heroic father fighting for the ideals that I have cherished since childhood has now turned into a murderer, greedy and treacherous. The good ideal of a war to liberate the holy city of Jerusalem was taken advantage of by kings and turned into a blatant robbery. From there, I started thinking about the things I was taught in the past, the values ​​that everyone recognized. Why is reality so different from what is taught? Why can people who still pride themselves on being children of God go against His teachings like that? After many nights of thinking without a solution, I asked this to Mona, the person I trust the most today.

After listening to my presentation, Mona was silent for a moment and then said:

- All values ​​about good and bad, right and wrong are set to create order for society. Those are only relative conventions and are accepted by everyone, but you will have to determine for yourself what is right and what is wrong and then choose your own actions. Of course, sometimes you will encounter ambiguous and awkward situations that make you unable to decide. Because what is right in one place may be wrong in another, in this country it is good but in another country it is unacceptable.

I'm confused:

- So what should I rely on to make the right decision?

Mona replied:

- When faced with such a difficult situation, I advise you to make decisions according to ethical standards by asking yourself whether this will cause damage or injury to others. If you only focus on benefiting yourself regardless of harming others, then the decision you make will definitely be wrong.

I immediately asked Mona:

- Having said that, is it wrong to kill, rob gold, silver, and property of infidels?

Mona nodded:

- That's right. In my opinion, that action is truly reprehensible. God never teaches His children to behave like that. They have forgotten all the old teachings, that they must know how to forgive and love everyone, even enemies, because all are children of God. Greed has made people blind, completely straying away from their original goals, doing everything they do only wants to benefit themselves, how to gain the most profit, regardless of the loss of others. Greed makes people never know enough, so they are willing to do anything, including killing, appropriating, and robbing, making life worse and worse. From greed will lead to disputes, then to war, and the people are the class that suffers the most. Kings and nobles only think about their own interests, only want to accumulate gold, silver, wealth, and land, but pay no attention to the suffering that the people have to endure. Therefore, as a child of God, you must extend compassion to everyone, no matter who they are, and you must never do anything against His advice.

At that time I did not understand everything Mona said, but I always remembered her words and often reflected on the indiscriminate love she spoke of.

Our group was still very far from Verden, but I was no longer anxious to see my father. On the contrary, I wanted the journey to be longer so that I could delay the day I had to face him. The singers often choose to follow the forest route to avoid harassment from local soldiers. That day we were about to exit a dense forest when we saw a cloud of black smoke rising from the direction of the village ahead. The whole group spurred their horses toward the village. As we approached, we began to worry because the atmosphere was strangely quiet and stuffy. Not a soul, not a sound. We hesitated but Alfonso still decided to go into the village. After walking a while, we saw a crowd gathering in front of us. It seemed like the whole village had gathered here. No wonder it was so deserted outside. There was screaming and even crying. When I got closer, I realized the crowd was screaming and chasing someone away. This person was wearing a large cloak that covered him from head to toe, holding a small jingling bell in his hand, and walking with great difficulty. I also caught a glimpse of two women, one old and one young, hugging each other and crying behind the crowd. While I was still surprised, just about to turn to ask Daniel, I heard Gilbert shout to the whole group:

- Everyone be careful, don't go near that person.

I asked:

- Why is that? What are you guys doing?

Gilbert replied with a tense voice:

- That person has leprosy. Don't you see everyone is chasing him away?

Alfonso saw this and immediately ordered the whole group to step back and stay to one side. Gilbert explained further:

- People with this disease must hold a bell and continuously ring it so that everyone knows to stay away, because this disease cannot be cured and getting close is very contagious.

At that moment, a strong wind blew, causing the scarf covering that person's face to blow back. I was startled to see a face full of pimples with deep-set eyes and a flattened nose that looked very creepy. The crowd continued to scream, driving the person out of the village. The troupe stopped on the side of the road and waited for the crowd to chase the other person into the nearby forest. Waiting for the tension to subside, Alfonso started a conversation with a villager and asked:

- Where did that leper come from?

The other person shook his head:

- No. He is from this village but is sick so he is forced to live in places reserved for lepers. However, because he missed his family, he escaped and returned home. So we had to chase him away.

Because Mona is good at medicine and specializes in preparing medicines, I asked her:

- Mona, can leprosy be cured?

Mona shook her head:

- Unfortunately, we don't know how to cure this disease. Illnesses are often classified by external causes such as broken arms or dislocated bones, or internal causes such as stomach disease or heart disease. If the cause is known, it can be cured. However, there are strange diseases that cannot be cured if no one knows the cause. I have never heard of anyone curing leprosy.

Hearing that, Pierre immediately said:

- Those strange diseases are punished by God.

Mona was surprised:

- Piere, why do you say that?

Piere explained:

- When I was at the monastery, I heard the priests say that there were people who worshiped Satan and opposed God, so God punished them by making them suffer from incurable diseases, such as leprosy.

Mona shook her head:

- I don't believe it. God loves everyone, so how could He punish people like that?

Piere argued:

- She doesn't live in a monastery so she doesn't know this. Priests also teach that when the four horsemen of the apocalypse appear, humanity will be destroyed. The first horseman, the conqueror on the white horse, is Satan, seducing and inciting people against God. The second horseman, the one riding the red horse, is the one who spreads hatred and causes war. The third horseman, the one riding the black horse, represents the scarcity of food, causing famine, causing countless deaths. The fourth rider, the one riding the gray horse, is the god of death, bringing countless deadly disasters such as pestilence, famine, and murder. They are the representatives of the end of the world. Currently, Satan has appeared to fight with God, so there are such incurable diseases. Soon there will be more terrible epidemics spreading everywhere, wars will break out, and the final judgment day will come. At that time, only a very few people will be saved and go to Heaven, while the majority of evil people will be banished to Hell and live there forever.

The whole group immediately stirred when Pierre said that. Mona signaled everyone to be quiet. She told Pierre:

- Although I don't live in a monastery like you, I believe God would never do that. He teaches us to love and He loves everyone, it is impossible for Him to punish people in such a terrible way.

Piere shook his head and was about to object when Mona continued:

- Without God's love, the universe would disintegrate. Without love there is no order, what remains is only endless chaos. Not only did God create the universe, but out of love, He also created humanity. Even His son Jesus affirmed: God is love.

As soon as Mona said that, for some reason I heard a strong aura sweep through my body, making me tremble and dizzy. I have a vague feeling that I've heard this saying before. Piere shrugged his shoulders in disagreement, but didn't seem to want to argue further so he just smiled faintly. But I was very interested in what Mona had just said, so I asked her:

- But Mona, if God is love, then why are there such terrible, incurable diseases in the world?

Mona looked at me and said:

- Jean, God works silently and secretly so we cannot know what He does, but we believe He acts for a certain reason.

I asked again:

- What about other diseases? Why is there disease?

Mona explains:

- Most diseases that occur are caused by humans, not by anyone else, much less by God. Disease originates from people not living according to the laws of harmony and balance of nature. Most people live by emotions, and are controlled by emotions such as anger, hatred, jealousy, greed, and selfishness, so illness follows. Therefore, the treatment of diseases must also be through controlling these emotions, starting from adjusting the way of eating, saving energy, changing the way of life, reducing hatred, anger, greed and selfishness, then combining the use of doses from herbs and plants with medicinal properties to restore balance to the body. These pathogens are all related to internal emotions, they lie within humans just waiting for a convenient opportunity to arise. People who do not know how to control negative emotions such as anxiety, anger, hatred, greed, and selfishness all carry these diseases. Of course, they do not arise immediately when a person is healthy, but they will arise when the body begins to weaken and by then it may be too late. Therefore, if you want to cure the disease, you need to pay attention to both factors. Use medicine to regulate the body, but if you want to cure the disease completely, you must pay attention to the internal cause. In other words, it's not enough to just treat the physical illness, you also have to take care of the mental aspect as well.

At that moment, a villager passed by and said to Alfonso, pointing towards the forest on the other side of the village:

- The forest you just passed through is okay, but if you continue through the forest on the other side, you must be careful. It was where people with leprosy lived. This region is relatively deserted, surrounded by mountains and forests, far from big cities, so the court gathered people with leprosy and forced them to live here. Many people who have the disease but have not yet developed the disease have gone out to live and mix with the public, so many people are infected.

The other person's warning made the whole group scared and confused. Alfonso decided we would detour to the grassland route instead of taking the forest route. Our group did not stay in this village, but only gathered some food and immediately left. But just a few days later, our group encountered a group of people with leprosy. That day, the troupe was moving across a field when they heard the sound of jingling bells from afar. Alfonso was immediately alert and ordered the whole group to move to a high mound to avoid it. Once we kept a safe distance, we stopped, looked in the direction of the bell sound, and saw a group of people dressed from head to toe, moving in rows. As they walked, they shook the bell and shouted in unison: We are sinners. Waiting for them to leave, Gilbert explained:

- Those are people with leprosy who are asking for atonement. They also often torture themselves by using hot iron rods to press into their bodies, partly to cure itching on their bodies, partly to ask for atonement for their sins.

Piere heard that and repeated:

- Those are people who believe in Satan, so God punished them.

Mona immediately objected, her tone clearly showing her displeasure:

- How do you know they were punished? God is merciful, there is no way He would do that.

Piere also did not give up, he asked:

- How do you know they are not being punished? If not God, then who can create such terrible diseases? At this time, Satan appeared, causing many people to lose faith in God, no longer knowing right from wrong but only knowing how to compete, cheat, and rob everything possible. People are doing all kinds of bad things, regardless of morality and ethics. The arguments within the family have spread to society, no one has any respect for each other anymore. Husbands are not husbands, wives are not wives, children are spoiled and promiscuous, gathering to plunder. Because everyone is confused, violence happens everywhere.

Mona looked clearly dissatisfied, but because she didn't want to argue with Pierre, she turned to us children and said:

- In my opinion, when an event happens, it is easy to blame someone else. But the chaotic state of society is due to people's blindness and greed, not God's punishment of anyone. When you do bad things, you don't think about it, just do it haphazardly regardless of everything, but when the consequences happen, you only know how to prostrate and beg, hoping to be redeemed. What's the use? Therefore, what you need to remember is to never do anything without thinking about the consequences.

The troupe continues to move north toward Verden. From information collected from passersby, we know that the current epidemic is raging everywhere, with countless deaths and exiles. No one knows the origin of the epidemic. There are all kinds of rumors, most of which believe that this is a punishment from God. While many people are afraid and seek to repent and hope to atone for their sins, there are also many people who lose faith and turn to do all sorts of bad things, regardless of morality and ethics. Faced with the threat of death, many people no longer hold back and do whatever they want. All the accumulated anger poured out, hatred rose. Everyone was crazy, fights and riots happened everywhere. The entire social order has been completely shaken.

A merchant who traveled to many places told us that even in the royal court, epidemics could not be avoided. Kings and mandarins also had the disease, causing suspicion and confrontation to become extremely tense. In addition, the royal court has called on people to join the new Holy War even though the echoes of the old battle are still here, making people's hearts even more confused.

Our group arrived at Verden in the afternoon. Alfonso stopped the horse to camp in a field at the edge of Verden territory and then let Daniel and I enter the city. Even though I had always wanted to meet my father since childhood, after hearing the story Piere told about him, all my old hopes and excitement gradually disappeared. Even though you were the one who gave birth to me, you left when I was young. Do you still remember me? Do you want to take me back? Will he be the father I always dreamed of? When I decided to leave home with Uncle Daniel, in addition to the purpose of reclaiming my father, I also secretly dreamed of a more comfortable and happier life of the aristocracy, but at this point, I suddenly felt full of doubts. What if my father doesn't take me back? I thought back to the time I lived with the Gitan people, wandering from place to place, sometimes hungry, sometimes full, sometimes happy, sometimes sad, and I suddenly felt a deep regret, as if I was about to lose something precious. These Gitan people accepted me, treating me like family. But if I become a noble, I certainly cannot have any relationship with vagrants, despised by society like them. I briefly thought of Ella and the feelings she had for me. From the beginning, my desire to become a noble prevented me from having any feelings for her, much less from reciprocating her feelings.

While immersed in confused thoughts, I suddenly heard a man's shout. An old farmer drove a horse cart past our group and stopped. He said to Alfonso:

- Hey guys, you should go somewhere else to perform. No one here comes to see it. This place is no longer safe.

Alfonso was surprised:

- Why, last year we performed here and nothing happened?

This person shook his head and said:

- Now everything is different.

Looking at our bewildered looks, he explained:

- When the royal court again called for a Holy War, the lord here ordered every young man in the area to participate. Perhaps you also know that during the last Holy War, few of those who left returned. But because it was a royal order and recognized by the Church, this time the people had to listen. No one expected that after the young man left, the lord revealed his greedy intentions. He confiscated most of the fields and gardens of families that no longer had men. Although he also divided some land for people to grow crops for a living, in fact he only took advantage of the opportunity to collect agricultural products and store them in his food warehouse. This year there is a drought, crops fail, people are hungry, many people starve to death... Life in Verden is very miserable right now. Yet the lord still brutally collected taxes to enrich his glorious life and the noble families that supported him.

Mr. Daniel stepped forward and asked:

- But what happened that this place is no longer safe?

The man sighed:

- Recently, some people who participated in the Holy War returned alive. They did not receive any rewards from the royal court, some were still injured, so they were extremely dissatisfied. When they saw that their house and land had been confiscated and their wife and children were hungry, they were extremely angry. A group launched a rebellion, then a large number of people responded. They competed to burn down the lord's agricultural warehouses. Soldiers were sent to keep order but could not resist those returning from battle who were seething with anger. During the battle, the lord was seriously injured, the soldiers had no leader so they disbanded. Some soldiers were already dissatisfied, so they followed this unfavorable trend and turned to bandits. Nowadays, this place no longer distinguishes who is the enemy and who is the soldier, people also flood the streets to destroy and rob food warehouses, creating extremely chaotic conditions. The law no longer exists here, you should go somewhere else.

Daniel thought and told me:

- If the soldiers no longer protect the lord, it will be easier to meet your father. But he has fallen, do you still want to see him?

I hesitated a bit then nodded. Alfonso heard that and immediately said:

- Daniel, quickly take Jean to see his father, hand it over to him and return here immediately. I don't want to stay in an unstable place like this for too long.

I reluctantly said goodbye to my friends in the troupe, the people who considered me family. Pedro emotionally held my hand while Ella cried. Mona hugged me and gently said:

- I'm happy for you to see your father again, but remember we are also your family.

Daniel and Pierre took me into the city. Everywhere I go, I encounter scenes of devastation and ruin. We weaved through the narrow streets to avoid the fights going on. It took us a long time to reach the lord's castle. When we arrived, unlike the majestic scene often seen in lords' castles, there were no soldiers guarding this place, and there were traces of fighting everywhere. Uncle Daniel signaled me to be careful, and we cautiously snuck inside. Once inside, we saw a group of people rushing to carry everything and run out. Mr. Daniel grabbed someone and asked:

- What's going on?

The other person replied:

- The lord is dead, the army is disbanded, at this time whoever is strong can take whatever he can. If you want to take advantage of this opportunity, then hurry up.

After speaking, the other person ran away and disappeared. Uncle Daniel pulled me into the hall, where many people were cheering, destroying, and dismantling the precious things they could get their hands on. Uncle Daniel approached one of the people and asked where the lord was. Following this person's directions, we immediately followed the hallway leading to the room, where a woman was crying next to a large chair. Sitting on it was a large man with a long scar on his face from his forehead to his chin.

Mr. Daniel pulled me closer and shouted at the other man:

- Hey Robert, do you recognize me?

Under the flickering candlelight, I clearly saw that this person's face and neck were full of wounds and blood. I was so scared I couldn't speak. Mr. Daniel pointed at me:

- Robert, do you know who this kid is?

The other person looked up at me, but his eyes were dull and lifeless. The woman nearby spoke up:

- Who are you to dare speak to my husband like that? Who is Robert? This is Lord Theodor, you should take care of yourself.

Mr. Daniel laughed:

- Please ask your husband who we are? Hey Robert, tell your wife...

Suddenly the man on the chair whispered, trembling:

- Don't... Don't... Babette, I know I'm at fault, don't drag me down there.

The woman asked in surprise:

- Theodor! Theodor! What are you doing? What are you talking about? Who is Babette?

Daniel was also suspicious:

- What are you talking about? Babette died a long time ago, only your son is here. Look!

The other person opened his eyes wide open:

- No... Babette is standing in the corner over there.

We looked around, but there was no one else in the room. The woman kneeling at Robert's feet said in a panic:

- I'm Agnes, Theodor. What are you doing?

The man gasped as if afraid of something, then suddenly howled:

- Theodor, please... Forgive me... I don't want to die...

Piere looked around worriedly and muttered:

- Oh God, it mentioned the knight Theodor.

The other person still asked:

- Forgive me... Please, Theodor, forgive me...

Facing the man's crazy situation, Daniel shook his head:

- I want Jean to meet his father, then you and your father will worry about each other. Unexpectedly...

Piere bent down close to the other person's chest, listening and then shook his head:

- The wound is so serious, his breathing is so weak, it's hard to live.

The other person's breathing became increasingly labored, his face pale, but he kept muttering:

- Please help me, don't let them drag me away... I don't want to go... Please don't drag me down there.

I stood frozen, my whole body paralyzed. Is this the father I've always wanted to meet? Is this the person who gave birth to me? Why do I feel so strange? What do you see when you are so close to the earth and far from the sky? Did you see my mother, the person you betrayed and made her die alone? Did you see Theodor, who considered you a trusted friend, but you betrayed and murdered him to steal his lordship? What exactly is my father feeling in these last moments of his life? Do you recognize me? Do you ever remember me? Many questions continued to swirl in my head but I had no way to say them. Daniel observed Robert's expression and then said to me:

- Your father is about to die, say whatever you want. We have no reason to stay here anymore. Must leave quickly.

I wanted to say a few words to my father, but my throat kept choking, so I just stood there watching him struggle in fear until his eyes rolled back and his breathing stopped. He is dead.

At that moment, there was a rush of footsteps, then a group of people ran into the room. Seeing that the lord was dead, they began racing to remove the decorations in the room, some even tried to remove the ring on his hand. One person shouted loudly:

- Hang this bastard's body in the square for everyone to see.

The crowd immediately gathered and dragged his body away. A woman named Agnes rushed forward and tried to stop the group of people, but another person grabbed her hair and pushed her to the ground.

I was about to rush in to stop, but Daniel immediately stopped me:

- Don't do anything stupid. In this situation, there is nothing more that can be done. Let's go, I can't stay here anymore.

Uncle Daniel pulled me out of the room. I walked like a sleepwalker because I was still moved by the image of my father who had just passed away in pain.

Piere asked:

- Are you going to bring him back to the troupe?

Mr. Daniel said quickly:

- Robert is dead, it's dangerous here. Get out of here and figure it out later.

Going to the street, the situation was much worse. Everything was ruined, the crowd seemed to have gone crazy. The cries, screams, and sounds of weapons clashing sounded extremely horrifying. I clearly heard someone shouting:

- Kill the nobles, kill all the nobles!

We met a group of soldiers dragging some women, even though these people screamed and cried bitterly.

Piere said in panic:

- God, everyone is crazy.

Mr. Daniel calmly said:

- Find a way to avoid it, you must return to the theater immediately.

We headed towards the field where the troupe's convoy was setting up camp. Coming closer, Daniel shouted loudly:

- Remove the camp. Leave here now.

Alfonso was surprised:

- Have you two met Jean's father?

Daniel replied breathlessly:

- Let's talk about this later. It's not safe here, you have to leave now. Go now!

Everyone panicked and hurriedly packed everything up and spurred their horses out of Verden. Just walking a short distance, we encountered a group of soldiers searching and robbing the fleeing people. The sound of people crying echoed loudly. Before we could turn the car in another direction, a soldier saw it and shouted loudly:

- Look, it's the Gitan, arrest them immediately.

Alfonso quickly pulled his horse in another direction to find a way out, but the soldiers rushed in. Gilbert and Daniel drew their swords to resist, giving the troupe a chance to escape. I also quickly jumped out of the car to provide reinforcements. Gilbert couldn't hold out for long. After throwing all the knives on his body, he was hit by several spears. Daniel, who was more skilled in combat, defeated a few soldiers, but was then surrounded by other aggressive soldiers. I had no experience in fighting, so as soon as I rushed in, I was hit by several spears, blood pouring out. A soldier spurred his horse forward, causing me to fall to the ground. He turned his horse around and attempted to deliver another fatal blow, but at that moment, I jumped up, grabbed his arm, and pulled him to the ground. Taking advantage, I jumped up and clung to the horse's neck. The horse jumped up and ran like crazy away from the fighting crowd. I couldn't hold the horse back, it continued to pass people running around on the road. Maybe because I lost too much blood, my mind became dizzy, my consciousness gradually disappeared, and then I didn't know anything anymore...

***

The Holy War or Crusades were a series of religious wars waged by Christian nations against Muslims in the Middle East and North Africa. The goal was to retake Jerusalem and the area around it, the so-called Holy Land. This is an area that is always in a state of tension because it is considered the Holy Land of all three religions: Islam, Judaism and Christianity.

Most historical documents of the Middle Ages (Middle Age) were written by European historians, so they are more or less biased. Many people believe that the Holy War was a just war, liberating Jerusalem from Muslim control. Although Pope John Paul II expressed regret over what happened in the past, when Christians and Muslims slaughtered each other, to this day many people still argue about this war that lasted nearly three centuries. Looking at the historical context at that time, we can see that after the fall of the Roman Empire, the whole of Europe fell into recession and chaos. Chaos and disorder occurred everywhere as kings and lords fought against each other to compete for land and power. The two powerful countries at that time, England and France, went through wars with many losses. Both countries' national treasuries were depleted, the economy declined, crops failed, and people's dissatisfaction increased because of high revenues and heavy taxes. Meanwhile, the Muslim empire consisting of many tribes united by religious power, stretching from India to Spain, was in a period of prosperity, controlling trade and commerce from Asia such as China, India and Bactria. Urban areas such as Cairo, Baghdad, and Damascus have become bustling and bustling commercial centers. People from all over come here to form a prosperous society. All activities such as literature, poetry, music and science also developed widely.

At that time, the Muslim Seljuks were expanding their power in Asia Minor, so the Christians of the Byzantine Empire (Eastern Roman Empire) called for aid from Western Europe. Pope Urban II immediately called for a military war to expel the pagans from the Holy Land. The soldiers participating in the war all wore red cross shirts, known as crusaders. There were eight major Holy Wars, lasting nearly three centuries, and hundreds of small wars in the border areas to control the road from Europe to Jerusalem.

In addition, Jerusalem is the holy land of Judaism. Jewish legend believes that this is the place King David chose to build the temple in the 10th century BC. This location is also extremely important to Christians, because this is where Jesus was born, preached, crucified and resurrected. Jerusalem also holds significance in Islam as it was the entry point to heaven for the prophet Muhammad, whom Muslims believe is the most important prophet of Allah. Since Muslims appeared in the Holy Land in the 7th century, this land has always been a tense place with constant tensions and disputes between these religions.

THE FIRST CRUSADE (1096 - 1099)

At that time, Christians making pilgrimages to Jerusalem often encountered bandits that European history books called Muslims. Pope Urban II, responding to a call for aid from the Byzantine Empire, convened a Council at Clermont calling on European kingdoms to send troops to liberate the Holy Land from the pagans. This is also an opportunity for the kings of European kingdoms to temporarily put aside old disputes because they have a common enemy. While the royal court was preparing for war, religious fervor caused the people, mostly farmers and workers, to automatically arm themselves to liberate the Holy Land. This ragtag group was severely massacred by the Muslim army. Despite many failures, many small wars continued continuously for three years with many factions participating. Finally, the victorious expedition marched into Jerusalem, slaughtering most of the Muslims and Jews there. Godfrey, one of the generals of the expedition, was appointed king but he refused this title, because he did not want to wear a golden crown in the country where Jesus had to wear a crown of thorns. Godfrey was later named Guardian of the Holy Sepulchre (Advocatus Sancti Sepulchri). Other leaders also occupied surrounding lands, establishing small kingdoms known collectively as Crusader states (Crusader states).

THE SECOND CRUSADE (1146 - 1149)

After the First Crusade regained Jerusalem, Western Europeans from everywhere increasingly flocked to the Holy Land for pilgrimage. In the name of protecting these pilgrims, an army called The Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon was founded in 1118 in France. This group later changed its name to the Knights Templar (Knights Templar) and was later recognized as a religious order. This force achieved many victories during the Crusades, so they quickly built up power, accumulated a lot of gold and silver, and became rich. The war between this force and the Muslims continued for many years, causing damage to both sides. Islamic history books write that the Knights Templar did not allow Muslims to make pilgrimages to Jerusalem, which Muslims consider a holy place, and often killed these people. In 1144, the Muslim army rose and recaptured Edessa, an important city. Saint Bernard, the most important spiritual leader of the European Christian community at the time, personally called for the Second Crusade. The European court immediately responded, especially King Conrad III of Germany and Louis VII of France even went personally. This was the Crusade officially led by the European court. However, because they were not familiar with the rugged desert terrain and could not control the wells, the Second Crusade was a major failure for the West, with the number of deaths reaching several tens of thousands. The Second Crusade was an absolute victory for the Muslims, it also produced the most powerful enemy of Christianity and the most revered defender of Islam – Saladin (Salah ad-Din). In 1187, the Muslims recaptured Jerusalem.

THE THIRD CRUSADE (1189 - 1192)

The Muslim Empire under the command of Saladin recaptured Jerusalem, destroyed the surrounding Crusader kingdoms and took complete control of the region. Hearing the news, Pope Gregory VIII called for a Third Crusade to reclaim Jerusalem. In 1188, King Frederick I of the Holy Roman Empire, Philip II of France, Henry II of England and Richard (Henry's son) took the oath to join the Crusade. The French and British troops, due to internal suspicions, delayed sending troops, while Frederick I's expeditionary army soon disbanded when the king died. King Henry II also died before departing, so only King Philip II of France and Richard I arrived in Jerusalem. King Philip II then returned home, leaving behind his army, while Richard I still tried to regain Jerusalem. However, in 1192, hearing about domestic unrest, Richard I was forced to sign an agreement with Saladin and return to England. Once again the Europeans failed to recapture Jerusalem. This war caused heavy losses to European countries both financially and socially. However, taking advantage of the people's enthusiasm for serving religion, the kings still opened more wars for the purpose of appropriation rather than liberation. The clearest evidence is that they allowed the Knights Templar group to have full control over collecting the spoils of war. Later, these people also became greedy. Instead of bringing it back to the court and the church, they secretly hid a lot of gold and silver and became rich. Over time, this group became a very influential tycoon force, so Pope Clement V had to order its disbandment. However, they still operated silently for centuries as a secret organization controlling all financial and commercial activities of Europe.

FOURTH CRUSES (1202 - 1204)

Pope Innocent III ascended the papal throne in 1198 and he set the goal of restarting a new Holy War. However, his call was not paid attention to by European kings because at this time the economies of European countries fell into severe recession and people's dissatisfaction rose. England and France were still fighting, while Germany was struggling to eliminate papal influence. However, in the end the Crusader army was still formed and deployed from Venice, with forces mainly coming from French regions. The Fourth Crusade ultimately became a campaign to seize money and property to replenish treasuries depleted by years of war. Instead of entering Jerusalem, this force entered Constantinople, the ancient capital of the Roman Empire, where most people followed Christianity and where all trade with Eastern countries was concentrated. The Crusaders committed terrible crimes in Constantinople, destroying and stealing many Ancient and Medieval works of Rome and Greece. Despite their oath and the threat of excommunication, the Crusaders destroyed the city's monastic churches, desecrated and plundered everything they could get their hands on...

THE FIFTH CRUSES (1215 - 1221)

Despite the failure of the Fourth Crusade, which succeeded only in destroying Christian cities, Pope Innocent III and his successor Pope Honorius III continued to call for a Fifth Crusade. Pope Innocent III assured that he had control over this war but he died before the war began. The Fifth Crusade had many warring parties with many different purposes, notably Hungary (led by King Andrew II), France, Germany, the Eastern Roman Empire, the Holy Roman Empire... Instead of attacking Jerusalem, these forces attacked Egypt, under the powerful Ayyubid dynasty. In most of the engagements, the Crusaders failed to win. In addition, the outbreak of disease caused the Crusaders to lose troops. The climax was when marching to Cairo, the rising Nile River caused heavy losses to the Crusaders, forcing them to surrender and withdraw their troops. Once again the Fifth Crusade was a complete failure.

SIXTH CRUSES (1228 - 1229)

The Sixth Crusade was led by Emperor Frederick II of the Holy Roman Empire with a large army. Taking advantage of the time when the court was busy suppressing rebel forces in Syria, Frederick II successfully regained Jerusalem through negotiations and then proclaimed himself king of Jerusalem without the approval of the Church. Afraid of being excommunicated, he returned to Europe to reconcile with Pope Gregory IX. A few years later, Jerusalem again fell under the control of Muslim forces.

THE SEVENTH Crusade (1248 - 1254)

After Jerusalem fell to Muslim forces in 1244, King Louis IX of France planned to conduct the Seventh Crusade, the target still being Egypt. After being ordered by Pope Innocent IV in 1248, King Louis IX of France led the Crusaders to land in Egypt, conquering Damietta, a major trade center. However, Muslim forces counterattacked, capturing King Louis IX alive, forcing the French court to ransom him with a huge sum of money and return Damietta. Therefore this Crusade was also a costly disaster.

THE EIGHTH CRUSADE (1270)

Even though the Seventh Crusade was unsuccessful, King Louis IX's greed for appropriating gold mines made him ask permission to lead the Eighth Crusade, targeting Tunisia and Morocco with many natural resources such as copper mines and gold mines. The Eighth Crusade ended when King Louis fell ill and died in Tunis. The remaining Crusaders under the command of King Edward I of England advanced deep into North Africa as far as the city of Acre but were also completely destroyed by the Muslims.

OTHER CRUSES

In 1291, Sultan Qalawun laid siege to Acre, ending the existence of the last independent Christian city-state in the Holy Land. Qalawun died in this siege, but his son Al-Ashraf Khalil ascended the throne and continued the eradication of European remnants in the Middle East. This was considered the end of the Crusade movement in the Holy Land, but greed motivated subsequent generations of kings and descendants to take advantage of religious fervor and send troops around the world to wage war against people of different religions, but the real purpose was only to loot and appropriate the property of other countries.

In parallel with the Crusades to the Holy Land, many military campaigns in the name of religion to other lands are sometimes called Crusades by historians, for example the Northern Crusade - against pagans in the Baltic region, or the military campaign against the Albi sect in France...

***

Economically, trade with Muslim tribes in Palestine and Syria opened up a large commercial field through trade. selling and exchanging goods with Asian countries. While European kingdoms focused on war, Italian merchants in Genoa and Venice quickly seized the golden opportunity, building large ships to transport goods everywhere as well as establishing a powerful navy to control all sea routes in the Mediterranean. Italian traders brought Europeans novel, high-value goods such as silk, spices and precious metals, creating a thirst for the products and produce of the Asian kingdoms. According to historical documents, ships carrying goods from the Middle East to Europe were the cause of the plague pandemic (Black Death) that killed more than a third of the European population. History clearly states that the epidemic started in China, passed through the Middle East and then spread to Europe through booty collected and transported on ships from the Middle East to Europe.

In ancient times, the Silk Road was the main transportation route leading through Asia. This road was under Muslim control, so the Europeans began looking for a new road. From there, European nations began competing for control of trade through Asia. Gradually, their goal turned into an adventure to explore far away places with new resources. Prince Henry of Portugal led a group of ships along the African coast, found a new sea route through Asia and opened the colonial era in which Europeans disguised themselves in the name of enlightening barbarian peoples.

Colonialism is the policy of controlling conquered areas, called colonies, with the purpose of economic and social domination through the process of imposing European religion, language and cultural practices on the people of the colonies. The main goal was to find ways to profit from the labor of the people as well as the resources in the colonies, bringing wealth to their country.

Historians give three main motives of Europeans when colonizing Asian and American countries: God, gold and glory (God, gold, glory). The Crusades used religion to justify war with Muslim countries, but now religion is applied to this colonization policy. The hatred from the Crusades led to religious intolerance towards peoples of different religions. Later, European countries turned to using the guise of religious conquest to reinforce their colonization policy to bring wealth and prosperity to their countries.

Children, love everyone as you love yourself.

tieu_de: Part Eight: Karmic Affinity - God is Love
noi_dung:
PART EIGHT

DESTINY

GOD IS LOVE

When I woke up, although my mind was still dizzy, I realized I was lying in bed. Sitting next to the bed was an elderly clergyman looking at me intently. Looking at his clothes, I guessed he was a bishop. Seeing that I was awake, that person signaled me to lie still. I whispered, feeling my throat hurt:

- Where are everyone... in the troupe?

The bishop slowly said:

- Don't worry, the danger is over. Lie still, don't move.

I panicked:

- Soldiers... There are soldiers...

The bishop replied:

- Rest assured, the Cathedral is a sacred place, no soldiers can enter here.

Even though my whole body was in indescribable pain, there was something very dear in the bishop's voice, making me feel very reassured. I tried to raise my head to look at him, but the pain came back and I fainted.

I don't know how long I lay in bed. Because the wound was quite serious, I was awake and asleep, but I knew someone was taking care of me and bandaging my wound.

It seemed like I lay there for a long time, until, in a daze, I suddenly heard a bell ringing and a deep prayer echoing. Suddenly my whole body felt comfortable. I opened my eyes, found myself fully awake and able to move easily. I sat up and looked through the window, it was dim outside because it wasn't quite bright yet. As if motivated by something, I tried to get out of bed and was excited to see that I could walk again. I listened to the sound of prayer, then pushed the door open and walked out, following the warm sound to the cathedral. Under the flickering candlelight, the priests were praying. Seeing that, I quickly knelt down and read along. The prayer went on for quite a long time, and when everyone stopped, the sun had already risen. Looking at the sunlight through the window, I knew it was almost noon.

When everyone stood up to leave, the old bishop saw me so he walked over and asked:

- Are you awake? Are you feeling better yet?

I nodded and timidly asked:

- Sir, why am I here?

The bishop smiled gently, his blue eyes sparkling:

- Someone saw you injured, lying unconscious at the edge of the forest, so they brought you here.

I asked:

- Where is this? How are the soldiers and opera troupe?

The bishop shook his head:

- I don't understand what you're saying, but this is a safe place, you don't have to worry about anything.

Today I saw this old bishop clearly, I felt that he had something very familiar to him. While I was still trying to think about where this feeling of familiarity came from, he spoke up, his eyes looking at me radiated kindness and sincerity:

- I'm very happy to see you again. Your injury is very serious, now you need to rest for a while longer and then we will talk more.

Did you just say see you again me? From childhood to adulthood, I never had contact with any clergy other than the priest in the village. While traveling with the troupe, I visited many places to perform, but I never met any clergy. I was about to ask more but the bishop looked at me, smiled strangely and leisurely walked away. I didn't know anyone else here, so I quickly followed him into the dining room.

After the meal, the bishop offered to take me for a walk to familiarize myself with the situation. I followed him out into the yard. This is a small monastery built of stone, located in the forest, hidden under the canopy of ancient trees so the air is very cool. The space here is extremely quiet, occasionally there is the sweet sound of birds singing mixed with the whispering wind, a scene that can soothe the soul. The bishop said:

- You can rest here for a while until your wound heals. However, everyone here is dedicated to praying, so you should also be careful to keep quiet. If you want, you can join us in praying.

I said immediately:

- Thank you, sir, but I need to go to Verden to find a theater company. A few days ago, my theater troupe was robbed. I don't know how everyone is doing now.

The bishop shook his head:

- Verden is very far from here. To get there you have to go through a dense forest. You should wait until your wound heals completely before leaving.

Although I was anxious about the fate of the troupe, I also knew that I could not go far with such a serious injury, so I had to stay at the monastery. Every day, I follow the missionaries to pray. What surprised me was that the prayer ceremony here was different from the ceremonies I had attended. There are prayer sessions that take place from morning until late at night. I was very surprised but didn't dare to ask anything but just tried to follow. After a week, I presented my questions to the bishop. He replied:

- We practice according to God's teachings to purify our bodies and minds for purity and perfection, not just following the usual rituals like other places. Perhaps you don't know, in the past, for the purpose of developing religion and expanding the laity, the clergy narrowed noble truths and simplified everything so that everyone could understand. However, this has lost the essence that God taught. What He taught was not limited to faith but was much more noble. Therefore, here we practice the ritual of constant prayer to reconnect with Him.

Seeing my bewildered face, the bishop added:

- We follow His teachings, Be perfect as your Father in heaven is perfect (S. Matt 5.48). Many clergy believe that this is impossible because humans are sinners, so how can they become perfect? Therefore, they ignored this precious teaching and gradually created a gap between humans and God. Who knows that if we try hard, we can still overcome our base nature and become purer and purer.

I'm confused:

- I've never heard that there is anything else besides faith.

The bishop nodded and replied:

- That's right, some clergy have simplified everything, lowering the noble essence that God teaches to a level that even an uneducated and foolish person can understand. They believe that believers only need to believe, not understand, because they take care of everything. The majority of the people did not know how to read or write, but only the clergy and nobles were taught to read and write. Therefore, they have full authority to teach and interpret the meaning of God's teachings according to their own wishes. This raised the clergy into a class with absolute power, becoming intermediaries between humans and God. Faith is necessary, but if you believe, you must learn to clearly understand His noble teachings, not simply believe, and once you understand, you must practice according to what is taught. If you just believe without understanding and not practicing the teachings but just waiting for God's help, it is just an unreasonable belief.

I wonder:

- I don't understand, if they want to develop religion, why do they have to simplify the essence?

The bishop explained:

- The path to the Kingdom of Heaven has many different high and low steps because everyone is not at the same level of understanding. Cognitive and action capacities must also change depending on this evolutionary scale. People reach high levels thanks to their insight and pure virtue. Therefore, what is taught must also be adapted to each person's level, reason and understanding. In ancient times, God taught a lot about practical methods to unite the human spirit with the spiritual realm so that God is all in all (I. Cor 15.28). Praying without ceasing is one of those methods.

The bishop looked at me attentively and added:

- Likewise, God teaches God is love. This is the absolute, undeniable truth. Because love is an essential condition to maintain harmony between people, without love it will lead to the strong oppressing the weak, the strong winning and the weak losing. The essence of what God teaches lies in these two words love, but nowadays people ignore it and call for discrimination, hatred, competition, and appropriation. Are these things according to God's will? God's will is never like that.

I think about the days spent wandering with the troupe, witnessing so many unfair and unreasonable things in life, things that made me dissatisfied and skeptical. Surely God's will will never be like that. I thought about it and asked the bishop:

- So, according to you, what is the difference between human love and God's love?

The bishop smiled gently and explained:

- Human love and God's love are only different in degree, the essence is still the same. Love is like water, flowing everywhere. God's love is like a vast and endless ocean, while human love is like a small stream flowing through the earth. When people know how to love is when they return to God and when they love sincerely and without demands is when the stream begins to merge into the sea. God has taught You should love everyone as you love yourself. The more clearly we understand the meaning of what is taught, the more we believe. If you believe like that, you must practice according to the teachings and the more you apply, the more you will believe. In short, it is impossible to just believe without doing anything. If you believe, you must find out the meaning of the teachings to follow and put them into practice. You cannot say that you believe but act differently or just believe and leave it at that.

I think of the greedy and tyrannical actions of the lords. On the one hand, they built many cathedrals to demonstrate their religious faith to the Church, but on the other hand, they continued to exploit, oppress and appropriate everything to enjoy material benefits and comforts. They believe that no matter what they do, in the end God will still let them go to heaven.

When I lived with a theater group, I often heard Mona read the Bible and she once told me that there was a person who came to ask God how to enjoy perfect life in Heaven. He answered: Keep the commandments. I really like this simple teaching because when I was little, my grandmother always reminded me to Respect God; love people; not greedy; do not kill.... But while living the life of a gangster, I witnessed many people acting completely contrary to these commandments. I wonder why many people believe in God, respect Him and know that He teaches to love each other, but not many people can do this? What the Crusaders did when liberating the Holy Land was to kill, plunder, and loot property for the royal court. I don't understand how they can use God's name and do such evil things.

I told the bishop my thoughts. He listened and then calmly said:

- Maybe Mona hasn't told her the whole story yet. When hearing God teach about keeping the commandments, the other person replied, You have kept all of these since you were a child, is there anything else you have not done?. To such obedient people, God further teaches, If you want to become perfect, sell all your possessions, give to the poor, and you will have a treasure in heaven, and then come here to me. Hearing that, the man went away sad because he had a lot of wealth.

I was surprised:

- I don't quite understand. Why do we have to do that to reach Him?

The bishop explained:

- If you want to be perfect, that is, become a person of the Kingdom of Heaven, you must know how to let go of all material things, maintain a poor, pure and obedient lifestyle. This means that we should not be attached to material possessions but should only consider ourselves as their stewards. Material wealth can come and go, as a manager of them, we use them when they come but do not regret when they go, because these things cannot be compared to the treasures of the Kingdom of Heaven. This teaching is very clear because God later explained further: It is difficult for a rich person to enter the kingdom of Heaven, even more difficult for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle (Matt 19:16:26). Why? Because man cannot serve two masters at the same time. Either worship money or worship God.

I recounted what Pierre said about the Holy War, the old bishop shook his head:

- Those are the people who dishonored God, they took advantage of the name of the Church and the people's ignorance to seek power and wealth for themselves. They are greedy and selfish people who only worship money and power. No matter how much you repent or atone for your sins, you cannot get them back. If they know the commandments Do not be greedy, do not take from others, do not kill but still violate them, then they do not deserve to be called children of God.

From then on, every day, after praying with everyone in the monastery, I often walked in the yard with the old bishop to receive further instructions from him. Thanks to that, I learned many things that I was not taught before. Being able to answer my old questions about faith and obeying the commandments has helped my heart expand. According to the bishop, faith is the key to opening the door to the Kingdom of Heaven, but entering it requires practice. Prayer is about knowing God and coming to Him, not just simply believing. The purpose of life is to realize that unity, so faith alone is not enough, we must also clearly understand the teachings and put them into practice. Only when our body and mind are clean and pure can we come to Him. Therefore, the monks at this monastery always keep the commandments and pray constantly.

When we keep the commandment not to kill, we will eliminate the mind of fighting and appropriating and will thus help us respect life. By keeping the commandment not to steal or take from others, it will eliminate greed and possessiveness and help us respect justice. When we keep the commandment not fornication, we will eliminate the desire for satisfaction and thus help us build affection and relationships between people. Once we know how to respect others, we cannot hurt anyone. By keeping the commandment not lying, it will eliminate cunning and greed and will thus help us to be careful with our words and only speak the truth. When we keep the commandment to honor our parents, we will eliminate selfishness and arrogance and will thus help us develop deep gratitude to those who gave birth, raised and taught us. Once people keep these commandments, they will change, become clean, pure, understand beautiful things and will have the treasures of heaven. Once you know what the treasures of heaven are like, all the material things of this world will no longer have any meaning.

One of the walks with the bishop, I mentioned the chaos and death everywhere and asked him if humanity could overcome this calamity. He pondered for a moment then leisurely said:

- Let me tell you a story. Once upon a time, there was a strange disease that made everyone's stomachs swell as if they were about to explode. Everyone was extremely scared but didn't know how to cure it. Until one day, a doctor came from far away with a bottle of medicine to cure this disease. He said: Everyone, listen here, anyone who wants to be cured of their illness must follow the correct usage method that I teach because tomorrow I will leave for another place. He carefully instructed how to use it and what dosage to take, then left the bottle of medicine for everyone. After he left, everyone gathered and started arguing. One person asks the question: where did that doctor come from, who did he learn medicine from, how talented he is, and what is his background? Why did you come here and what was your purpose? Others question whether they should believe in that medicine or not, what if they take it and their illness gets worse? So many questions were debated about that doctor. They argued all day and then forgot all the doctor's teachings. The medicine bottle is still there but no one knows how to use it.

The bishop stopped to let me think about the story and then concluded:

- Blessed are those who believe, understand and follow.

Looking at the bewildered look on my face, he smiled and added:

- Do you know what that strange disease is? It is that disease of greed. The current chaotic situation comes from the shaking of people's faith. They abandoned the commandments and abandoned their faith. Even if the cure is right in front of you, not many people will see it.

I lived at the monastery for a while, and my wound gradually healed. Every day I still follow the clergy to pray. At first, praying lasted too long and made me tired, but after a while, I put all my heart and soul into praying so I felt time passed easily, just like a split second. Many times I pray from morning to night and still feel comfortable. The old bishop seemed satisfied with this, he said:

- Put all your heart in God, don't think about anything and you will receive unexpected blessings.
