When His image manifests clearly in my heart, I will completely forget the illusion of my own me, and I will see love and charity flooding everywhere. Prayer is a fire that refines every molecule in a person, helping to purify and prepare for clarity, calmness, and purity, like a flower gradually blooming under the light of the sun. To serve God, you must become a center to transport that blessing, promoting good influence everywhere. As you can see, all the people living here are disciplined, live simply, and clean themselves to serve God. Whatever you think or do, it contains and reflects love and charity to everyone. That is also the purpose of practicing here. In the past, God taught a lot and some things were recorded in books, but books by themselves do not bring us closer to Him. What we need is to live in such a way that life has a positive and beautiful meaning as He has instructed.

Relaxing and practicing at the same time helps me not only recover quickly but also change my personality. I began to feel peace in this tumultuous life. Until one time, while praying, I suddenly felt my whole body become strangely calm as if I had been raised to a certain level. Although the candlelight in the room flickered dimly, I could somehow see everything around me clearly.

I saw the clergy sincerely praying, then my eyes widened from the Cathedral to the forest outside with rows of tall ancient trees. My vision rose higher and higher and suddenly I saw a group of Gitan camping in a dense forest. I saw the two carriages of the Alfonso troupe and several other carriages that I did not recognize, all gathered in a large circle. I saw Mona and Ella sitting gloomily in the car while Pedro and two other young men were cleaning musical instruments nearby. These images appeared clearly in my mind until the prayer ended.

Prayer is a fire that refines every molecule in a person, helping to purify and prepare for clarity, calmness, and purity, like a flower gradually blooming under the light of the sun.

That night, I couldn't sleep because I kept thinking about those strange images. Suddenly, I thought of Ella and her feelings for me. Many times Ella secretly sang me gentle love songs that she composed just for me, but my heart was not moved. Once Pedro hunted a hare, Ella saved the best part for me, but that made me feel uncomfortable so I decided not to eat it. Ella therefore couldn't hold back her tears. There were times when I suddenly felt like I hated Ella and said harsh words to her. Gilbert was so surprised by my attitude that he once pulled me aside to a corner of the forest and scolded me. At that time, I argued with him that I was not a Gitan but had only lived with them until I met my father. If I were raised and educated by my father, I would become a noble, I would no longer have any relationship with this troupe and Gitan people like Ella. Gilbert looked at me very strangely, then shook his head, showing disappointment:

- I didn't expect you to think like that. How can you think you belong to the aristocracy and then look down on Gitan people, when we already consider you as family?

Since that time Gilbert was more distant from me than before even though he still taught me. Actually, I don't understand why I have such thoughts? Why do I think I am greater and more important than the Gitan people even though I live with them like a family?

I was exhausted thinking about these things and fell asleep. Just as I fell asleep, Ella suddenly appeared again, but this time I heard her say: Jean, save me, don't leave me. This statement created a strange shock in my mind. In a dream, I felt the ground shake violently and then large streams of water came from somewhere. I saw a girl in tattered clothes trying to hold my hand in that flood water. Suddenly, I saw clearly that the girl was Ella. A strange scene appeared in my mind and I clearly heard a loud cry: I will not leave you. I sat up startled, my chest pounding continuously. At that moment, I knew I had to return to find Ella.

The next day, I went to see the bishop to say goodbye to him. After listening to my presentation, he was silent for a long time, then looked at me sadly:

- Why can you be so confused? Having practiced so much, we still let trivial things drag us away. If we don't wake up and keep stepping into that place of gossip, who knows when we will be able to escape?

At that time, I didn't understand what he was saying because I was anxious to quickly find the troupe and Ella. I bowed my head and whispered:

- I thank you for saving me and teaching me in the past. But the time has come for me to return to the theater to meet the person I love.

The bishop felt sad:

- It's a pity, I've tried, but the old connections still bind you too strongly... You and I have known each other for a long time. I still follow you to help you, but you don't know and you don't make any progress.

I was surprised:

- Sir, what do you say I don't understand? Since when have we known each other? If we've known each other for a long time, why don't you remember anything?

The bishop sighed and said:

- What I say you may not understand right now, because your mind is affected by events in your current life. Last night, I remembered some things that happened a long time ago as well as relationships that were related to each other from before, that's because I inherently have this ability. However, just like before, when you are not aware of who you are, where you come from, what lessons you have experienced, what you have learned and what you have not learned, you have lost many valuable opportunities to learn. Then you will have to learn those lessons over and over again until you truly understand to be able to accept other lessons. There are things that saying it now won't change anything because your mind can't understand it yet. You have forgotten the lesson you learned in the past and has been obscured by other factors, so even if I explain it to you, you cannot understand it. Well, let's go...

Even though I was very curious about what the bishop said, even though I had many questions inside that needed to be answered, right now I really wanted to see Ella again. I had to say goodbye to the bishop, promising him that I would find a chance to return to see him. I left the monastery and headed towards Verden at my fastest speed, but after several days I still couldn't reach my destination. That day, the sun had just set. I was looking for a place to rest for the night when I met a Gitan setting animal traps nearby. He saw me and immediately asked:

- Kid, who are you? Why are you wandering around in the woods at this time?

I replied:

- I am a member of the Alfonso troupe, I have been lost for a long time.

He looked at me intently and then shook his head:

- Alfonso's singing troupe is no longer there, now there is only Moreno's singing troupe.

Foreseeing something bad, I asked:

- What do you mean by that? What happened?

That person explained:

- Alfonso's troupe encountered an accident, many people were killed, in the end only five people survived. Alfonso lost all his property, musical instruments, and performance equipment, so he could not make a living and had to join Moreno's theater troupe. If you're Alfonso's man, just go east about half a mile and you'll find him.

I followed the instructions and walked a short distance when I heard music echoing from afar. I happily walked towards the sound of music and saw a group of Gitan gathering around a large fire. Through the lyrics and singing, I knew they were holding a wedding. I slowly walked closer and heard someone say that it was Moreno's wedding day. At that moment, there was loud applause, a middle-aged man in the car got out, looking at his clothes and the white towel wrapped around his waist, I knew it was the groom. The music played loudly, then the two people in the back slowly walked out. I was startled to realize that Alfonso was walking next to a young woman with many flowers in her hair. My eyes widened, I blurted out loudly:

- Ella!

My whole body was shocked, my mind was spinning, I had never felt my heart beat so strongly. Gilbert's old words suddenly rang out: Don't lose this opportunity. I clenched my hands to try to stay calm, but my whole body was still shaking with emotion. I understand that because Alfonso lost all his musical instruments and tools to make a living, he had to apply to be merged with another theater troupe. Because Moreno is the leader, everything must follow his orders. If he is unmarried or widowed, he can ask to marry Ella. According to Gitan customs, marriage is entirely based on the parents' decision.

I heard in my head Ella's passionate cry in the dream the day before: Brother Jean, save me, please don't leave me. At that moment, in front of the fire, Alfonso took Ella's hand and placed it in Moreno's hand and solemnly announced the beginning of the wedding. This is an important moment. If no one objects, the wedding will be held. As if motivated by some force, I shouted loudly:

- I oppose this marriage!

My scream surprised everyone, the music stopped, all eyes turned to me. Moreno was surprised:

- What? Who are you?

There was a stir, the crowd simultaneously shouted:

- Challenge! Challenge!

According to Gitan customs, when there is a dispute that cannot be resolved, there will be a challenge period between the two people to determine the winner.

Ella broke away from Moreno's hand and cried loudly:

- Mr. Jean, Mr. Jean... no way.

Alfonso was also surprised:

- Jean, are you still alive?

A Gitan came out holding two short knives and handed them to me and Moreno. He took off the white towel wrapped around his waist, picked up the knife and smiled faintly:

- Guy, are you ready?

Alfonso walked right up to me:

- Jean, you have to apologize right away. Moreno is the leader of the troupe, you cannot embarrass him.

At that time, I no longer had enough reason, my whole body seemed to be controlled by a strange force. I reached out to take the short knife and walked in front of Moreno. Alfonso grabbed my hand but I pushed him away. Seeing this, Ella shouted loudly:

- Mr. Jean! No way, no way!

One person pulled Ella behind and held her tightly. The fight happened very quickly, Moreno was a skilled knife user, in just a few seconds he stabbed me several times. Despite my wound, I still fought back, but just a few minutes later, he prevailed, pushing me close to the fire. Suddenly, I stepped on a piece of wood and staggered. Moreno took advantage of it and swung the knife and stabbed me in the chest, causing me to collapse. Moreno gave me a few more blows until I could no longer stand up. Moreno stepped back and laughed:

- With such talent, you dare to challenge me?

My eyes became dizzy and gradually blurred, my strength was gone, I let go of the knife. Ella jumped up and ran to me and tried to lift me up. I smiled:

- Ella, I won't leave you but... it's late... I'm sorry...

Ella leaned down and placed a kiss on my lips and whispered:

- You know I won't leave you alone no matter what.

Suddenly, Mona cried loudly:

- No... no!

I clearly felt a hot liquid spraying into my chest and heard Ella's voice:

- Mr. Jean, let's go together!

I tried to open my eyes and saw Ella holding the handle of a short knife, but the blade had pierced her chest, blood pouring out and drenching my body. She said weakly:

- I will... follow you forever!

My breathing became weaker but I still tried my best to hold Ella's hand tightly:

- Okay, let's go together... together, never apart!

***

When talking about his life in France, Thomas also talked about the development of Christianity at that time. As a Christian, he had a special interest in this period, a period he described as the dark period.

According to Thomas, although God's teachings are still spread, some essences have been lost because they are no longer talked about or taught. The reason is that during the Middle Ages (Middle Age), when the teachings of God were transmitted from the Middle East to Europe, the level of the people at that time was still low, those who could read, write and were educated were only a minority. If the entire teachings are taught to the masses, uneducated and low-level people cannot comprehend them, so some clergy have simplified the teachings and lowered it to make it suitable for the majority of people. The sublime essences were only taught to a small group of carefully selected people, but over time, they were more or less lost.

He said: I know many people do not agree with this, because they believe that everything that needs to be taught has already been said or written down. Some clergymen assert that there is nothing else besides what is recorded in the Bible, that the magic of the Bible is in its simplicity that anyone can read and understand. But it is a mistake if people only know the things that are recorded and do not talk about the things that are not recorded, the things that are only taught within a limited scope.

The teachings of God were described very clearly by Origen, the first scholar of the Church. That when God taught the people, He used many parables to teach. Besides those parables, He did not say anything else. And when He was alone, the twelve apostles asked Him about these parables. Then He explained everything to them and said that parables are given to you to understand the mystery of the Kingdom of Heaven, but to outsiders everything is just parables, so they look but do not see, hear but do not understand, but only those who understand and repent will be forgiven (S. Mark 4:10,11, 33, 34). Mark emphasized the verses when He was alone and to outsiders implying that some of the superior elites were taught privately only to close disciples, because their level was higher than the level of the majority of the people at that time. Even to the disciples, He also said: I have many more things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now (St John 16:12).

In the Middle Ages, monks simplified many of His profound teachings and lost their transcendent essence, and today, some monks simplify even more.

Many things taught today are completely different from what God taught in the past. Can one follow a religion without truly understanding its teachings? Faith and a deep understanding of the meaning of the teachings are essential. Therefore, a true religion must require learning and carefully studying the teachings to apply it to life to bring happiness to people, not just mere belief. If you just believe without studying and researching carefully, it is easy to go down the path of superstition, error, and fall prey to those who take advantage of religion for personal gain. Nowadays, there are many evil cults appearing everywhere, with clergy who are eloquent and persuasive, attracting a large number of followers. They collected some basic teachings but modified and taught them differently in order to attract and attract the masses and give themselves certain authorities.

Not many people know how to question the purpose of religions. Is religion spread to promote the evolution of humanity, returning to its divine roots? The problem is that each place and each region has different cultures, customs and languages, so it is impossible to propose a single religion for all. That's why there are many different religions appearing in different places. Human evolution can be seen as a long ladder from bottom to top, with people on each step. People at high levels will be different from people at low levels. Therefore, teaching must also depend on each person's level and understanding. The sublime and wonderful things reserved for noble people are incomprehensible to foolish people. In the same way, a basic teaching that is suitable for beginners will become insipid to someone with profound understanding. Therefore, every religion has many different levels depending on the level of the believer. Otherwise, it will not achieve its goal of developing wisdom and understanding.

However, whether it is the deepest or the simplest, the most profound meaning for every religion or spiritual belief is to develop love and charity. If any religion or believer goes against these two criteria, it is a mistake. Cause and effect is a signpost for people to return to goodness. By thoroughly understanding this law, our world will be filled with the light of love. Ultimately, unconditional love is the path that leads us to absolute freedom and harmony with the Supreme Being.

The life in France was also the last memorable life that Thomas told me. He also briefly said that he later returned for a few short lives to learn his lessons. Not every life he was wise and had the opportunity to awaken, but he gradually found his path, the path of spiritual development, spiritual connection and consciousness transformation. Thomas and I continued to have conversations to talk about his karma in this life, about the things he was doing and the things he had realized.

tieu_de: Part Nine: The Gift Economy - Seeds of Goodness
noi_dung:
PART NINE

THE GIFT ECONOMY

SEEDS OF GOODNESS

Recently, on a business trip to Chicago, I called my old friend, billionaire Farnum, whom I had recently met again, and asked to visit him. The billionaire happily invited me out to eat. Instead of going to luxury restaurants, suitable for my status, Farnum took me to a popular restaurant, with a large number of people lined up in front of the door waiting for their turn to dine.

Looking at the simple display and the restaurant's name Karma Kitchen, I thought to myself that perhaps this is an Indian restaurant with special dishes that Farnum likes. When the menu was presented, I was surprised because it was all common dishes, nothing special or new. Farnum chose the dish and then looked at me and smiled. I tried not to show my surprise and chose the dish. We chatted about recent hot topics until the dishes were brought. The food is nothing special, if not mediocre. As I ate, I wondered why a rich billionaire like Farnum would choose to eat at a popular restaurant like this. After eating, when it was time to pay, I saw a zero on the bill, along with the words: Your dish is a gift from the person who came to eat first. To continue the cordial bond, we ask that you also please give a gift to the next person. I read and re-read the bill in surprise and then looked up at Farnum with a puzzled expression. Farnum has been observing my attitude all this while. Satisfied with the surprised look on my face, he explained:

- Our meal has already been paid for by the previous user. Chicago has thousands of eateries, but this is a special one because it gives people the opportunity to share kindness and love with others. This restaurant is the idea of ​​some people who want to create change in today's hurried, greedy, selfish, and indifferent life. They promote the sending of love, kindness, and sharing to others by paying the next person to eat like a gift, creating a bond of affection from one person to another. This idea was started a few years ago but has now spread everywhere, causing economic experts to give it the name: Gift Economy (Gift Economy) or the exchange of values ​​but not buying and selling but giving unconditionally.

Farnum's explanation reminded me of something that happened not long ago. That day I was driving to New Jersey and passed a toll booth. When I stopped to pay, the toll collector said that the previous car had already paid the toll for me. Seeing that, Angie immediately said: If that's the case, we'd also like to pay for the car later. Continuing to give when you receive something good has a long tradition, there is even an idiom for this action (Pay it forward). I think this restaurant operates with the mission of spreading this spirit.

Farnum explains further:

- Karma Kitchen is a restaurant without prices, diners can pay as much as they want to dine, and that amount is used as a gift for the next person to eat. The shop operates with the spirit of service, the purpose is to give, without expecting anything. Receiving a gift from the person who ate first and then giving a gift to the person who ate later, even if no one knows anyone, is a gentle, silent joy that everyone can experience. This noble action became a movement to spread love to everyone. Its principle is to encourage acts of kindness to transform selfishness into altruism and spread love to others.

Love is like water, flowing everywhere. God's love is like a vast and endless ocean, while human love is like a small stream flowing through the earth. When people know how to love is when they return to God and when they love sincerely and without demands is when the stream begins to merge into the sea.

I smiled and applauded:

- That's great. What a meaningful form of giving. Personally, I think it is more meaningful than charity restaurants.

Farnum nodded:

- Charity restaurants for the poor are run by charity associations. Even though people who come to eat do not have to pay, they are just consumers and do not have the opportunity to spread kindness to others. Nowadays, money is the dominant factor in everything, everything requires money. People look at each other through money, compare each other through money and treat each other through money. Karma Kitchen provides an opportunity for people to be quietly kind to each other by paying the next person as a gift.

I nodded in agreement and then suddenly wondered:

- But without a price and just relying on everyone's kindness, will the shop have enough money to maintain?

Farnum laughed:

- I think a restaurant like that must lose money, right? No, the surprising thing is that the amount of money coming in is often more than the amount spent. Almost everyone who comes to eat wants to pay more to keep the restaurant operating. The shop's motto is Give people a chance to do kindness and they will spread it everywhere. Currently, there have been several dozen Karma Kitchen restaurants opened in the US, and it has also spread to India, Singapore, Malaysia, England, Japan, Poland, France and Dubai. This is a novel economic concept of generous giving without asking for anything in return. Its purpose is to awaken everyone's inherent potential for love and kindness, so that they can spread love to all in order to transform themselves as well as others. That's why I invited you here, I want you to pay attention to this movement.

While we were talking, a few waiters in the restaurant passed by the table to warmly greet Farnum. I asked:

- It seems that you come here often and are very familiar with this place?

Farnum smiled and explained:

- Karma Kitchen is a restaurant where everyone from the cook to the waiter works completely voluntarily, without pay. Some people work for a few days, some work for weeks or longer. Most of them are students, enthusiastic about the ideal of serving and spreading altruism and kindness. When I heard about this, I volunteered to wash dishes and take out the trash here for two weeks to see how they worked. That's why I know most people here.

Farnum added:

- I am a person of action. If I want to know more about something, I personally go there to examine and research it. If necessary, I am ready to start working to understand how they work. Karma Kitchen's rule is to develop kindness, creating a chain of kindness from one person to another. If businessmen like us invest in stocks, then the people who work here as well as the guests who come to eat invest in compassion and kindness.

Farnum is a billionaire who specializes in investing in start-up companies but leads a private life, never appearing in public, so not many people know about him. However, the fact that he voluntarily came to work in a popular restaurant to learn more made me very impressed. Farnum continued:

- After voluntarily signing up, we will sit around in a circle to introduce ourselves to the people working there. Everyone only knows each other's names, no one knows who I am and I don't know who they are either. This job is a service, completely voluntary, regardless of age, fame, or status, but has only one purpose: to complete the assigned work. Even if someone has a defect, it doesn't matter. In the spirit of service, everyone helps each other without criticism. Whether rich or poor, no matter how high your degree or status is, it doesn't matter. In serving, sincerity is the only factor. Therefore, when doing this, there cannot be ego involved. No one who works voluntarily is self-respecting and arrogant. If you still value yourself, then serving that person is just a means to achieve another goal.

I nodded in agreement, then asked further:

- So what did you do here? How do people work here? I'm really curious. I see that everyone seems very enthusiastic and energetic, not like they are working for nothing.

Farnum laughed:

- That's right, everyone here has a passion for goodness. Early in the morning, when everyone gathers, the restaurant operator will talk about that day's menu, instruct how to cook the dishes, and then proceed to assign tasks to everyone. When I first came here, because I was not familiar with the job, I was assigned simple tasks such as sweeping, cleaning and taking out the trash. After working for a few days, a new volunteer arrived, and I was assigned to set the table and bring dishes to the guests. After a week, because I had experience, I was assigned to help the cook. Every day, when the shop closes, everyone cleans up, arranges tables and chairs, then sits in a circle to share with each other about that day's work to gain experience. These sharing sessions are unforgettable experiences. People started telling each other about their feelings when doing these jobs. These are short stories but full of meaning. For example, when a guest is harsh or impolite, how do they maintain a gentle attitude? The principle of volunteering to work here is to develop compassion to change yourself and spread it to others. Sometimes our reactions and behaviors also help customers transform their attitudes. Their sharing is valuable and helps me understand clearly what the spirit of non-profit service is. During my two weeks here, I learned many things: Giving, speaking kindly, spreading kindness, and working together in a spirit of service. Or, in the language of Buddhism, it is almsgiving, loving speech, beneficial actions, and cooperation. Thanks to that, I better understand the gift economy or the system of exchanging things with human affection. This is in complete contrast to a market economy, where everything is exchanged only with money.

At that moment, a young man passed by and greeted Farnum enthusiastically. He introduced this young man to me:

- This is Roger, the person who has worked here the longest. Looks like six months, right?

The young man nodded and smiled:

- Yes, I work three days a week, and have done so for more than six months now.

I asked:

- What are you currently doing to be able to spend time here volunteering for so long?

Roger happily answered:

- I am a student at the University of Chicago...

Farnum immediately said:

- Hey Roger, please tell my friend why you volunteered to work here.

Roger nodded and smiled:

- I study computing. Most of my friends in school cherish the dream of starting a business to get rich. Everyone wants to become the next Bill Gates or Steve Jobs. Almost every story, every day topic of theirs is related to money and doesn't care about any other issues. Of course, money is not bad, but their obsessive desire for money disappointed me. I want to have a noble, better life. I read books about Buddhism, the thing that attracts me the most is the concept of karma (Karma), which is understood as if you do good things, good things will come to you. I don't expect anything in return other than trying to be a good person. Therefore, outside of school hours, I volunteer to work here and feel happier than ever.

After Roger left, Farnum continued our interrupted conversation:

- You see, we often invite friends to eat and drink, but no matter how close friends are, sometimes there is still an expectation of reciprocation. If I pay you today, you will pay me next time. It's not often that we think about paying money to someone we don't know without expecting anything in return. Most people would think that would be stupid. However, in this world, no one is a stranger. And everyone we are destined to meet in life has a relationship with us from before. In this world of more than seven billion people, we are estimated to only meet a few thousand people in our entire lives. Among them, I only know a few hundred people. Have you ever wondered why we meet? Why are we close to each other and not anyone else? Could it be that they all had previous contact? We come together to learn, help, and also to share and spread love.

Farnum emphasized:

- The problem is that few people really think about this. In countless relationships, most people only get close to someone when they see something beneficial for them. Sometimes friends are also objects to be taken advantage of, not necessarily true friendship. Rich and famous people often have many friends gathered to praise and flatter them. Have you seen a poor, hungry person with so many friends?

Farnum suddenly pondered:

- Since going through my near-death experience, I have thought a lot about how I can help people transform their minds to more noble, meaningful things? Nowadays, many people are accustomed to a selfish lifestyle, only caring for themselves and not thinking about anyone else. Even though they know they won't take material wealth with them when they die, they still keep as much as possible. Few people know how to give it away. I remember the stranger who accompanied my father once advised that only when we know how to forget ourselves can all good things manifest, when the ego is destroyed, the love within will shine. From then on I tried to live like that.

I looked at Farnum, my old classmate, one of Chicago's richest and most successful billionaires. Going through a near-death experience, he became a very different person. The person whose comfort and serenity always shines on his face, which has wrinkles over the years. He silently entrusted me with all his assets to do meaningful things. I think of rich people like him, although they are old, they still struggle with every short remaining day of their lives to worry about and calculate every number in their bank account.

Farnum continued:

- I once saw a poor beggar who just asked for a piece of pizza and immediately shared it with a skinny stray dog ​​wandering around looking for food nearby. Giving without expecting anything in return is even more noble than millionaires who are willing to spend large amounts of money on charity but the purpose is to have their names and contributions praised in the press. As a Catholic, I really like the question of Saint Francis of Assisi: Is there anyone who wants to serve God for free?. No merit means not expecting anything, just serving wholeheartedly.

I nodded:

- You're right. Most people who work expect some kind of result, whether it's a material reward or just a compliment.

Farnum continued:

- Perhaps you also see that most rich people tend to collect and cannot bear to give. More than half of the people with power and huge fortunes only know how to accumulate and do not know how to give alms, give or help others. For them, hearing the word alms makes them feel shy, because their nature is to hold on tightly, while giving away means loss, pain, and grief. A society with so many stingy rich people cannot be a healthy society, it rots from the inside.

Only when we forget ourselves can all good things manifest. When the ego disappears, the love within will shine.

Farnum was silent as if thinking, then continued:

- We are all people who work in the financial field so we know economic data well. In the past, most large and small companies distributed profits fairly and widely. Through financial reports, we know clearly how much they pay their employees, what benefits they have, and how they pay taxes to the government. This equitable distribution policy has created prosperity for society for a long time. However, starting in the 70s, there was a big change due to the concept of economist Milton Friedman, when he asserted that: The social responsibility of business is to utilize all its resources and participate in activities designed to increase the profits of the business. At that time, investors like us all wholeheartedly praised Milton, especially when he won the Nobel Prize in Economics for his contributions to monetarism (Monetarism), which is still considered the golden rule to this day.

I agree:

- Many leaders also applied this policy to their countries, few people expected the consequences later.

Farnum nodded:

- This concept has fueled the greed of some executives, who take advantage of this theory and apply it in a misleading way to grab all they can get. You and I both see clearly that while the salaries of workers in businesses remain stagnant, the salaries of executives have increased exponentially. This inequality still continues to this day. In the past, most business leaders started from a low position and then worked their way up. They were all professionals with many years of experience in the field of operations. Starting in the 70s, with the notion of increasing business profits, most of these executives were replaced by finance graduates from top universities such as Harvard, Chicago, Pennsylvania, Stanford... A Business Administration degree (MBA) is the key to opening the door to enter the position of CEO. These people have only one goal, which is to maximize profits to increase stock prices. They fired a large number of workers to cut costs, closed many factories, and transferred production to other countries with low wages to increase profits. They fabricate nouns like globalization, bringing jobs to less developed countries, promoting economic development in those places. In fact, the only purpose is to reduce expenses and increase revenue to make maximum profits. From then on, the company's value is no longer assessed by products or high quality but by profit levels, by how many points the stock price increases. This is a short-term but extremely harmful policy. Although it brings profits to businesses, executives and stockholders, it causes social instability, increases unemployment, shrinks the middle class, and creates inequality between rich and poor. How can a business that has no new innovations and only produces products at low cost but wants to earn high profits to overcome and progress in today's harshly competitive world?

The issue Farnum just mentioned makes me think of the mass bankruptcy of large companies in recent times. Most of the companies that had great success in the early 20th century are now in decline or have disappeared from the market. Is it just the greed of a minority of leaders that has brought about such disastrous consequences?

Farnum added:

- Since businesses around the world applied this policy, the stock market and stock prices have increased more than ever. I see many executives today being ruthless like never before. Every company is racing to lay off workers, close factories, move jobs overseas, and cut research budgets, just to achieve the goal of increasing profits, regardless of all the risks posed to the future. When stock prices rise, people investing in stocks increase, and businesses have more money, what will these directors do? They directly pay off rival companies to reduce competition. Perhaps you also know that currently the world economy has shrunk into the hands of a few dozen extremely large corporations, controlling almost everything. The influence and power of these giants can overwhelm the entire world economy in the future. I am also very concerned about the globalization policy that many national governments are currently praising. They only see short-term benefits, helping them solve unemployment without realizing the harmful consequences that can follow later. Most of the technologies transferred to countries with cheap labor are outdated, the machines are old, as a result they cause serious pollution, chemical waste dumped into rivers and seas has destroyed the environment, causing many incurable diseases that cannot be cured. Deforestation, mountain cutting, and exploitation of natural resources for export have brought many consequences in the future that no one expected. Is it all just because of greed, wanting to have a lot of money and get rich quickly?

Farnum continued:

- The 70s was also the time when information technology developed, start-ups such as Apple, Microsoft, Google all became big players in the stock market. When their stocks increased hundreds of times, very young, immature people became big bosses with assets reaching billions. Their success is the driving force that motivates the current young generation to be more ambitious and greedy. Many recent graduates, when interviewing for jobs, say their only goal is to make as much money as possible.

I agree with Farnum:

- You're right, I have met people like that. I haven't heard them say anything about my ability to contribute to the company and the country, but I've heard them say how I can make a lot of money.

Farnum sighed:

- In society, when a minority becomes extremely rich, while the majority has to do everything to survive, that society cannot progress or develop, and will eventually disintegrate. To create balance in society, we must first begin with education about human duties and responsibilities in society and on this earth, in order to change the habits of greed, selfishness and self-interest.

I'll say it now:

- This is easy to say but difficult to apply. Nowadays, money has dominated almost everything, so people's minds have been affected, more or less corrupted, making it difficult to give up greed or selfishness...

Farnum mused:

- We are all stock investors, buying and selling stocks, so we are partly responsible for this situation. Therefore, I want to use all my assets to support actions that can awaken and create a transformation of consciousness for everyone. We need to encourage noble deeds to raise humanity's consciousness to a higher level. Once the mind is imbued with noble thoughts, bad habits will obviously be eliminated.

I asked:

- So what can we do?

Farnum silently thought and then said:

- Currently, technological development has changed the foundation of the family, as a result, children are no longer as close or have a close relationship with their parents as before. The young generation has fallen into a state of disconnection and become lost and lonely, having to find comfort through technology products such as games, virtual social networks, and socializing with strangers on social networks. Young people today are gradually losing the direct connection between people and having to go through the mediation of technology. This causes them to not only lose connection with their families and previous generations but also lose connection with themselves. They are helpless, lost, lonely, and miserable in a mechanical, emotionless world. Most have lost faith in everything, including family and religion. In the past few decades, the pressure of social life has pushed many families to separation and breakup. The divorce rate is high, spouses and children become strangers to each other, sometimes even turning into hatred. Family is the foundation of society, when everyone in it is no longer connected to each other, how can society be maintained?

I ask:

- In your opinion, how can we build a stronger society?

Farnum continued:

- To build a healthy society, we need to start from the basics, from the root of the family. A tree needs to have roots that go deep into the ground to grow. Why are today's young people not as resilient as before? The problem is not entirely with them but with the family. The duty of parents is to teach their children to be filial, to become honest citizens, to love their family, to focus on the fatherland, to protect the nation, to build and do useful things for the country. When a family breaks down, when husband and wife don't get along, and arguments constantly break out, how can children follow and be obedient? Parents must be clearly aware of their responsibility to educate and orient their children and cannot assign it to anyone else. If children are taught from a young age to develop their personality in the right direction, when they grow up they can overcome challenges and not be swayed by money, status, beauty or fame. Today, some psychologists call for children to be given the freedom to develop according to their nature. I don't object to this, but freedom is not about doing whatever you want. Children who are not taught from a young age and left to develop as they please will only make them insensitive and spoiled.

I suggest:

- I still know that, but in today's situation, few families can live comfortably with one source of income. Both husband and wife have to work to make ends meet, so requiring them to spend a lot of time educating their children is a big problem.

Farnum objected:

- But it's not necessary that everyone has to spend all their time to make money. No matter how busy they are, if they want, parents can still take time to learn and sympathize with their children. When giving birth, no parent wants their child to become spoiled, but many people leave this important education to school. Schools can only teach general knowledge, but only parents can teach and orient basic human ethics. Children learn from their parents, how parents act, children learn. If we don't take the time to teach, listen, understand and sympathize with our children from an early age, how can we know what our children need when they grow up? Why do young people today tend to be independent, rebellious and disobedient to their parents? Because parents don't know anything about their children, what they think, what they do, or what problems they have. Because parents don't teach their children anything, they only learn through friends and social networking sites. Children learn that successful people are those who can make a lot of money, so they are willing to do anything just to have money, regardless of good or bad. They learn that if they want to be famous, they must follow movie stars or people who are creating influence on social networks. Therefore, they shop, dress, and speak indiscriminately like these people. Instead of reading valuable books, they only read comments and messages on social networks and chat with strangers because they can no longer talk and have intimate conversations with their parents. That is the serious disconnect in family education today in the world.

I agree and add:

- You're right, I see that today the vast majority of young people pay little attention to events in the world, compared to people of previous generations. My friend, a university professor, had to complain that most students only watch news via Facebook, Twitter, TikTok, YouTube or WeChat... They only care about what young people like them are doing on social networks. They become increasingly insensitive, no longer eager to explore to increase their knowledge and only follow material things or temporary trends. People still believe that thanks to the Internet, young people are more connected to each other, but in fact, most connections through technology applications are only superficial and inauthentic.

Farnum looked worried:

- Why are the world's moral standards so degraded? Is it because people only know how to follow the call of money and fame and don't pay attention to education? Even as schools compete with each other to enroll as many students as possible, the goal is to make a lot of money and few people care about the quality of education, good or bad. Not to mention the fact that schools race to increase tuition every year, and there are many other fees that arise, causing many families to fall into poverty, no longer having the strength to care about the quality of education. Once education has degenerated, how can we train talented people for the country? How to train noble souls or true heroes to protect the homeland? Today, many young people do not know anything about morality, human love, justice or charity, but only live after immediate pleasures, living with indulgent habits, enjoying themselves in all kinds of ways. If we do not encourage the restoration of ancient noble values ​​through action, it will be very difficult to save the current serious decline.

I answer:

- Many people have spoken out about improving the state of education as well as parenting responsibilities in this era, but so far they are still just hopeless cries.

Farnum smiled:

- For many years, every government has initiated many large-scale programs with huge budgets to do that. They hired experts with advanced degrees and graduates from top universities to do the job, but the results didn't go anywhere. Do you know why? Because most of these people, despite their ability and knowledge, only work to get paid, not from the heart.

Farnum concluded:

- In my opinion, all changes must happen from within to have an impact on the outside. Transformation only happens from experiences and actions with what we believe. That's why I don't want to do big things, but I'm also willing to support small but meaningful things. That's why I invited you to this restaurant to introduce to you the operating principle of this place, which is: Give people a chance to do kind things and they will spread this everywhere. Who knows, small things can awaken everyone's good potential, bringing transformation for the future...

After meeting with Farnum at Karma Kitchen, I returned to New York and kept thinking about our conversation. I discussed with Angie that it was time for me to spend more time doing these meaningful things. After careful discussion, both my husband and I decided to hand over the management of the company to associates we trust to focus on using funds to support programs that can bring about changes for the better. We also agreed to merge all of our assets into Farnum's treasury to support future projects.

According to Farnum's suggestion, I asked Andrew to learn and research more about the Karma Kitchen project or similar activities. Not long after, Andrew brought me a file on giftism that he had collected. He said:

- According to my research, Karma Kitchen is an independently operated restaurant chain, established in 2007, currently present in 23 countries, with more than half a million people coming to eat each year to experience kindness. The gift economy has now spread everywhere. Details and facts about the operations of these restaurants are recorded in this report.

Looking at the file containing hundreds of pages, I was quite surprised because I didn't think this project would have such a large scale and long-term operation. Partly because, I don't think Andrew would put so much effort into research outside of investment data. Andrew is a market research expert with sharp ability and careful attention to detail. For many years, he has been the employee I trust the most. Once I give Andrew something to do, he will never disappoint me. And with this sideline job, Andrew is still as dedicated as ever. I reached out to pick up the file, and as soon as I opened it, Andrew immediately said:

- Perhaps you need to know that Karma Kitchen is just a program within a larger movement called Service Space (Service Space). This is an organization initiated in the past decade, operating as an ecosystem with great influence on many young people.

I was surprised:

- Is there another movement that is bigger and more meaningful? I haven't heard of it.

Andrew confirmed:

- That's right, Service Space is an organization consisting of many young people with the same goal of contributing to building and changing society. The special thing is that all programs are carried out in a spirit of volunteerism to spread kindness and love everywhere.

I was more surprised:

- How does this organization work? Why haven't I heard anyone talk about it before?

Andrew laughed:

- The reason we don't know is because in the company's commercial investment research, this organization will never be on the radar, because it is only a non-profit organization, the construction and operation is completely done by volunteers. This organization has no employees, no office or physical headquarters, but only uses technology to encourage and call people to perform small actions to spread love and sympathy everywhere.

I was pleasantly surprised:

- How does an organization operate without employees or headquarters?

Andrew explains:

- This organization is just a website that helps people interact and operate with each other according to pre-prepared processes. All work and projects in the organization have a common goal of inspiring love and kindness through services to help people transform. Volunteers will enjoy much joy through non-profit actions. People who receive that help also continue to participate in other services so that kindness can spread everywhere. In this ecosystem, everyone is connected to each other in the spirit of service - just giving, not expecting anything in return. In this ecosystem, every action leads to connection between people, not to meet any need. From those voluntary, non-profit actions, people experience miraculous transformations from within, while establishing external relationships between people with the same ideals and aspirations. Therefore, in addition to the research data about Karma Kitchen, I also recorded additional details about the Service Space organization and their operating program in this report.

I didn't expect that what Farnum told me a few months ago about this gift economy had already been done many years ago. When I planned to contribute my part to the process of transforming human consciousness, all the foundations were almost ready. What a strange coincidence, I thought to myself. I remember Mr. Kris's saying: Once fate is enough, everything happens faster than you think.

Andrew continued:

- According to information on this organization's website, with the access address ServiveSpace.org, anyone can propose a project and use their own tools to plan according to a pre-written process. Anyone can voluntarily participate in announced programs. Most of the participants are students with the concept of Change yourself, change the world.
